title: Diplomatic mission
text: A diplomatic mission or foreign mission is a group of people from one state or an organisation present in another state to represent the sending state/organisation officially in the receiving state.

title: Diplomatic mission
text: In practice, a diplomatic mission usually denotes the resident mission, namely the embassy, which is the office of a country's diplomatic representatives in the capital city of another country, whereas consulates are diplomatic missions which are not performed in the capital of the receiving state.

title: Diplomatic mission
text: As well as being a diplomatic mission to the country in which it is situated, it may also be a non-resident permanent mission to one or more other countries.

title: Diplomatic mission
text: There are thus resident and non-resident embassies.

title: Diplomatic bag
text: A diplomatic bag, also known as a diplomatic pouch, is a container with certain legal protections used for carrying official correspondence or other items between a diplomatic mission and its home government or other diplomatic, consular, or otherwise official entities.

title: Diplomatic bag
text: The physical concept of a "diplomatic bag" is flexible and therefore can take many forms (e.g., a cardboard box, briefcase, duffel bag, large suitcase, crate or even a shipping container).

title: Diplomatic bag
text: Additionally, a diplomatic bag usually has some form of lock and/or tamper-evident seal attached to it in order to deter or detect interference by unauthorized third parties.

title: Diplomatic bag
text: The most important point is that as long as it is externally marked to show its status, the "bag" has diplomatic immunity from search or seizure, as codified in article 27 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

title: Diplomatic bag
text: It may only contain articles intended for official use.

title: Diplomatic bag
text: It is often escorted by a diplomatic courier, who is similarly immune from arrest and detention.

title: Participant observation
text: Participant observation is one type of data collection method typically used in qualitative research.

title: Participant observation
text: It is a widely used methodology in many disciplines, particularly cultural anthropology and (European) ethnology, less so in sociology, communication studies, human geography and social psychology.

title: Participant observation
text: Its aim is to gain a close and intimate familiarity with a given group of individuals (such as a religious, occupational, sub cultural group, or a particular community) and their practices through an intensive involvement with people in their cultural environment, usually over an extended period of time.

title: Participant observation
text: The method originated in the field research of social anthropologists, especially Bronisław Malinowski and his students in Britain, the students of Franz Boas in the United States, and in the later urban research of the Chicago School of sociology.

title: Muted group theory
text: Muted group theory (MGT) is developed by social anthropologists Edwin Ardener and Shirley Ardener in 1975.

title: Muted group theory
text: The theory describes the relationship between a dominant group and its subordinate group(s): As the dominant group contributes mostly to the formulation of the language system, including the norms and vocabulary, members from the subordinate group have to learn and use the dominant-made language to express themselves.

title: Muted group theory
text: However, this translation process may result in loss and distortion of information as the people from subordinate groups cannot articulate their ideas clearly.

title: Muted group theory
text: The dominant may also ignore the voice of the lower-power.

title: Muted group theory
text: All these may eventually lead to the mutedness of the subordinate group.

title: Muted group theory
text: Although this theory is initially developed to study the different situations faced by women and men, it can also be applied to any marginalized group that is muted by the inadequacies of their languages.

title: Coral Gardens and Their Magic
text: Coral Gardens and Their Magic, properly Coral Gardens and Their Magic: A Study of the Methods of Tilling the Soil and of Agricultural Rites in the Trobriand Islands, is the final book in anthropologist Bronisław Malinowski's ethnographic trilogy on the lives of the Trobriand Islanders.

title: Coral Gardens and Their Magic
text: It concentrates on the cultivation practices the Trobriand Islanders used to grow yams, taro, bananas and palms.

title: Coral Gardens and Their Magic

title: Coral Gardens and Their Magic

title: Coral Gardens and Their Magic
text: The book has been described as Malinowski's "magnum opus".

title: Gardnerville Branch Jail
text: Prior to 1910, the only county jail was in Genoa, the county seat; however, since Gardnerville was several miles from Genoa, it resorted to housing prisoners in the local judge's granary.

title: Gardnerville Branch Jail
text: As the granary was considered unfit for holding prisoners, the community petitioned the county to construct a new jail.

title: Gardnerville Branch Jail
text: However, local leaders in Minden, who wanted to move the county seat to their town, protested the move, as they suspected that Gardnerville was attempting to claim the county seat itself.

title: Gardnerville Branch Jail
text: Nonetheless, the county approved the construction of the new jail.

title: Gardnerville Branch Jail

title: Rostker v. Goldberg
text: Rostker v. Goldberg, 453 U.S. 57 (1981) , was a decision of the United States Supreme Court holding that the practice of requiring only men to register for the draft was constitutional.

title: Rostker v. Goldberg
text: After extensive hearings, floor debate and committee sessions on the matter, the United States Congress enacted the law, as it had previously been, to apply to men only.

title: Rostker v. Goldberg
text: Several attorneys, including Robert L. Goldberg, subsequently challenged the gender distinction as unconstitutional.

title: Rostker v. Goldberg
text: (The named defendant is Bernard D. Rostker, Director of the Selective Service System.)

title: Rostker v. Goldberg
text: In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court held that this gender distinction was not a violation of the equal protection component of the due process clause, and that the Act would stand as passed.

title: One Rank, One Pension
text: One Rank One Pension (OROP), or "same pension, for same rank, for same length of service, irrespective of the date of retirement", is a longstanding demand of the Indian armed forces and veterans.

title: One Rank, One Pension
text: The demand for pay-pension equity, which underlies the OROP concept, was provoked by the exparte decision by the Indira Gandhi-led Indian National Congress (INC) government, in 1973, two years after the historic victory in the 1971 Bangladesh war, and shortly after Field Marshal SHFJ Manekshaw retired, to decrease armed forces pensions by 20–40 percent, and increase civilian pensions by 20 percent, without consultation with armed forces headquarters.

title: Chief of the Defence Staff (Canada)
text: The Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS; French: "chef d'état-major de la Défense" ) is the second most senior member of the Canadian Armed Forces (after the commander-in-chief) and heads the Armed Forces Council, having primary responsibility for command, control, and administration of the forces, as well as military strategy, plans, and requirements.

title: Chief of the Defence Staff (Canada)
text: The position is held by a senior member of one of the three main branches of the Canadian Armed Forces.

title: Chief of the Defence Staff (Canada)
text: The current CDS, since 17 July 2015, is Jonathan Vance.

title: September 16 military parade
text: The 16 September military parade in honour of the anniversary of Mexican Independence is an annual tradition dating back to the late 19th century and the beginning of the professionalisation of the Mexican Armed Forces in the 20th century.

title: September 16 military parade
text: Held yearly in the Zócalo in Mexico City, this parade, the largest of the various parades held simultaneously nationwide on September 16, Mexican Independence Day, is presided by the President of Mexico in the fulfillment of his duty as the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.

title: September 16 military parade
text: It is also attended by members of the Cabinet of Mexico, the Congress of the Union, civil service employees, the Secretaries of National Defense and Navy, members of the Mexican Armed Forces and Federal Police, uniformed service veterans, the state diplomatic corps, delegations representing the religious sector, indigenous peoples, sports and the private sector, and the general public.

title: September 16 military parade
text: Seen on TV and the Internet and heard on radio, this is one of the biggest events of the year.

title: September 16 military parade
text: Taking part in this are members of the Mexican Armed Forces and the Federal Police.

title: Fernando Tapias Stahelin
text: Fernando Tapias Stahelin (born July 14, 1943 - † September 27, 2015) was a General (retired) of Colombian Armed Forces.

title: Fernando Tapias Stahelin
text: He served as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of Colombian Armed Forces for a period of four years (1998–2002) during the presidential term of president Andres Pastrana.

title: Fernando Tapias Stahelin
text: After that, he served as ambassador of Colombia in Dominican Republic from 2002 to 2004 and subsequently served as Deputy Minister of Defense for its social and business group for two years from 2009 to 2010 during the presidential term of president Alvaro Uribe.

title: Fernando Tapias Stahelin
text: He was in the Colombian Armed Forces for 41 years, achieving all the military ranks all the way up to his appointment as General Commander for the Colombian Armed Forces.

title: Conscription in the United States
text: Conscription in the United States, commonly known as the draft, has been employed by the federal government of the United States in four conflicts: the American Civil War, World War I, World War II, and the Cold War (including both the Korean and Vietnam Wars).

title: Conscription in the United States
text: The third incarnation of the draft came into being in 1940 through the Selective Training and Service Act.

title: Conscription in the United States
text: It was the country's first peacetime draft.

title: Conscription in the United States
text: From 1940 until 1973, during both peacetime and periods of conflict, men were drafted to fill vacancies in the United States Armed Forces that could not be filled through voluntary means.

title: Conscription in the United States
text: The draft was ended when the United States Armed Forces moved to an all-volunteer military force.

title: Conscription in the United States
text: However, the Selective Service System remains in place as a contingency plan; all male civilians between the ages of 18 and 25 are required to register so that a draft can be readily resumed if needed.

title: Armed Forces Covenant
text: The Military Covenant or Armed Forces Covenant is a term introduced in 2000 into British public life to refer to the mutual obligations between the nation and its Armed Forces.

title: Armed Forces Covenant
text: According to "The Guardian", "it is an informal understanding, rather than a legally enforceable deal, but it is nevertheless treated with great seriousness within the services".

title: Armed Forces Covenant
text: It was coined in , and has now entered political discourse as a way of measuring whether the government and society at large have kept to their obligations to support members of the armed forces.

title: Armed Forces Day (Poland)
text: Armed Forces Day, known also as the Feast of the Polish Armed Forces (Polish: "Święto Wojska Polskiego" ), is a national holiday celebrated annually on 15 August in Poland, commemorating the anniversary of the 1920 victory over Soviet Russia at the Battle of Warsaw during the Polish–Soviet War.

title: Armed Forces Day (Poland)
text: Armed Forces Day is held in conjunction with the Day of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, itself a separate public holiday.

title: Armed Forces Day (Poland)
text: The event is marked by military parades, equipment reviews, showcases and remembrances by all branches of the Polish Armed Forces across the country.

title: Armed Forces Day (Poland)
text: One of the most prominent events of the day is in the capital Warsaw, which hosts a large military parade through the city's center.

title: Armed Forces Day (Poland)
text: Originally celebrated during the Second Republic, the holiday was barred by authorities during the communist era beginning in 1947, only to be revived again in 1992.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::0
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: In June 1941, Roosevelt issued Executive Order 8802, which created the Fair Employment Practice Committee (FEPC).

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::1
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: It was the most important federal move in support of the rights of African-Americans between Reconstruction and the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::2
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: The President's order stated that the federal government would not hire any person based on their race, color, creed, or national origin.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::3
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: The FEPC enforced the order to ban discriminatory hiring within the federal government and in corporations that received federal contracts.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::4
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: Millions of blacks and women achieved better jobs and better pay as a result.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::5

text: The war brought the race issue to the forefront.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::6
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: The Army and Navy had been segregated since the Civil War.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::7
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: But by 1940, the African-American vote had largely shifted from Republican to Democrat, and African-American leaders like Walter Francis White of the NAACP and T. Arnold Hill of the Urban League had become recognized as part of the Roosevelt coalition.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::8
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: In June 1941, at the urging of A. Philip Randolph, the leading African-American trade unionist, Roosevelt signed an executive order establishing the Fair Employment Practice Committee and prohibiting discrimination by any government agency, including the armed forces.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::9
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: In practice the services, particularly the Navy and the Marines, found ways to evade this order — the Marine Corps remained all-white until 1942.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::10
title: Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights
text: In September 1942, at Eleanor's instigation, Roosevelt met with a delegation of African-American leaders, who demanded full integration into the forces, including the right to serve in combat roles and in the Navy, the Marine Corps and the United States Army Air Forces.

chunk_id: 5a88658955429938390d3f47::Franklin D. Roosevelt's record on civil rights::11

text: Roosevelt agreed, but then did nothing to implement his promise.

text: It was left to his successor, Harry S. Truman, to fully desegregate the armed forces.

title: Canyon Creek Food Company
text: Canyon Creek Food Company () is a food processing company based in Edmonton, Alberta that provides fresh soups and other prepared food products geared towards health conscious consumers.

title: Canyon Creek Food Company
text: The company provides its fresh food product line to grocery retailers and a broad range of food service establishments such as restaurants and institutions throughout Canada.

title: Robert's American Gourmet Food
text: Robert's American Gourmet Food was and is a snack food company located in the United States.

title: Robert's American Gourmet Food
text: Founded by businessman Robert Ehrlich in 1986, the company was best known for its snack food, Pirate's Booty, which is found in over 90% of United States supermarkets. Robert's American Gourmet targeted health-conscious shoppers with a range of snack foods.

title: Rewrapped
text: Rewrapped is a reality cooking television show hosted by Joey Fatone that premiered on April 21, 2014, on Food Network.

title: Rewrapped
text: Similar to short-form cooking reality shows, it features three chefs challenged to first recreate a classic snack food, then innovate a totally new dish using said snack food as the main ingredient.

title: Rewrapped
text: The show is a loose spinoff of the show "Unwrapped", whose host Marc Summers acts as "Head Judge" for each episode, alongside a representative of the company that produces the food of the day, and a third impartial judge involved in the food industry in some way (chef, critic, blogger, etc.).

title: PepsiCo
text: PepsiCo, Inc. is an American multinational food, snack, and beverage corporation headquartered in Purchase, New York.

title: PepsiCo
text: PepsiCo has interests in the manufacturing, marketing, and distribution of grain-based snack foods, beverages, and other products.

title: PepsiCo
text: PepsiCo was formed in 1965 with the merger of the Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay, Inc.

title: PepsiCo
text: PepsiCo has since expanded from its namesake product Pepsi to a broader range of food and beverage brands, the largest of which included an acquisition of Tropicana Products in 1998 and the Quaker Oats Company in 2001, which added the Gatorade brand to its portfolio.

title: Snackbox Food Holdings
text: Snackbox Food Holdings Co, Ltd (Korean: 스낵박스푸드홀딩스 ) is a Korean lunch snack food company.

title: Snackbox Food Holdings
text: Its headquarters is in Mokdong-Ri Gyoha-Eup Paju Gyeonggi-do, Korea, and was established in 2004.

title: Snackbox Food Holdings
text: It offers a number of snack food services to home party foods.

title: Snackbox Food Holdings
text: The company offers a range of products including fruit lunch packs, salad, yogurt and sandwiches.

title: Snackbox Food Holdings
text: Snack Box has about 25 employees as of January, 2006.

title: Snack Foods Limited
text: Snack Foods Limited is an Australian snack food company and was officially formed on 25 November 1999, and was owned by Arnott's Biscuits Holdings Pty Ltd.

title: Snack Foods Limited
text: , a subsidiary of the American Campbell Soup Company.

title: Snack Foods Limited
text: Snack Foods Limited owns one of Australia's largest salted snack food companies, Snack Brands Australia.

title: Snack Foods Limited
text: In April 2008, Campbell Arnott's sold Arnott’s Snackfoods to The Real McCoy Snackfood Co and the company is now known as Snack Brands Australia.

title: Deep-fried peanuts
text: Deep Fried Peanuts are a snack food created by deep frying peanuts in an oil.

title: Deep-fried peanuts
text: The resulting product is a snack food that can be eaten in its entirety, both shell and nut.

title: Deep-fried peanuts
text: The deep-frying process does not change the flavor or texture of the nutmeats, but changes the texture and flavor of the shells -- especially if seasonings are used -- to make them more palatable.

title: Twisties
text: Twisties are a type of cheese curl, corn-based snack food product, available mainly in Australia, and other Oceanian countries such as Papua New Guinea, New Caledonia, Vanuatu and Fiji, the Southeast Asian countries Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore and Brunei, and the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean.

title: Twisties
text: It was launched in 1950 by the General Foods Corporation.

title: Twisties
text: The brand name is owned by The Smith's Snackfood Company.

title: Twisties
text: While originally an Australian-owned company, Smith's was acquired in August 1998 by Frito-Lay, the second largest producer of snack foods in Australia, which in turn is owned by American multi-national PepsiCo.

title: Twisties
text: In Malaysia, Twisties is a product of Mondelēz International, after having been a part of Danone and later, Kraft Foods previously.

title: Twisties
text: In Thailand, the Twisties trademark is owned by Lay's, which like The Smith's Snackfood Company, is owned by PepsiCo.

title: Twisties
text: In New Zealand, Malta and Italy, Twisties are marketed under different names.

title: Handi-Snacks
text: Handi-Snacks are a snack food product line sold by Mondelez International.

title: Handi-Snacks
text: The common two-compartment Handi-Snack has a small spread compartment and a larger compartment for crackers; a red plastic spreader is included with crackers.

title: Mondelez International
text: Mondelez International, Inc., styled Mondelēz ( ), is an American multinational confectionery, food, and beverage company based in Illinois which employs about 107,000 people around the world.

title: Mondelez International
text: It consists of the global snack and food brands of the former Kraft Foods Inc after the October 2012 spin-off of its North American grocery operations.

title: Mondelez International
text: The Mondelez name, adopted in 2012, was suggested by Kraft Foods employees and is derived from the words "mundus" (Latin for “world”) and "delez" (a proxy for the word "delicious").

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Sheila Cavanagh is an associate professor of sociology and former chair of the Sexuality Studies Program at York University.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Cavanagh is currently chair of the Canadian Sexuality Studies Association and co-editor (along with Malena Gustavson) of the "Somatechnics" journal.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Her research is in the area of gender and sexuality with a concentration on queer, cultural, and psychoanalytic theories.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Cavanagh is editing a special issue on transgender and psychoanalysis in "Transgender Studies Quarterly" and completing her third book monograph titled "Transgender and the Other Sexual Difference: Bracha L. Ettinger and Jacques Lacan".

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: She co-edited a collection with Angela Failler and Rachel A. J. Hurst titled "Skin, Culture and Psychoanalysis" (2013) published by Palgrave Macmillan.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Her first sole-authored book titled "Sexing the Teacher: School Sex Scandals and Queer Pedagogies" (2007) was given honorable mention by the Canadian Women’s Studies Association.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Her second sole-authored book titled "Queering Bathrooms: Gender, Sexuality, and the Hygienic Imagination" (2010) is a GLBT Indie Book Award finalist and recipient of the CWSA/ACEF Outstanding Scholarship Prize Honourable Mention (2012).

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Her performed ethnography titled Queer Bathroom Monologues (QBM) premiered at the Toronto Fringe Festival (2011) and was given the Audience Pick Award.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: The play was professionally staged at Buddies in Bad Times Theatre, Toronto, in June 2014 for WorldPride and has toured at conferences, colleges and universities in Canada and the United States.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: She has published in a wide range of international journals and given keynotes addresses at conferences in Sweden, Turkey and Canada.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: Cavanagh teaches an undergraduate course titled Sociology of Gender and a range of graduate courses in sexuality studies, feminist theory and queer theory.

title: Sheila Cavanagh
text: She is also interviewed in Rohan Spong's documentaries "T is for Teacher" (2009) and "Queer Science" (2008).

title: Gregory B. Craig
text: Gregory Bestor "Greg" Craig (born March 4, 1945) is an American lawyer and former White House Counsel under President Barack Obama from 2009 to 2010.

title: Gregory B. Craig
text: A former attorney at the Washington, D.C. law firm of Williams & Connolly, Craig has represented numerous high-profile clients.

title: Gregory B. Craig
text: Prior to becoming White House Counsel, Craig served as assistant to the President and special counsel in the White House of President Bill Clinton, where he directed the team defending Clinton against impeachment.

title: Gregory B. Craig
text: Craig also served as a senior advisor to Senator Edward Kennedy and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

title: The White House Doctor
text: The White House Doctor: My Patients Were Presidents – A Memoir is a book authored by Connie Mariano, the first military woman in the history of the United States to be appointed as Physician to the President, the first female director of the medical unit of the White House, and the first Filipino-American to become a rear admiral in the US Navy.

title: The White House Doctor
text: With a foreword from Bill Clinton, the autobiographical book takes a look at the personal lives of three American Presidents (George H.W. Bush, Bill Clinton, and George W. Bush) and three American First Ladies (Barbara Bush, Hillary Clinton, and Laura Bush) she had taken care of while working as a White House physician.

title: The White House Doctor
text: It was described as a "fascinating look into what goes on behind closed doors at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue".

title: Once Upon a Secret
text: Once Upon a Secret: My Affair with President John F. Kennedy and Its Aftermath is a book by the former White House intern Mimi Alford in February 2012.

title: Once Upon a Secret
text: It contains the autobiographical account of the woman who had an affair with U.S. President John F. Kennedy towards the end of his life (from June 1962 to July 1963).

title: Once Upon a Secret
text: Despite its consuming influence over her life at the time, Alford managed to keep her involvement in the affair secret for nearly 50 years, until basic details were published in the 2003 Kennedy biography "" by Robert Dallek.

title: Their Lives
text: Their Lives: The Women Targeted by the Clinton Machine is a book by Candice E. Jackson.

title: Their Lives
text: Published by conservative publisher World Ahead Publishing on May 31, 2005, it recounts the stories of seven women who crossed paths with Bill Clinton: Monica Lewinsky, Paula Jones, Gennifer Flowers, Kathleen Willey, Elizabeth Gracen, Juanita Broaddrick, and Sally Perdue.

title: Eric Schultz
text: Eric Schultz is a senior advisor to former President Barack Obama and is the founder of Schultz Group.

title: Eric Schultz
text: Schultz is a former White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary and special assistant to President Obama.

title: Eric Schultz
text: Recognized by "Politico" as the strategist “White House officials turn to in a crisis to handle communications,” Schultz was originally hired at the White House in 2011 to respond to Congressional oversight investigations.

title: Eric Schultz
text: After White House Deputy Press Secretary Josh Earnest replaced Jay Carney to become White House Press Secretary, Schultz was appointed White House Deputy Press Secretary.

title: Eric Schultz
text: In this role, Schultz often diffuses "tensions with humor.

title: Eric Schultz
text: But he can be relentless in pushing his message in both public and private conversations.”

title: Eric Schultz
text: Former White House Communications Director Jen Psaki compared Schultz to fictional crisis manager Olivia Pope, "he's the person you want next to you in a foxhole when there's a crisis."

title: Eric Schultz
text: At the end of President Obama's second term, former White House Senior Advisor Valerie Jarrett said of Schultz, “We’ve all grown to rely on his wise counsel" and that the President "trusts his sound judgement."

title: William H. Ginsburg
text: William H. Ginsburg (March 25, 1943 – April 1, 2013) was an American lawyer, best known for representing former White House intern Monica Lewinsky in her controversy regarding sexual activities with President Bill Clinton in 1998.

title: Mark D. Fabiani
text: Mark D. Fabiani (born 1957) is an American political strategist, crisis management expert, former Deputy Mayor of Los Angeles and chief of staff to Mayor Tom Bradley, and former White House lawyer and spokesman.

title: Mark D. Fabiani
text: He is recognized for his work as special counsel to President Bill Clinton and legal spokesperson for the Clinton White House from 1994 through 1996, as well as for his work as head of communications for the Gore presidential campaign in 2000.

title: Mark D. Fabiani
text: He also served in senior positions at the Department of Housing and Urban Development and at the Department of Justice.

title: Monica Lewinsky
text: Monica Samille Lewinsky (born July 23, 1973) is an American activist, television personality, fashion designer, and former White House intern.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: The Lewinsky scandal was an American political sex scandal that involved 49-year-old President Bill Clinton and 22-year-old White House intern Monica Lewinsky.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: The sexual relationship took place between 1995 and 1996 and came to light in 1998.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: Clinton ended a televised speech with the statement that he did not have sexual relations with Lewinsky.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: Further investigation led to charges of perjury and to the impeachment of President Clinton in 1998 by the U.S. House of Representatives.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: He was subsequently acquitted on all impeachment charges of perjury and obstruction of justice in a 21-day Senate trial.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: Clinton was held in civil contempt of court by Judge Susan Webber Wright for giving misleading testimony in the Paula Jones case regarding Lewinsky and was also fined $90,000 by Wright.

title: Lewinsky scandal
text: His license to practice law was suspended in Arkansas for five years; shortly thereafter, he was disbarred from presenting cases in front of the United States Supreme Court.

title: Paul Manafort
text: Paul John Manafort Jr. (born April 1, 1949) is an American lawyer, lobbyist and political consultant.

title: Paul Manafort
text: He joined Donald Trump's presidential campaign team in March 2016 and served as campaign manager from June to August 2016.

title: Paul Manafort
text: He was previously an adviser to the U.S. presidential campaigns of Republicans Gerald Ford, Ronald Reagan, George H. W. Bush, and Bob Dole.

title: Paul Manafort
text: In 1980 Manafort co-founded the Washington, D.C.-based lobbying firm Black, Manafort & Stone, along with principals Charles R. Black Jr., and Roger J. Stone.

title: Paul Manafort
text: In 1984 it was renamed Black, Manafort, Stone and Kelly (BMSK) & associates, after Peter G. Kelly was recruited.

title: Donald Trump (Last Week Tonight)
text: "Donald Trump" is a segment of the HBO news satire television series "Last Week Tonight with John Oliver" devoted to Donald Trump, who later became the President of the United States.

title: Donald Trump (Last Week Tonight)
text: It first aired on February 28, 2016, as part of the third episode of "Last Week Tonight"'s third season, when Trump was the frontrunner for the Republican Party nomination for the presidency.

title: Donald Trump (Last Week Tonight)
text: During the 22-minute segment, comedian John Oliver discusses Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and his career in business, outlining his campaign rhetoric, varying political positions and failed business ventures.

title: Donald Trump (Last Week Tonight)
text: He also says the Trump family name was changed at one point from the ancestral name "Drumpf".

title: Brad Parscale
text: Brad Parscale (born January 3, 1976) is an American digital media and political strategist.

title: Brad Parscale
text: He served as the digital media director for Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign.

title: Brad Parscale
text: Parscale began working for the Trump Organization in 2011, developing and designing websites, and creating and managing digital media strategies.

title: Brad Parscale
text: In early 2015, Trump hired Parscale and his firm, Giles-Parscale, to create a website for his exploratory campaign.

title: Brad Parscale
text: When Trump declared himself a Republican candidate in 2015, one of the first people he called was Parscale, asking him to update his exploratory campaign site into a "full-fledged presidential campaign website."

title: Brad Parscale
text: Throughout the Republican primary, Parscale was responsible for the Donald J. Trump for President website, as well as for digital media strategy and online fundraising campaigns.

title: Brad Parscale
text: In June 2016, Parscale was officially named digital media director for the Donald J. Trump for President campaign, overseeing all aspects of digital media and online fundraising, as well as traditional media strategy, like radio and television placements.

title: Brad Parscale
text: In January 2017, Parscale, along with another senior Trump aide, Nick Ayers, formally launched America First Policies, a non-profit organization that promotes President Trump's agenda and White House initiatives.

title: Donald Trump in music
text: Donald Trump in music refers to songs, albums and bands that refer to Donald Trump and his various brands, including Trump Tower, his TV show, his hotel chain, and his casinos.

title: Donald Trump in music
text: Though recent songs refer to Trump's campaign and subsequent election as president of the United States, more than 200 songs refer to Trump prior to his successful presidential campaign between 1989 and 2013.

title: Donald Trump in music
text: With his victory in the 2016 presidential election, Trump's prominence in hip-hop music has been liked to that of Ronald Reagan's in hardcore punk during the 1980s.

title: Trump campaign–Russian meeting
text: On June 9, 2016, a meeting was held in Trump Tower in New York City between three senior members of the presidential campaign of Donald TrumpDonald Trump Jr., Jared Kushner, and Paul Manafortand at least five other people, including Russian lawyer Natalia Veselnitskaya.

title: Trump campaign–Russian meeting
text: The meeting was arranged by publicist and long-time Trump acquantiance, Rob Goldstone on behalf of his client, singer-songwriter Emin Agalarov.

title: Trump campaign–Russian meeting
text: It was disclosed to U.S. government officials when Kushner filed a revised version of his security clearance form.

title: Protests against Donald Trump
text: Protests against Donald Trump, or anti-Trump protests, have occurred both in the United States and elsewhere since Donald Trump's entry into the 2016 presidential campaign.

title: Protests against Donald Trump
text: Protests have expressed opposition to Trump's campaign rhetoric, his electoral win, his inauguration and various presidential actions.

title: Protests against Donald Trump
text: Some protests have taken the form of walk-outs, business closures, petitions and, especially since Trump's inauguration, rallies, demonstrations or marches.

title: Protests against Donald Trump
text: While most protests have been peaceful, some protesters have destroyed property, and attacked Trump supporters.

title: Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2000
text: Donald Trump's presidential campaign of 2000 for the nomination of the Reform Party began when real estate magnate Donald Trump of New York announced the creation of a presidential exploratory committee on the October 7, 1999 edition of "Larry King Live".

title: Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2000
text: Though Trump had never held elected office, he was well known for his frequent comments on public affairs and business exploits as head of The Trump Organization.

title: Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2000
text: He had previously considered a presidential run in 1988 as a Republican, but chose not to run.

title: Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2000
text: For 2000, Minnesota Governor Jesse Ventura persuaded Trump to seek the presidential nomination of the Reform Party, which was fracturing despite achieving ballot access and qualifying for matching funds as a result of the 1996 presidential campaign of businessman Ross Perot.

title: Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2000
text: Trump's entrance into the Reform Party race coincided with that of paleoconservative commentator Pat Buchanan, whom Trump attacked throughout the campaign as a "Hitler-lover."

title: Tony Fabrizio
text: Anthony Fabrizio (born 1960) is an American Republican pollster and strategist.

title: Tony Fabrizio
text: He is the principal in Fabrizio, Lee & Associates, and was the pollster for Donald Trump's fall 2016 Presidential campaign, former Senator Bob Dole's 1996 Presidential campaign, U.S. Senator Rand Paul's U.S. Senate and 2016 Presidential campaign, and former Governor Rick Perry's 2012 Presidential campaign, among others.

title: Tony Fabrizio
text: He also served as a pollster for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce in the 2014 midterm elections.

title: David Urban

title: Energy shot
text: Energy shots are a specialized kind of energy drink that contain a dose of the stimulant caffeine in a small amount of liquid.

title: Energy shot
text: Whereas most energy drinks are sold in cans or bottles, energy shots are usually sold in 50ml bottles.

title: CytoSport

text: Zurracapote (sometimes abbreviated as zurra) is a popular Spanish alcoholic mixed drink, similar to sangría.

title: Zurracapote

title: Chagrin Documentary Film Festival
text: That year, the festival had an attendance of 1,800.

title: Chagrin Documentary Film Festival

title: British Journal
text: The British Journal was an English newspaper published from 22 September 1722 until 13 January 1728.

title: British Journal

title: London Review of Books

title: Doc NYC

title: British Journal of Social Psychology
text: The British Journal of Social Psychology is a peer-reviewed academic journal published by Wiley-Blackwell on behalf of the British Psychological Society.

title: British Journal of Social Psychology
text: It publishes original papers on subjects like social cognition, attitudes, group processes, social influence, intergroup relations, self and identity, nonverbal communication, and social psychological aspects of affect and emotion, and of language and discourse.

title: British Journal of Social Psychology

title: British Journal of Social Psychology
text: According to the "Journal Citation Reports", the journal has a 2010 impact factor of 2.056.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: Thomas Gordon (c. 1691–1750) was a Scottish writer and Commonwealthman.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: Along with John Trenchard, he published "The Independent Whig", which was a weekly periodical.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: From 1720 to 1723, Trenchard and Gordon wrote a series of 144 essays entitled "Cato's Letters", condemning corruption and lack of morality within the British political system and warning against tyranny.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: The essays were published as "Essays on Liberty, Civil and Religious", at first in the "London Journal" and then in the "British Journal".

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: These essays became a cornerstone of the Commonwealth man tradition and were influential in shaping the ideas of the Country Party.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: His ideas played an important role in shaping republicanism in Britain and especially in the American colonies leading up to the American revolution.

title: Thomas Gordon (writer)
text: Zuckert argues, "The writers who, more than any others, put together the new synthesis that is the new republicanism were John Trenchard and Thomas Gordon, writing in the early eighteenth century as "Cato."

title: New Haven Documentary Film Festival
text: New Haven Documentary Film Festival (also known as NHdocs) is an annual documentary film festival held in New Haven, Connecticut, over a weekend in the month of June.

title: New Haven Documentary Film Festival
text: Screenings take place at Yale University’s Whitney Humanities Center Auditorium and the New Haven Free Public Library.

title: New Haven Documentary Film Festival

title: New Haven Documentary Film Festival
text: NHdocs was launched in 2014 when the film festival’s co-founders Charles Musser, Gorman Bechard, Jacob Bricca, and Lisa Molomot came together at the Big Sky Documentary Film Festival and decided to create a documentary film festival in New Haven that would “build a sense of community among documentary filmmakers from the greater New Haven area.”

title: New Haven Documentary Film Festival

title: Scott's Run Nature Preserve

title: Terren Peizer
text: Terren Scott Peizer dubbed the "Zelig of Wall Street" is currently the Chairman of his personal Los Angeles-based investment company, Acuitas Group Holdings (AGH), which in turn owns 100% of Crede Capital Group (CCG) which invests in public companies, and provides growth capital to small and medium-sized enterprises.

title: AES+F
text: AES+F is an artist collective of four Russian artists: Tatiana Arzamasova (1955), Lev Evzovich (1958), Evgeny Svyatsky (1957), and Vladimir Fridkes (1956).

title: AES+F
text: It was first formed as AES Group in 1987 by Arzamasova, Evzovich, and Svyatsky, becoming AES+F when Fridkes joined in 1995.

title: AES+F
text: The collective works in photography, video, installation, and animation, as well as more traditional media, such as painting, drawing, and sculpture.

title: AES+F
text: AES+F's early work included performance, installation, painting, and illustration.

title: AES+F
text: Well known for their monumental video-art installations that Gareth Harris describes as "monumental painting set in motion", AES+F create grand visual narratives that explore contemporary global values, vices and conflicts.

title: Lev Kuleshov
text: Lev Vladimirovich Kuleshov (Russian: Лев Влади́мирович Кулешо́в ; 13 January [O.S. 1 January] 1899 – 29 March 1970) was a Russian and Soviet filmmaker and film theorist, one of the founders of the world's first film school, the Moscow Film School.

title: Lev Kuleshov
text: He was given the title People's Artist of the RSFSR in 1969.

title: Lev Kuleshov
text: He was intimately involved in development of the style of film making known as Soviet montage, especially it's psychological underpinning, including the use of editing and the cut to emotionally influence the audience, a principle known as the Kuleshov effect.

title: Lev Kuleshov
text: He also developed the theory of creative geography, which is the use of the action around a cut to connect otherwise disparate settings into a cohesive narrative.

title: Pamela Gilbert
text: Pamela B. Gilbert (born October 3, 1958) is an American lawyer and has been a partner of the law firm Cuneo Gilbert & LaDuca, LLP since 2003, where she heads the firm's lobbying practice.

title: Pamela Gilbert
text: Gilbert is a noted consumer rights advocate who has testified before Congress over fifty times and made dozens of appearances in the national print and electronic media.

title: Lev Yilmaz
text: Levni Yilmaz (born 1973) is a San Francisco based independent film maker, artist and publisher, best known for his “Tales of Mere Existence” animated comic series.

title: Pamela B. Green
text: Pamela B. Green is an American film producer and director known for her work in feature film titles and motion graphics.

title: Pamela B. Green
text: She is the director and producer of the documentary "Be Natural: The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blache".

title: Pamela B. Davis
text: Pamela B. Davis, MD, PhD is a pediatric pulmonologist specializing in cystic fibrosis research.

title: Pamela B. Davis
text: She has been Dean of the School of Medicine at Case Western Reserve University since 2007.

title: Pamela B. Davis
text: She was elected to the Institute of Medicine in 2014.

title: Visa policy of Hong Kong
text: The visa policy of Hong Kong deals with the requirements in which a foreign national wishing to enter the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region must meet to obtain an entry permit or visa, which depending on the traveller's nationality, may be required to travel to, enter, and remain in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

title: Visa policy of Hong Kong
text: Visitors from over 145 countries are permitted visa-free entry for periods ranging from 7 to 180 days, to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for tourism or certain business-related activities.

title: Visa policy of Hong Kong
text: All visitors must hold a passport valid for more than 1 month.

title: Rabat
text: Rabat (Berber: , Arabic: الرِّبَاط‎ ‎ , Moroccan Arabic: رّباط‎ ‎ ) is the capital city of Morocco and its second largest city with an urban population of approximately 580,000 (2014) and a metropolitan population of over 1.2 million.

title: Rabat
text: It is also the capital city of the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra administrative region.

title: Sinuiju Special Administrative Region
text: Sinŭiju Special Administrative Region is a special administrative region (SAR) of North Korea proclaimed in 2002 (but has not been put into "de facto" operation as of 2014), on the border with China.

title: Sinuiju Special Administrative Region
text: It was established in September 2002 in an area including parts of Sinŭiju and the surrounding area, in an attempt to introduce market economics, and is directly governed as in the case of "Directly Governed Cities".

title: Sinuiju Special Administrative Region
text: The special administrative region was modelled after China's Special Administrative Regions (SARs), Hong Kong and Macau, and, like them, has a "Basic Law" (기본법; Kibonpŏp).

title: Caraga
text: Caraga, officially known as the Caraga Administrative Region or simply Caraga Region and designated as Region XIII, is an administrative region in the Philippines occupying the northeastern section of the island of Mindanao.

title: Caraga
text: The Caraga Region was created through "Republic Act No. 7901" on February 23, 1995.

title: Caraga
text: The region comprises five provinces: Agusan del Norte, Agusan del Sur, Surigao del Norte, Surigao del Sur and Dinagat Islands; six cities: Bayugan, Bislig, Butuan, Cabadbaran, Surigao and Tandag; 67 municipalities and 1,311 barangays. Butuan is the regional administrative center.

title: 2014 NPCSC Decision on Hong Kong
text: The Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Issues Relating to the Selection of the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region by Universal Suffrage and on the Method for Forming the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in the Year 2016 (), commonly known as 31 August Decision (), is a decision made by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (NPCSC), the national legislative body of the People's Republic of China (PRC) on 31 August 2014 which set limits for the 2017 Chief Executive election and 2016 Legislative Council election in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR).

title: Ilocos Region
text: The Ilocos Region (Ilocano: "Rehion/Deppaar ti Ilocos" ; Pangasinan: "Sagor na Baybay na Luzon" ; Filipino: "Rehiyon ng Ilocos" ) is an administrative region of the Philippines, designated as Region I, occupying the northwestern section of Luzon.

title: Ilocos Region
text: It is bordered by the Cordillera Administrative Region to the east, the Cagayan Valley to the northeast and southeast, and the Central Luzon to the south.

title: Ilocos Region
text: To the west lies the South China Sea.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: The Wolong Special Administrative Region () is an area in Sichuan, China.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: It is located in the southwest of Wenchuan County, Ngawa Tibetan and Qiang Autonomous Prefecture of Sichuan.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: It was formerly known as Wolong Special Administrative Region of Wenchuan County, Sichuan Province and was founded in March 1983 with approval of the State Council.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: It was given its current name and placed under Sichuan provincial government with administrative supervision by the provincial department of forestry.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: Its area supersedes Sichuan Wolong National Nature Reserve and its administrative office is the same as the Administrative Bureau of the State Forestry Administration for the reserve.

title: Wolong Special Administrative Region
text: It currently has a population of 5343.

title: Moroccan Ambassador to China
text: The Moroccan ambassador in Beijing is the official representative of the Government in Rabat to the Government of the People's Republic of China.

title: Liaison Office (Hong Kong)
text: The Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (; abbr.

title: Liaison Office (Hong Kong)
text: LOCPG or 中聯辦) is an organ of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China (PRC) in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR).

title: Liaison Office (Hong Kong)
text: It replaced the New China News Agency (NCNA) as the representative of the PRC government in Hong Kong in 2000.

title: Hong Kong Basic Law
text: The Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China is the constitutional document of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

title: Hong Kong Basic Law
text: Being a national law of the People's Republic of China, the Basic Law was adopted on 4 April 1990 by the Seventh National People's Congress and signed by President Yang Shangkun.

title: Fuding Railway Station
text: Fuding Railway Station () is a railway station located in Fuding City, Ningde, Fujian Province, China, on the Wenzhou-Fuzhou Railway operated by the Nanchang Railway Bureau, China Railway Corporation.

title: Yingkou
text: Yingkou () is a prefecture-level city of Liaoning province, People's Republic of China.

title: Yingkou
text: It is a port city of the Bohai Sea, and is the location of the mouth of the Liao River.

title: Fuding
text: () is a county-level city in northeastern Ningde prefecture level city, on Fujian's border with Zhejiang province.

title: Roman Catholic Diocese of Yingkou
text: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Yingkou/Yingkow (Latin: "Imcheuven(sis)" , ) is a diocese located in the city of Yingkou in the Ecclesiastical province of Shenyang 瀋陽 in China.

title: Yingkou Lanqi Airport
text: Yingkou Lanqi Airport (IATA: YKH, ICAO: ZYYK) is an airport serving the city of Yingkou in Liaoning province of Northeast China.

title: Yingkou Lanqi Airport
text: It is located in Lanqi Village in Xishi District of Yingkou, about 17 km from the city center by road.

title: Yingkou Lanqi Airport
text: The airport opened on 3 February 2016, when the inaugural China Eastern Airlines flight landed from Shanghai Pudong International Airport.

title: Yingkou Lanqi Airport
text: The total investment for the project was estimated at CNY 8.94 billion.

title: Tongcheng Subdistrict, Fuding
text: Tongcheng () is a subdistrict of the city of Fuding, Fujian, People's Republic of China.

title: Xiapu County
text: Xiapu (; Foochow Romanized: Hà-puō) is a county in the municipal region of Ningde, Fujian, People's Republic of China, located along a stretch of East China Sea coast, with many harbours and islands.

title: Xiapu County
text: It is bordered by Fuding City and Zherong County to the north, Fu'an City and Ningde's urban area to the west, and—in Fuzhou City—Luoyuan County to the south.

title: Taimushan Railway Station
text: Mount Taimu Railway Station () is a railway station located in Fuding City, Ningde, Fujian Province, China, on the Wenzhou-Fuzhou Railway operated by the Nanchang Railway Bureau, China Railway Corporation.

title: Yingkou East Railway Station
text: Yingkou East Railway Station (IATA: YDD) is a railway station of Beijing–Harbin High-Speed Railway, in particular of both the Panjin–Yingkou and Harbin–Dalian sub-sections.

title: Yingkou East Railway Station
text: It is located in Dashiqiao, in the Yingkou prefecture level city, in the Liaoning province of China.

title: Bayuquan Railway Station
text: Bayuquan Railway Station (IATA: JYQ) is a railway station of the Harbin–Dalian section of the Beijing–Harbin High-Speed Railway.

title: Bayuquan Railway Station
text: It is located in Bayuquan, in the Yingkou prefecture level city, in the Liaoning province of China.

title: Mascogos
text: The Mascogos (also known as "negros mascagos") are an afrodescendant group in Coahuila, Mexico.

title: Mascogos
text: Centered on the town of El Nacimiento in Múzquiz Municipality, the group are descendants of Black Seminoles escaping the threat of slavery in the United States.

title: Dhoolpet
text: Dhoolpet is one of the old suburbs in Hyderabad, India.

title: Dhoolpet
text: It is part of the old city of Hyderabad.

title: Dhoolpet
text: This place is inhabited by people who migrated from Uttar Pradesh during the Nizam rule.

title: Dhoolpet
text: The Nizam helped these people settle in this area.

title: Dhoolpet
text: The area is notorious for bootlegging and has witnessed attacks on policemen or excise department officials during raids.

title: Seminole music
text: Seminole music is the music of the Seminole people, an indigenous people of the Americas who formed in Florida in the 18th century.

title: Seminole music
text: Today most live in Oklahoma, but a minority continue in Florida.

title: Seminole music
text: They have three federally recognized tribes, and some people belong to bands outside those groups.

title: Seminole music
text: Their traditional music includes extensive use of rattles, hand drums, water drums, and flutes.

title: Seminole
text: The Seminole are a Native American people originally from Florida.

title: Seminole
text: Today, they principally live in Oklahoma with a minority in Florida, and comprise three federally recognized tribes: the Seminole Tribe of Oklahoma, the Seminole Tribe of Florida, and Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida, as well as independent groups.

title: Seminole
text: The Seminole nation emerged in a process of ethnogenesis from various Native American groups who settled in Florida in the 18th century, most significantly northern Muscogee (Creeks) from what is now Georgia and Alabama.

title: Seminole
text: The word "Seminole" is derived from the Creek word "simanó-li", which may be itself be derived from the Spanish word "cimarrón", menaning "runaway" or "wild one".

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: The history of draining and development of the Everglades dates back to the 19th century.

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: During the Second Seminole War beginning in 1836, the United States military's mission was to seek out Seminole people in the Everglades and capture or kill them.

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: Those missions gave the military the opportunity to map land that seemed to frustrate and confound them at every turn.

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: A national push for expansion and progress toward the latter part of the 19th century stimulated interest in draining the Everglades for agricultural use.

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: According to historians, "From the middle of the nineteenth century to the middle of the twentieth century, the United States went through a period in which wetland removal was not questioned.

title: Draining and development of the Everglades
text: Indeed, it was considered the proper thing to do."

title: Muscogee language
text: The Muscogee language (Mvskoke in Muscogee), also known as Creek, Seminole, Maskókî or Muskogee, is a Muskogean language spoken by Muscogee (Creek) and Seminole people, primarily in the U.S. states of Oklahoma and Florida.

title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
text: Seminole County is a county located in the U.S. state of Oklahoma.

title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
text: As of the 2010 census, the population was 25,482.

title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
text: Its county seat is Wewoka.

title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
text: Before Oklahoma's admission as a state, the county was the entire small portion of Indian Territory allocated to the Seminole people, who were removed from Florida in the 1820s.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: The Battle of Jupiter Inlet occurred on January 15, 1838, between the Seminole Indians - Seminole Negro and the United States Navy.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: This was the first of a series of battles led by the US Navy in the area, also referred to as the First Battle of Loxahatchee.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: The battle started when Lt. Levin Powell led an expedition of 200 soldiers, sailors and marines, down the east coast of Florida.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: The Navy spotted a trail alongside the Jupiter Inlet, and seventy-five men were landed to find the Seminole camp nearby.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: The camp was led by Sam Jones, Ar-pi-uck-i, the spiritual medicine and war chief of the Miccosukee and Seminole people during the war.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: The officers that advanced on the camp were outnumbered and ambushed.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: After a long fight, the US retreated with five men killed in action and about twenty others wounded.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: Ltn.

title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
text: Powell was one of those killed in battle.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is a federally recognized Native American tribe based in the U.S. state of Oklahoma.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: It is the largest of the three federally recognized Seminole governments, which include the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: Its members are descendants of the 3,000 Seminoles who were forcibly removed from Florida to Indian Territory, along with 800 Black Seminoles, after the Second Seminole War.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is headquartered in Wewoka within Seminole County, Oklahoma.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: Of 18,800 enrolled tribal members, 13,533 live within the state of Oklahoma.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: The tribe began to revive its government in 1936 under the Indian Reorganization Act.

title: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
text: While its reservation was originally larger, today the tribal jurisdictional area covers Seminole County, Oklahoma, within which it has a variety of properties.

title: Black Seminoles
text: The Black Seminoles are black Indians associated with the Seminole people in Florida and Oklahoma.

title: Black Seminoles
text: They are the descendants of free blacks and of escaped slaves (called maroons) who allied with Seminole groups in Spanish Florida.

title: Black Seminoles
text: Historically, the Black Seminoles lived mostly in distinct bands near the Native American Seminole.

title: Black Seminoles
text: Some were held as slaves of particular Seminole leaders; but they had more freedom than did slaves held by whites in the South and by other Native American tribes, including the right to bear arms.

title: Karen Clark Sheard
text: Karen Clark-Sheard (born Karen Valencia Clark; November 15, 1960) also known as "The Maestris Of Gospel" is an American gospel four-time Grammy Award-winning singer, musician, and songwriter.

title: Karen Clark Sheard
text: The youngest daughter of pioneering gospel choral director Mattie Moss Clark, Sheard began her career as a member of the legendary Grammy Award-winning female gospel group The Clark Sisters.

title: Karen Clark Sheard
text: She is the mother of contemporary gospel singer and actress Kierra "Kiki" Sheard.

title: David Huntsinger
text: David Huntsinger is a pianist, composer, songwriter, and arranger who moved from his native California to Nashville, TN, in 1976 and played for the Rambos.

title: David Huntsinger
text: He co-wrote the song, "Holy Spirit, Thou Art Welcome", with Dottie Rambo, as well as the children’s musical, "Down By The Creek Bank".

title: David Huntsinger
text: In 1979 he left the Rambos to pursue a career as a studio pianist.

title: David Huntsinger
text: He wrote and arranged music for the 1989 Grammy-winning album "A Child’s Gift of Lullabyes", and arranged for and co-produced Andy Griffith’s 1996 Grammy-winning album, "I Love To Tell The Story: 25 Timeless Hymns".

title: David Huntsinger
text: He has worked with many artists, such as Sandi Patti, Steve Green, Kathy Troccoli, Michael Crawford, Glen Campbell, Carman, Larnelle Harris, Johnny Cash and Dolly Parton.

title: David Huntsinger
text: He toured with Vince Gill for a Christmas tour in 1999, and in 2001 for the Amy Grant/Vince Gill Christmas tour.

title: David Huntsinger
text: He has also written a number of children’s musicals, as well as produced many albums of his own original works and arrangements.

title: David Huntsinger
text: He played the piano for "An Unfinished Life", and contributed to two songs heard in "The Great Debaters".

title: David Huntsinger
text: He arranged for and played piano in the 1997 Christmas album "Piano Winterlude" (Unison).

title: David Huntsinger
text: He has done several projects for Discovery House Music.

title: David Huntsinger
text: In 2010 he composed a number of pieces for a special 25th Anniversary concert for the international television network 3ABN called "Pillars of Our Faith".

title: Just as I Am (Yolanda Adams album)
text: Just as I Am is the debut album by gospel singer Yolanda Adams, released on September 22, 1987 on the Sound of Gospel label and produced by Thomas Whitfield, who also worked with singer Vanessa Bell Armstrong on early 1980s gospel releases.

title: Just as I Am (Yolanda Adams album)
text: Though original pressings of the vinyl and cassette release are difficult to find, the album has since been re-released on CD along with another catalog album from Sound of Gospel by Wanda Nero Butler entitled "New Born Soul".

title: Andraé Crouch
text: Andraé Edward Crouch (July 1, 1942 – January 8, 2015) was an American gospel singer, songwriter, arranger, record producer and pastor.

title: Andraé Crouch
text: Referred to as "the father of modern gospel music" by contemporary Christian and gospel music professionals, Crouch was known for his compositions "The Blood Will Never Lose Its Power", "My Tribute (To God Be the Glory)" and "Soon and Very Soon".

title: Andraé Crouch
text: In secular music, he was known for his collaborative work during the 1980s and 1990s with Stevie Wonder, Elton John and Quincy Jones as well as conducting choirs that sang on the Michael Jackson hit "Man in the Mirror" and Madonna's "Like a Prayer".

title: Andraé Crouch
text: Crouch was noted for his talent of incorporating contemporary secular music styles into the gospel music he grew up with.

title: Andraé Crouch
text: His efforts in this area helped pave the way for early American contemporary Christian music during the 1960s and 1970s.

title: J-Shin
text: Jonathan "J-Shin" Shinoster is a contemporary R&B/gospel singer born in Liberty City, Florida, who was signed to Slip-n-Slide Records/Atlantic Records and is best known for his hit single "One Night Stand" with LaTocha Scott of Xscape.

title: Larnelle Harris
text: Larnelle Steward Harris (born July 6, 1947) is an American gospel singer and songwriter.

title: Larnelle Harris
text: During his 30-plus years of ministry, Harris has recorded 18 albums, won five Grammy Awards and 11 Dove Awards, and has had several number one songs on the inspirational music charts.

title: Kierra Sheard
text: Kierra Valencia "Kiki" Sheard (born June 20, 1987 in Detroit, Michigan) is an American gospel singer, fashion designer, and radio host.

title: Kierra Sheard
text: She is the daughter of gospel singer Karen Clark Sheard (member of gospel singing group The Clark Sisters) and the granddaughter of gospel choral director Mattie Moss Clark.

title: Kierra Sheard
text: Sheard portrayed Litha in the 2010 Christian-drama film "Preacher's Kid".

title: Kierra Sheard
text: After appearing on her mother's albums, Sheard broke onto the music scene with the release of her debut album "I Owe You" in 2004.

title: Kierra Sheard
text: Her hit single "You Don't Know" was written about her mother's bout with an almost fatal blood clot.

title: Charles Charamba
text: Charles Charamba (born 27 April 1971) is a Zimbabwean gospel musician and a pastor in the Apostolic Faith Mission Church of Zimbabwe.

title: Charles Charamba
text: Charamba's albums have been the top selling gospel music in Zimbabwe since the early 2000s.

title: Charles Charamba
text: He has toured both Great Britain and the United States, and throughout southern Africa.

title: Charles Charamba
text: One of Charamba's most famous songs is “Machira Chete”.

title: Charles Charamba
text: His wife, Olivia (née Maseko), is also a gospel singer, and appears with him on stage and on his albums; they are often called the "First Family of Gospel".

title: Latice Crawford
text: Latice Crawford (born July 22, 1982 as Latice Tenae Crawford) is an American urban contemporary gospel singer and composer.

title: Latice Crawford
text: She is best known for using her three-octave, contralto vocal range of to finish third on the second season of the competitive gospel singing television show "Sunday Best" on Black Entertainment Television.

title: Latice Crawford
text: Her self-titled debut album reached two "Billboard" charts, the Top Gospel Albums and the Top Heatseekers.

title: Latice Crawford
text: Her second album, "Diary of a Church Girl", also appeared on the Top Gospel Albums chart.

title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
text: Muyiwa Olarewaju (born 26 November is a British Gospel singer and songwriter who mixes traditional gospel music with elements of world music (from Africa, the Caribbean and Asia), soul, R&B and pop.

title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
text: He is also an experienced performer, broadcaster and presenter.

title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
text: In 2009 he became the first-ever international act to perform on America's popular entertainment channel, BET, for the prestigious annual Celebration of Gospel show.

title: Muyiwa Olarewaju

title: George Raft

title: Johnny Angel (song)

title: Johnny Angel (song)

title: Johnny Angel (song)
text: British singer Patti Lynn had a moderate hit with her cover of "Johnny Angel" the same year on the UK Singles Chart.

title: Johnny Angel (song)
text: The American pop music duo The Carpenters also covered "Johnny Angel" in 1973 as part of a medley of oldies on side two of their album "Now & Then".

title: Claudia Drake
text: Claudia Drake (January 30, 1918 – October 19, 1997) was an American actress and singer.

title: Claudia Drake
text: She appeared in a number of B Movies in a mixture of leading and supporting roles.

text: She starred in the 1945 film noir "Detour".

title: Sumie Tanaka
text: Sumie Tanaka ("田中澄江"; April 11, 1908—March 1, 2000) was a Japanese screenwriter and playwright born in Tokyo.

title: Sumie Tanaka
text: She was most well known for her long collaboration with film director Mikio Naruse and for writing screenplays for Japan's first major female director Kinuyo Tanaka.

title: Sumie Tanaka
text: Member of the Bungakuza theatre company, she was married to playwright and dramatist Chikao Tanaka.

title: Sumie Tanaka
text: The screenplays she wrote for Repast ("めし", Meshi; 1951), Home Sweet Home ("我が家は楽し ", Wa ga ya wa tanoshi; 1951), and Record of Youth ("少年期 ", Shonenki; 1951) won her the Blue Ribbon Award for Best Screenplay in 1951.

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: Michael Wynne is an English playwright born in Birkenhead on 3 August 1972.

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: While reading for a Politics degree in London, he entered a competition for new young writers run by the Royal Court Theatre.

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: He won this with his first play "The Knocky" - an award-winning comedy, set on a Birkenhead council estate.

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: It was produced at the Royal Court in 1995 and subsequently performed at Liverpool's Everyman Theatre in 1997.

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: In 2010, Wynne won the Olivier Award for Best New Comedy for "The Priory".

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: In 2011, Wynne wrote the BBC Christmas show, "Lapland".

title: Michael Wynne (playwright)
text: A series was later announced, entitled "Being Eileen", again written by Wynne, which began to air on 4 February 2013.

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: James Roland MacLaren (1839–1912) was a British actor and playwright born on 10 June 1839 in Bonhill, Scotland to Archibald MacLaren and Anne McIntyre.

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: The family later moved to Liverpool, where James Roland MacLaren first took to the stage, appearing second to Barry Sullivan, the well known Victorian actor.

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: He subsequently went to Sunderland with Alfred Davis where he took over the New Royal Lyceum Theatre (now demolished).

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: It was here with MacLaren that the actor Sir Henry Irving made his first stage appearances before moving to London where he later became famous as the inspiration for Bram Stoker's Count Dracula.

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: For some thirty years MacLaren was renowned in the north east of England as an actor in stock companies, a noted recitalist and a playwright.

title: James Roland MacLaren
text: He usually played heavy villain roles and was popular amongst the audience as the 'traitor'.

title: Three Men on a Horse
text: Three Men on a Horse is a play by George Abbott and John Cecil Holm.

title: Three Men on a Horse
text: The comedy focuses on a man who discovers he has a talent for choosing the winning horse in a race as long as he never places a bet himself.

title: DeObia Oparei

text: His parents are of Nigerian ancestry.

title: Finn Iunker

title: Finn Iunker
text: He lives in Oslo.

title: Jeffrey Stanley

title: Jeffrey Stanley
text: He began writing in elementary school, and graduated from New York University Tisch School of the Arts Undergraduate Film Program and Graduate Dramatic Writing Program.

title: Jeffrey Stanley
text: He was also a guest at Yaddo, a Copeland Fellow at Amherst College, and a 2014-15 Amtrak Residency for Writers recipient.

title: Jeffrey Stanley
text: He was a 2011-12 PDC playwright-in-residence at Philadelphia's Plays and Players Theatre.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Lenelle Moïse (born 1980) is a poet, actress and playwright born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Currently based in the United States, she performs at colleges throughout the country, presenting work about race, gender, class, immigration and sexuality.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Her spoken word CD "Madivinez" won the 2007 Patchwork Majority Radio Album Award for Best Solo Album.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Moïse was a member of the permanent ensemble cast in the Culture Project's premiere production of "Rebel Voices", a play by Rob Urbinati based on Howard Zinn and Anthony Arnove's book "Voices of a People's History of the United States."

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: In 2008, she developed a two-person vocal musical about art, infamy and race called "EXPATRIATE", also at the Culture Project, in which she co-starred with Karla Cheatham-Mosley.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: When she was a junior at Ithaca College, Lenelle co-wrote "Sexual Dependency", a feature film by Bolivian filmmaker Rodrigo Bellot who was a schoolmate at the time.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: The film went on to win the International Film Critics' Award at the Locarno International Film Festival in Switzerland.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Moïse also wrote and starred in Mara Alper's short experimental video "To Erzulie" which premiered at the Berlin Sommerfest der Literaturen in July 2002.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: She has completed her own experimental shorts "Blue Passersby Eyes" and "Atlantic Soul."

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Her homemade music video "Pied Piper" was an official selection of the International Museum of Women 2007 Online Film Festival.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Her essays and poems are published in a number of anthologies, most recently "Word Warriors: 35 Women Leaders of the Spoken Word Revolution" (Seal Press).

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: Her debut book "Haiti Glass" (City Lights Publishers, April 2014), part of the Sister Spit series, is a collection of verse and prose.

title: Lenelle Moïse
text: She experiments with collage as a form of meditative practice and nonlinear storytelling.

title: Bertha Runkle
text: Bertha Runkle (1879–1958) was an American novelist and playwright born in Berkeley Heights, New Jersey.

title: Bertha Runkle
text: From a literary family, she wrote five novels.

title: Bertha Runkle
text: Her first and best known, "The Helmet of Navarre", was made into a Broadway play.

title: George Abbott
text: George Francis Abbott (June 25, 1887 – January 31, 1995) was an American theater producer and director, playwright, screenwriter, and film director and producer whose career spanned nine decades.

title: Howard Graham Buffett
text: Howard Graham Buffett (born December 16, 1954) is an American businessman, former politician, philanthropist, photographer, farmer, and conservationist.

title: Howard Graham Buffett
text: He is the middle child of billionaire investor Warren Buffett.

title: Howard Graham Buffett
text: He is named after Howard Buffett, his grandfather, and Benjamin Graham, Warren Buffett's favorite professor.

title: George D. Buffett
