title: George D. Buffett
text: He was an arch-conservative state representative, owner of Buffett's Candy and cousin of Warren Buffett.

title: TaeguTec
text: TaeguTec Ltd. (Korean: 대구텍), formerly known as Korea Tungsten Company, is a multinational corporation headquartered in Daegu, Korea.

title: TaeguTec
text: It is the largest cutting tools manufacturer in the Far East, also Korea's largest manufacturer of tungsten cutting tools and hard metal tools with the only integrated tungsten production plant in the world.

title: TaeguTec
text: TaeguTec group has 26 overseas subsidiaries and over 130 distributors and 30 agents in 50 countries across Europe, Asia, Australia, and the American countries.

title: TaeguTec
text: Considered as the world's oldest manufacturer of tungsten and related products, the group has earned reputation for its excellent global marketing and large production capacity worldwide.

title: TaeguTec
text: In addition to the initial 80 per cent stake purchased in 2006, Warren Buffett paid additional 2 billion dollars for the remaining stake in IMC, of which TaeguTec was a part.

title: TaeguTec
text: Through this acquisition, TaeguTec became Berkshire Hathaway's first and only wholly owned subsidiary in Korea.

title: TaeguTec
text: On October 25, 2007, Buffett flew to Daegu to tour TaeguTec and to meet with the management.

title: TaeguTec
text: On March 21, 2011, Warren Buffett re-visited the firm to attend TaeguTec Plant 2 inauguration ceremony and later met with Korean President Lee Myung-bak.

title: Warren Buffett
text: Warren Edward Buffett ( ; born August 30, 1930) is an American business magnate, investor, and philanthropist.

title: Warren Buffett
text: Buffett serves as the Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Berkshire Hathaway.

title: Warren Buffett
text: He is considered by some to be one of the most successful investors in the world, and as of August 2017 is the second wealthiest person in the United States, and the fourth wealthiest in the world, with a total net worth of $76.9 billion.

title: Buffett Foundation
text: The Buffett Foundation is a charitable organization formed by Omaha, Nebraska investor and industrialist Warren Buffett as a vehicle to manage his charitable giving.

title: Buffett Foundation
text: It was renamed Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation in honor of his wife Susan Buffett when she died in 2004.

title: Howard Warren Buffett
text: Howard Warren Buffett (born October 14, 1983) is an American public relations professor, political advisor, and philanthropist.

title: Howard Warren Buffett
text: He serves as faculty member at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs and was previously the executive director of the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, a private philanthropic foundation that funds initiatives aimed at improving the standard of living and quality of life for the world’s most impoverished and marginalized populations.

title: Howard Warren Buffett
text: He previously led agriculture-based economic stabilization and redevelopment programs in Iraq and Afghanistan while at the United States Department of Defense, and as a policy advisor in the Executive Office of the President of the United States under President Barack Obama.

title: Susan Buffett
text: Susan Thompson Buffett (June 15, 1932 – July 29, 2004), the first wife of investor Warren Buffett, was active in civil rights, abortion rights and population control causes.

title: Susan Buffett
text: She was a director of Berkshire Hathaway, owning 2.2 percent (worth US$3 billion in 2004) of the company at the time of her death.

title: Susan Buffett
text: She was the 153rd richest person in the world.

title: Susan Buffett
text: She was president of the Buffett Foundation, which has contributed millions of dollars to educational groups, medical research, population-control groups and other charities.

title: Susan Alice Buffett
text: Susan Alice Buffett (born July 30, 1953) is the daughter of Warren Buffett.

title: Susan Alice Buffett
text: She is also an American philanthropist, her charitable work has focused largely on the Sherwood Foundation, formerly known as the Susan A. Buffett Foundation, an organization in Omaha that provides grants in public education, human services and social justice in the interest of promoting the welfare of children from lower-income families.

title: Susan Alice Buffett
text: She is also on the boards of the Buffett Foundation and Girls, Inc. According to a 2010 interview with her brother Howard Graham Buffett, Buffett's philanthropic focus has consistently remained on children, education and family issues, but she has also committed to other causes, including Debt, AIDS, Trade, Africa, a non-governmental organization dedicated to various improvements in Africa.

title: The Warren Buffett Way
text: The Warren Buffett Way, a book by author Robert Hagstrom, outlines the principles of value investing practiced by successful investor Warren Buffett.

title: Owner earnings
text: Owner earnings is a valuation method detailed by Warren Buffett in 1986.

title: Owner earnings
text: He stated that the value of a company is simply the total of the net cash flows (owner earnings) expected to occur over the life of the business, minus any reinvestment of earnings.

title: 413th Flight Test Squadron

text: It performs flight testing on C-130 Hercules, CV-22 Osprey, MH-53 Pave Low, UH-1 Iroquois, and HH-60 Pave Hawk aircraft.

title: 486th Flight Test Squadron
text: The 486th Flight Test Squadron is a secretive unit, with a somewhat misleading designation, assigned to Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, and which is associated with United States Department of State Foreign Emergency Support Team activities.

title: 486th Flight Test Squadron
text: The squadron motto is ""Non semper ea sunt quae videntur"" which translates as "Not always what they seem".

title: 486th Flight Test Squadron
text: It was apparently assigned to the 227th Special Operations Flight, later redesignated the 150th Special Operations Squadron, McGuire Air Force Base, New Jersey, but is currently assigned to the 46th Test Wing at Eglin, and operates a pair of Boeing C-32B or Boeing 757-23A aircraft, on stand-by alert for special operations and intelligence missions world-wide.

title: 486th Flight Test Squadron
text: Official documents make it clear that operations fall under the aegis of Air Force Special Operations Command.

title: Hill Air Force Base

title: Hill Air Force Base

title: Heaven in Judaism

title: Heaven in Judaism

title: Tabernacle

title: Tabernacle

title: Tabernacle

title: Inquiline
text: In zoology, an inquiline (from Latin "inquilinus", "lodger" or "tenant") is an animal that lives commensally in the nest, burrow, or dwelling place of an animal of another species.

title: Inquiline
text: For example, some organisms such as insects may live in the homes of gophers and feed on debris, fungi, roots, etc.

title: Inquiline
text: The most widely distributed types of inquiline are those found in association with the nests of social insects, especially ants and termites – a single colony may support dozens of different inquiline species.

title: Inquiline
text: The distinctions between parasites, social parasites, and inquilines are subtle, and many species may fulfill the criteria for more than one of these, as inquilines do exhibit many of the same characteristics as parasites.

title: Inquiline
text: However, parasites are specifically "not" inquilines, because by definition they have a deleterious effect on the host species, while inquilines do not.

title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: Although attempts to regulate campaign finance by legislation date back to 1867, the modern era of "campaign finance reform" in the United States begins with the passage of the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA) of 1971 and, more importantly, 1974 amendments to that Act.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::1
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: The 1971 FECA required candidates to disclose sources of campaign contributions and campaign expenditures.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::2
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: The 1974 Amendments essentially rewrote the Act from top to bottom.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::3
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: The 1974 Amendments placed statutory limits on contributions by individuals for the first time, and created the Federal Election Commission (FEC) as an independent enforcement agency.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::4
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: It provided for broad new disclosure requirements, and limited the amounts that candidates could spend on their campaigns, or that citizens could spend separate from candidate campaigns to promote their political views.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::5
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: Specifically, it attempted to restrict the influence of wealthy individuals by limiting individual donations to $1,000 and donations by political action committees (PACs) to $5,000.

chunk_id: 5a879adb5542996e4f30887f::Campaign finance reform in the United States::6
title: Campaign finance reform in the United States
text: However, the Act's provisions limiting expenditures were struck down as unconstitutional in the 1976 Supreme Court decision Buckley v. Valeo.

title: Oakland, California
text: Oakland is the largest city and the county seat of Alameda County, California, United States.

title: Oakland, California
text: A major West Coast port city, Oakland is the largest city in the East Bay region of the San Francisco Bay Area, the third largest city overall in the San Francisco Bay Area, the eighth largest city in California, and the 45th largest city in the United States, with a population of 419,267 as of 2015 .

title: Oakland, California
text: It serves as a trade center for the San Francisco Bay Area; its Port of Oakland is the busiest port in the San Francisco Bay, the entirety of Northern California, and the fifth busiest in the United States of America.

title: Oakland, California
text: The city was incorporated in 1852.

title: Ragazzi Boys Chorus
text: The Ragazzi Boys Chorus is a boys' and young men's chorus in the San Francisco Bay Area San Francisco Bay Area and is known for winning a Grammy Award for Best Classical Album in 2000 for its participation in Perséphone with the San Francisco Symphony.

title: Ragazzi Boys Chorus
text: The chorus was formed in 1987 with 6 boys, and it now includes more than 170 singers from 86 schools in 26 Bay Area communities including San Mateo, Santa Clara and Santa Cruz counties.

title: Ragazzi Boys Chorus
text: The choir has placed highly in numerous international competitions.

title: Ragazzi Boys Chorus
text: It also auditions the most singers to either national or state American Choral Directors Association honor choirs each year.

title: Codornices Creek
text: Codornices Creek (sometimes spelled and/or pronounced "Cordonices"), 2.0 mi long, is one of the principal creeks which runs out of the Berkeley Hills in the East Bay area of the San Francisco Bay Area in California.

title: Codornices Creek
text: In its upper stretch, it passes entirely within the city limits of Berkeley, and marks the city limit with the adjacent city of Albany in its lower section.

title: Codornices Creek
text: Before European settlement, Codornices probably had no direct, permanent connection to San Francisco Bay.

title: Codornices Creek
text: Like many other small creeks, it filtered through what early maps show as grassland to a large, northward-running salt marsh and slough that also carried waters from Marin Creek and Schoolhouse Creek.

title: Codornices Creek
text: A channel was cut through in the 19th Century, and Codornices flows directly to San Francisco Bay by way of a narrow remnant slough adjacent to Golden Gate Fields racetrack.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: The Association of Bay Area Governments (ABAG) is a regional planning agency incorporating various local governments in the San Francisco Bay Area in California.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: It encompasses nine counties surrounding the San Francisco Bay.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: Those counties are Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Solano, and Sonoma.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: It has the ability to establish housing and transportation goals for cities to minimize urban sprawl by that requiring housing be zoned for near new workplace construction.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: It deals with land use, housing, environmental quality, and economic development.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: Non-profit organizations as well as governmental organizations can be members.

title: Association of Bay Area Governments
text: All nine counties and 101 cities within the Bay Area are voluntary members of ABAG.

title: San Francisco Bay Area Water Trail
text: The San Francisco Bay Area Water Trail is a growing network of launch and landing sites that allow people in non-motorized small boats and beachable sail craft such as kayaks, canoes, dragon boats, stand up paddle and windsurf boards, to safely enjoy San Francisco Bay through single and multiple-day trips.

title: San Francisco Bay Area Water Trail
text: The Water Trail is enhancing Bay Area communities’ connections to the Bay and creating new linkages to existing shoreline open spaces and other regional trails as well as increasing education about personal safety, navigational safety, and appropriate boating behavior near sensitive wildlife species and shoreline habitat.

title: San Francisco Bay Area Water Trail
text: The Water Trail is implemented under the leadership of the California Coastal Conservancy in close collaboration with the Association of Bay Area Governments, the San Francisco Bay Conservation and Development Commission, and the California Department of Boating and Waterways.

title: Old and in the Way (album)
text: Old and in the Way is the self-titled first album by the bluegrass band Old and in the Way.

title: Old and in the Way (album)

title: Old and in the Way (album)

title: Old and in the Way (album)

title: Key System
text: The Key System (or Key Route) was a privately owned company that provided mass transit in the cities of Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, Emeryville, Piedmont, San Leandro, Richmond, Albany and El Cerrito in the eastern San Francisco Bay Area from 1903 until 1960, when it was sold to a newly formed public agency, AC Transit.

title: Key System
text: The Key System consisted of local streetcar and bus lines in the East Bay, and commuter rail and bus lines connecting the East Bay to San Francisco by a ferry pier on San Francisco Bay, later via the lower deck of the Bay Bridge.

title: Key System
text: At its height during the 1940s, the Key System had over 66 mi of track.

title: Key System
text: The local streetcars were discontinued in 1948 and the commuter trains to San Francisco were discontinued in 1958.

title: Key System
text: The Key System's territory is today served by BART and AC Transit bus service.

title: Owsley Stanley
text: Owsley Stanley (born Augustus Owsley Stanley III, January 19, 1935 – March 12, 2011) was an American audio engineer and clandestine chemist.

title: Owsley Stanley
text: He was a key figure in the San Francisco Bay Area hippie movement during the 1960s and played a pivotal role in the counterculture of the 1960s.

title: Owsley Stanley
text: Under the professional name Bear, he was the soundman for the rock band the Grateful Dead, whom he met when Ken Kesey invited them to an Acid Test party.

title: Owsley Stanley
text: As their sound engineer, Stanley frequently recorded live tapes behind his mixing board, designed their trademark skull logo, and developed their Wall of Sound sound system, one of the largest mobile public address systems ever constructed.

title: Gary Arlington

title: Gary Arlington

title: Gary Arlington

title: Gary Arlington

title: Old US 67 Rest Area
text: The Old US 67 Rest Area is a historic roadside rest area in rural Clark County, Arkansas.

title: Old US 67 Rest Area

title: Old US 67 Rest Area

title: Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame
text: The Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame is a collection of plaques, mounted on a brick wall in the Ashburn Alley section of Citizens Bank Park, the ballpark of the Philadelphia Phillies.

title: Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame

title: Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame

title: Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame

title: Philadelphia Baseball Wall of Fame

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: The Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry was an American college football rivalry between the Texas A&M Aggies football team of Texas A&M University and Texas Tech Red Raiders football team of Texas Tech University.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: The series began in 1927.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: The rivalry had continued uninterrupted since 1957 when the two schools became conference rivals.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas A&M leads the series 37–32–1.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas A&M started the series with a 12–3 advantage while the two teams played each other as non-conference opponents from 1927–1955.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas Tech took a 2–1 record during its probationary membership in the Southwest Conference from 1957–59.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas A&M led the series during the Southwest Conference years (1960–95) with an 18–17–1 record.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas Tech led the series during the Big 12 Conference years (1996–2011) with a 10–6 record.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Both teams are tied with six games each for the longest winning streak.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas Tech holds the longest uninterrupted winning streak of the series, six games between 1968 and 1973, while Texas A&M has the longest nonconsecutive winning streak, six games in 1927, 1932 and 1942 through 1945.

title: Texas A&M–Texas Tech football rivalry
text: Texas A&M currently holds a three-game winning streak but with their departure from the Big 12 Conference in 2012, it is uncertain if the rivalry will continue in the future.

title: Claude Auchinleck
text: Field Marshal Sir Claude John Eyre Auchinleck {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (21 June 1884 – 23 March 1981) was a British Army commander during the Second World War.

title: Claude Auchinleck
text: He was a career soldier who spent much of his military career in India, where he rose to become Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army by early 1941.

title: Claude Auchinleck
text: In July 1941 he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Middle East theatre, but after initial successes the war in North Africa turned against the British, and he was relieved of the post in 1942 during the crucial Alamein campaign.

title: Claude Auchinleck

title: Claude Auchinleck

text: Field Marshal Stapleton Cotton, 1st Viscount Combermere {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (14 November 1773 – 21 February 1865), was a British Army officer, diplomat and politician.

title: Stapleton Cotton, 1st Viscount Combermere

text: It was constructed by Bharatpur Jat rulers.

title: Lohagarh Fort
text: Maharaja Suraj Mal used all his power and wealth to a good cause, and built numerous forts and palaces across his kingdom, one of them being the Lohagarh Fort (Iron fort), which was one of the strongest ever built in Indian history.

title: Lohagarh Fort
text: The inaccessible Lohagarh fort could withstand repeated attacks of British forces led by Lord Lake in 1805 when they laid siege for over six weeks.

title: Lohagarh Fort
text: Of the two gates in the fort, one in the north is known as Ashtdhaatu (eight metalled) gate while the one facing the south is called Chowburja (four-pillared) gate.

title: Siege of Bharatpur

text: The Last Embrace is the final release by Spirit Caravan.

title: The Last Embrace
text: It was released on 2xCD and 2xLP in 2003 by Meteor City Records.

title: The Last Embrace
text: It contains 19 songs from their two albums, "Jug Fulla Sun" and "Elusive Truth", the three songs that appeared on their debut 7" (under the name Shine), the two songs from their final 7", "Spirit Caravan", the song from their split 7" with Sixty Watt Shaman and their song from the Rise 13 compilation on Rise Above Records.

title: The Last Embrace
text: It also features the last three songs Spirit Caravan recorded, "The Last Embrace," "Brainwashed" and "Dove-Tongued Aggressor."

title: Discovery Museum and Planetarium
text: The Discovery Museum and Planetarium is a hands-on science museum in Bridgeport, Connecticut, that serves as both a tourist destination and an educational resource for area schools.

title: Discovery Museum and Planetarium
text: The Discovery Museum provides dynamic, hands-on STEM experiences designed to resonate with the innate curiosity, learning desire, and spirit of exploration of visitors, encouraging young learners to ask questions, solve problems, and engineer solutions today so they are better prepared to embrace the challenges of tomorrow.

title: Discovery Institute
text: The Discovery Institute (DI) is a politically conservative non-profit think tank based in Seattle, Washington, best known for its advocacy of the pseudoscientific principle of intelligent design (ID).

title: Discovery Institute
text: Its "Teach the Controversy" campaign aims to permit teaching of anti-evolution, intelligent-design beliefs in United States public high school science courses alongside accepted scientific theories, positing that a scientific controversy exists over these subjects.

title: Truth Initiative
text: Truth Initiative (formerly the American Legacy Foundation or Legacy) is a nonprofit tobacco control organization "dedicated to achieving a culture where all youth and young adults reject tobacco."

title: Truth Initiative
text: It was established in March 1999 as a result of the Master Settlement Agreement between the attorneys general of 46 states, the District of Columbia and five United States territories, and the tobacco industry.

title: Truth Initiative
text: Truth Initiative is best known for its youth smoking prevention campaign.

title: Truth Initiative
text: Its other primary aims include conducting tobacco control research and policy studies, organizing community and youth engagement programs and developing digital cessation and prevention products, including through revenue-generating models.

title: Truth Initiative
text: The organization changed its name from the American Legacy Foundation to Truth Initiative on September 8, 2015, to better align with its Truth campaign.

title: Truth Initiative
text: As of 2016, the organization had more than $957 million in assets and a staff of 133 based primarily in its Washington, D.C. office.

title: Extrema (band)
text: Extrema formed in 1986 in Milan.

title: Extrema (band)
text: The initial lineup included guitarist Tommy Massara, vocalist/guitarist Andrea Boria, bassist Luca Varisco, and drummer Stefano Bullegas.

title: Extrema (band)
text: Regarded as one of Italy's first thrash metal bands, Extrema's first EP, "We F**kin' Care" (1987), sold an impressive 3,000 copies by word of mouth alone.

title: Extrema (band)
text: Italian heavy metal fans didn't yet seem prepared to embrace local talent, however, and the next four years saw Extrema (by then entirely re-vamped, with Massara signing on new members Gianluca Perotti on vocals, Mattia Bigi on bass, and Chris Dalla Pellegrina on drums) relegated to open for visiting acts like Slayer, D.R.I., and Corrosion of Conformity.

title: Extrema (band)
text: Finally realizing that their only hope of impressing local talent scouts lay in conquering from the outside-in, Extrema started aggressively shopping their demos to international heavy metal critics, and even financed a trip to New York City for a one-off gig.

title: Extrema (band)
text: The strategy worked, and their four-track demo from 1991 was soon making waves with some major international publications, eventually leading to a record deal with Contempo Records.

title: Extrema (band)
text: The result was the 1993's "Tension at the Seams" album, which led to stadium support slots with Italian rock star Vasco Rossi, and more importantly a high-profile metal festival appearance in Turin alongside Megadeth, The Cult, Suicidal Tendencies, and Metallica.

title: Extrema (band)
text: The album also featured an unconventional cover of The Police's "Truth Hits Everybody" and spawned a video clip for the track "Child O' Boogaow" which was on heavy rotation on Italy's MTV affiliate, Videomusic.

title: Truth (anti-tobacco campaign)
text: Truth (stylized as truth) is a national campaign aimed at curbing youth smoking in the United States.

title: Truth (anti-tobacco campaign)
text: The "truth" campaign is produced and funded by the American Legacy Foundation, a public health nonprofit organization established in 1999 under the Master Settlement Agreement between U.S. tobacco companies, 46 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, and five territories.

title: Truth (anti-tobacco campaign)
text: "truth" produces television and online content to promote anti-tobacco messages.

title: Truth (anti-tobacco campaign)
text: In August 2014, "truth" launched "Finish It", a redesigned campaign encouraging youth to be the generation that ends smoking.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: An unforgiving sun, a parched earth, and a failed economy have left a small Texas town desolate.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: For ten years Promise, Texas has known nothing but one curse after another.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: It's barren, broken, and dying, leaving a town full of despair.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: When a couple finds a boy walking along a dusty road, alone in the middle of nowhere, with nothing but a mat tucked under his arm, they pick him up in hopes of helping him.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: What they don't realize is that he has come to help them and the residents of Promise.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: No one knows who he is or where he came from.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: Some think he's an answer to prayer.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: Others think he's a runaway or a false prophet.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: And the only thing this boy will say about himself is that he's here to help.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: The town's sheriff, Brody, is determined to uncover the truth.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: But Brody has his own problems trying to hold a dying town together.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: Miracle after miracle takes place and the residents of Promise embrace the boy.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: But when the beloved town doctor dies, it is time for the truth to be revealed.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: The boy pleads with Brody in front of the whole town to believe that he's come to help, not to hurt anyone.

title: I Am... Gabriel
text: Finally, with his back against the wall the boy reveals his true identity.

title: Discovery Networks Benelux

title: Discovery Networks Benelux

title: Where We Belong (Lostprophets song)

title: Ian Watkins (Lostprophets)

title: Ian Watkins (Lostprophets)

title: Ian Watkins (Lostprophets)

title: Lostprophets

title: Under Your Skin (album)

title: Under Your Skin (album)

title: We Bring an Arsenal
text: It has been released to rock radio since this date in the United States, but the single has yet to be officially released in the UK as of 5 June 2012, but will unlikely happen due to Ian Watkins's imprisonment in 2013.

title: We Bring an Arsenal

text: It is the first album to feature singer Bobby Amaru, after Josey Scott left the band in 2012.

title: In It to Win It (Saliva album)
text: The album was temporarily released via Rum Bum Records on September 3, 2013.

title: In It to Win It (Saliva album)
text: The album is no longer available for purchase as the band rereleased the album as "Rise Up" features all of its songs except "Animal", "Flesh", and "I.D.N.A.E".

title: Always (Saliva song)
text: "Always" is the first single off the album "Back into Your System" by the rock band Saliva with lead vocalist Josey Scott.

title: Always (Saliva song)
text: It made it to number 1 on the Modern Rock Tracks for one week in February 2003, and has been Saliva's most successful hit, peaking at #51 on the Hot 100.

title: Josey Scott

title: Josey Scott
text: In addition to Saliva, Scott co-wrote and performed "Hero" (which was used as one of the theme songs to the 2002 film "Spider-Man") with Chad Kroeger of Nickelback.

text: Jayne has attained nine number-one songs on the Dance Club Songs chart as of 2016, most recently "How Many Fucks".

title: Marisa Letícia Lula da Silva
text: Marisa Letícia Lula da Silva (née Rocco Casa; São Bernardo do Campo, 7 April 1950 – São Paulo, 3 February 2017) was the second wife of former President of Brazil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and First Lady of Brazil from 2003 to 2010.

title: Marisa Letícia Lula da Silva
text: Lula's first wife, Maria de Lourdes da Silva, died in labour when Lula was in his twenties.

title: Marisa Letícia Lula da Silva
text: And Marisa'a first spouse, Marcos Cláudio da Silva, died in 1971.

title: Fortaleza Metro
text: The Fortaleza Metro (Portuguese: "Metrô de Fortaleza" , commonly called "Metrofor") is the meter gauge 43 km metropolitan rail system that operates in the city of Fortaleza in Ceará, Brazil.

title: Fortaleza Metro
text: It is operated by Companhia Cearense Metropolitan Transport, which was founded in May 2, 1997, and is responsible for the management, construction and subway system planning in the city of Fortaleza and its metropolitan area.

title: Fortaleza Metro

title: Marco Da Silva (dancer)

title: José Graziano da Silva
text: José Graziano da Silva (born November 17, 1949) is a Brazilian American agronomist and writer.

title: José Graziano da Silva
text: As a scholar, he has authored several books about the problems of agriculture in Brazil.

title: José Graziano da Silva
text: Between 2003 and 2004, Graziano served in the Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cabinet as Extraordinary Minister for Food Security, being responsible for implementing the Fome Zero (Zero Hunger) program, which took 28 million people out of the national poverty line during the 8 years of the Lula administration .

title: José Graziano da Silva
text: On June 26, 2011, Graziano was elected director-general of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), becoming the first Latin American ever to hold the position.

title: José Graziano da Silva
text: After his first term from 1 January 2012 to 31 July 2015, Graziano da Silva was re-elected for a second 4 year-term (1 August 2015 to 31 July 2019) during FAO's 39th Conference.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: Kargil War Memorial, also known as the Vijaypath, is a war memorial built by the Indian Army, located in Dras, in the foothills of the Tololing Hill.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: The memorial is located about 5 km from the city centre across the Tiger Hill.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: It is located on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway 1D.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: The memorial is in the memory of the soldiers and officers of the Indian Army who were killed during the 1999 conflict between India and Pakistan.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: The conflict later became known as the "Kargil War".

title: Dras War Memorial
text: The memorial has a huge epitaph with names of all the officers and soldiers who died in war.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: Kargil Vijay Diwas is celebrated on 26 July every year at the memorial simultaneously the Prime Minister of India pays tribute to the soldiers at Amar Jawan Jyothi at the India Gate, New Delhi.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: The main attraction of the whole memorial is the Sandstone wall, in the open, which has the names of all the Indian army personnel, who laid their lives during the Kargil war besides there is also a souvenir shop.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: Visitors to the memorial can also see from there, some of the peaks that the Indian army captured back from Pakistan.

title: Dras War Memorial
text: A giant national flag, weighing 15 kg was hoisted at the Kargil war memorial to commemorate the 13th anniversary of India’s victory in the war

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: The Devon County War Memorial is a First World War memorial, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and situated on the cathedral green in Exeter, the county town of Devon, in the south west of England.

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: It is one of fifteen War Crosses designed by Lutyens to a similar specification, and one of two to serve as a civic memorial in a city.

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: The first proposal for the county's war memorial was to complete the construction of a cloister at Exeter Cathedral to be dedicated to the Devon's war dead, but this scheme was abandoned due to lack of funds.

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: After considering multiple proposals, the Devon County War Memorial Committee commissioned Lutyens to design a War Cross instead.

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: The committee chose to site the memorial on the green of Exeter Cathedral after scouting several locations.

title: Devon County War Memorial
text: A war memorial for Exeter itself was being considered concurrently, but the committees for the two projects failed to work together, resulting in two separate memorials—the county memorial by the cathedral and Exeter City War Memorial in Northernhay Gardens.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: Manchester Cenotaph is a First World War memorial, with additions for later conflicts, by Sir Edwin Lutyens in St Peter's Square in Manchester, England.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: Manchester was late in commissioning a war memorial compared to most British towns and cities—the city council did not convene a war memorial committee until 1922.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: The committee quickly raised £10,000 but finding a suitable location for the monument proved controversial.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: The preferred site in Albert Square, requiring the removal and relocation of several statues, was opposed by the city's artistic community.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: The next choice was Piccadilly Gardens, an area ripe for development, but in the interests of expediency, the council chose St Peter's Square, although it already contained a memorial cross to the former St Peter's Church.

title: Manchester Cenotaph
text: Negotiations to move the cross were unsuccessful and the war memorial was built with the cross in situ.

title: York City War Memorial
text: The York City War Memorial is a First World War memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and located in York in the north of England.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Proposals for commemorating York's war dead originated in 1919 but proved controversial.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Initial discussions focused on whether a memorial should be a monument or should take on some utilitarian purpose.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Several functional proposals were examined until a public meeting in January 1920 opted for a monument.

title: York City War Memorial
text: The city engineer produced a cost estimate and the war memorial committee engaged Lutyens, who had recently been commissioned by the North Eastern Railway (NER) to design their own war memorial, also to be sited in York.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Lutyens' first design was approved, but controversy enveloped proposals for both the city's and the NER's memorials.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Members of the local community became concerned that the memorials as planned were not in keeping with York's existing architecture, especially as both were in close proximity to the ancient city walls, and that the NER's memorial would overshadow the city's.

title: York City War Memorial
text: Continued public opposition forced the committee to abandon the proposed site in favour of one on Leeman Road, just outside the walls, and Lutyens submitted a new design of a War Cross and Stone of Remembrance to fit the location.

title: York City War Memorial
text: This was scaled back to the cross alone due to lack of funds.

title: Maiwand Lion
text: The Maiwand Lion is a sculpture and war memorial in the Forbury Gardens, a public park in the town of Reading, in the English county of Berkshire.

title: Maiwand Lion
text: The statue was named after the Battle of Maiwand and was erected in 1884 to commemorate the deaths of 329 men from the 66th (Berkshire) Regiment of Foot during the campaign in the Second Anglo-Afghan War in Afghanistan between 1878 and 1880.

title: Maiwand Lion
text: It is sometimes known locally as the Forbury Lion.

title: Reading Post
text: The Reading Post (until 2009, the Reading Evening Post), was an English local newspaper covering Reading, Berkshire and surrounding areas.

title: Reading Post
text: The title page of the paper featured the Maiwand Lion, a famous local landmark at Forbury Gardens.

title: Reading Post

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: Spalding War Memorial is a First World War memorial in the gardens of Ayscoughfee Hall (pronounced ) in Spalding, Lincolnshire, in eastern England.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: It was designed by the architect Sir Edwin Lutyens.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: The proposal for a memorial to Spalding's war dead originated in January 1918 with Barbara McLaren, whose husband and the town's Member of Parliament, Francis McLaren, was killed in a flying accident during the war.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: She engaged Lutyens via a family connection and the architect produced a plan for a grand memorial cloister surrounding a circular pond, in the middle of which would be a cross.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: The memorial was to be built in the formal gardens of Ayscoughfee Hall, which was owned by the local district council.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: When McLaren approached the council with her proposal, it generated considerable debate within the community and several alternative schemes were suggested.

title: Spalding War Memorial
text: After a public meeting and a vote in 1919, a reduced-scale version of McLaren's proposal emerged as the preferred option, in conjunction with a clock on the town's corn exchange building.

title: Kerosene lamp

title: Kerosene lamp

title: Kerosene lamp

title: Kerosene lamp

title: Glow switch starter
text: A glow switch starter is a type of preheat starter used with fluorescent lamp.

title: Glow switch starter
text: It is commonly filled with neon gas or argon gas and contains a bimetallic strip and a stationary electrode.

title: Glow switch starter
text: The operating principle is simple, when current is applied, the gas inside ionizes and heats a bimetallic strip which in turn bends toward the stationary electrode thus shorting the starter between the electrodes of the fluorescent lamp After a second the starter's bimetallic strip will cool and open the circuit between the electrodes and the process repeats until the lamp has lit.

title: Glow switch starter
text: One disadvantage of glow switch starters is that when the lamp is at the end of its life it will continuously blink on and off until the glow switch starter wears out or an electrode on the fluorescent lamp burns out.

title: Carbon button lamp

title: Carbon button lamp
text: A carbon button lamp contains a small carbon sphere positioned in the center of an evacuated glass bulb.

title: Carbon button lamp
text: This type of lamp must be driven by high-frequency alternating current, and depends on an electric arc or perhaps a vacuum arc to produce high current around the carbon electrode.

title: Carbon button lamp
text: The carbon electrode is then heated to incandescence by collisions by ions which constitute the electric current.

title: Carbon button lamp
text: Tesla found that these lamps could be used as powerful sources of ionizing radiation.

title: Battle of Cross Keys
text: The Battle of Cross Keys was fought on June 8, 1862, in Rockingham County, Virginia, as part of Confederate Army Maj. Gen. Thomas J. "Stonewall" Jackson's campaign through the Shenandoah Valley during the American Civil War.

title: Battle of Cross Keys
text: Together, the battles of Cross Keys and Port Republic the following day were the decisive victories in Jackson's Valley Campaign, forcing the Union armies to retreat and leaving Jackson free to reinforce Gen. Robert E. Lee for the Seven Days Battles outside Richmond, Virginia.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: The Battle of Gaines's Mill, sometimes known as the First Battle of Cold Harbor or the Battle of Chickahominy River, took place on June 27, 1862, in Hanover County, Virginia, as the third of the Seven Days Battles (Peninsula Campaign) of the American Civil War.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: Following the inconclusive Battle of Beaver Dam Creek (Mechanicsville) the previous day, Confederate General Robert E. Lee renewed his attacks against the right flank of the Union Army, relatively isolated on the northern side of the Chickahominy River.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: There, Brig. Gen. Fitz John Porter's V Corps had established a strong defensive line behind Boatswain's Swamp.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: Lee's force was destined to launch the largest Confederate attack of the war, about 57,000 men in six divisions.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: Porter's reinforced V Corps held fast for the afternoon as the Confederates attacked in a disjointed manner, first with the division of Maj. Gen. A.P. Hill, then Maj. Gen. Richard S. Ewell, suffering heavy casualties.

title: Battle of Gaines's Mill
text: The arrival of Maj. Gen. Stonewall Jackson's command was delayed, preventing the full concentration of Confederate force before Porter received some reinforcements from the VI Corps.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: Savage's Station was the wartime name of a supply depot, ammunition dump, field hospital, and command headquarters of the Army of the Potomac during the Peninsula Campaign of the American Civil War.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: Savage's Station was located in Henrico County, Virginia on what was the Richmond and York River Railroad, however the historical department of the Norfolk Southern Railroad, the railroad track's current owner, has no record that an actual train station or station house ever existed on the property.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: A farmhouse is known to have been located in a copse of trees on a small knoll next to the railroad track and is visible in several period drawings and photographs made during the war.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: The house served as the nucleus of a large field hospital during and after the battle of Seven Pines and the Seven Days Battles.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: The house also functioned as General George B. McClellan's headquarters during the battle of Savage's Station on June 29, 1862.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: Although the house survived the battle in 1862, it was burned by Federal cavalry under General Philip H. Sheridan in 1864.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: The house appears to have never been rebuilt, and no trace of it remains today.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: However, a smokehouse from the 19th century still existed on the property as late as the 1930s when it was photographed during a survey of local historical structures as a project of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: The smokehouse fell into ruin and collapsed sometime prior to the 1980s.

title: Savage's Station, Virginia
text: A small brick-walled cemetery from the 18th century still sits near the former location of the house not far from the railroad track.

title: Battle of Port Republic
text: The Battle of Port Republic was fought on June 9, 1862, in Rockingham County, Virginia, as part of Confederate Army Maj. Gen. Thomas J. "Stonewall" Jackson's campaign through the Shenandoah Valley during the American Civil War.

title: Battle of Port Republic
text: Port Republic was a fierce contest between two equally determined foes and was the most costly battle fought by Jackson's Army of the Valley during its campaign.

title: Battle of Port Republic
text: Together, the battles of Cross Keys (fought the previous day) and Port Republic were the decisive victories in Jackson's Valley Campaign, forcing the Union armies to retreat and leaving Jackson free to reinforce Gen. Robert E. Lee for the Seven Days Battles outside Richmond, Virginia.

title: Seven Days Battles
text: The Seven Days Battles were a series of six major battles over the seven days from June 25 to July 1, 1862, near Richmond, Virginia, during the American Civil War.

title: Seven Days Battles
text: Confederate General Robert E. Lee drove the invading Union Army of the Potomac, commanded by Maj. Gen. George B. McClellan, away from Richmond and into a retreat down the Virginia Peninsula.

title: Seven Days Battles
text: The series of battles is sometimes known erroneously as the Seven Days Campaign, but it was actually the culmination of the Peninsula Campaign, not a separate campaign in its own right.

title: Northern Virginia Campaign
text: The Northern Virginia Campaign, also known as the Second Bull Run Campaign or Second Manassas Campaign, was a series of battles fought in Virginia during August and September 1862 in the Eastern Theater of the American Civil War.

title: Northern Virginia Campaign
text: Confederate General Robert E. Lee followed up his successes of the Seven Days Battles in the Peninsula Campaign by moving north toward Washington, D.C., and defeating Maj. Gen. John Pope and his Army of Virginia.

title: Battle of Malvern Hill
text: The Battle of Malvern Hill, also known as the Battle of Poindexter's Farm, was fought on July 1, 1862 between the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia, led by Gen. Robert E. Lee, and the Union Army of the Potomac under Maj. Gen. George B. McClellan.

title: Battle of Malvern Hill
text: It was the final battle of the Seven Days Battles during the American Civil War, taking place on a 130 ft elevation of land known as Malvern Hill, near the Confederate capital of Richmond, Virginia and just one mile (1.6 km) from the James River.

title: Battle of Malvern Hill
text: Including inactive reserves, more than fifty thousand soldiers from each side took part, using more than two hundred pieces of artillery and three warships.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Maxine's Tap Room is a historic bar in Fayetteville, Arkansas, located on 107 N. Block Ave. It is one of the oldest bars in Northwest Arkansas.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Marjorie Maxine Miller opened the bar in 1950 when she was 24 years old with money she borrowed from her parents.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: She managed to pay her parents back within the year.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: In 1960 she tore down the old wooden building in which the bar had been located and had the current building—a long, narrow brick structure—built in its place.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: The new building had only one window, exactly 8.5 in by 40 in , in the front, which was the minimum size allowed by the building codes at the time.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: This was more than likely a business decision aimed at limiting break-ins.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Other examples of Miller's shrewd business style include keeping a club behind the bar, having only a pay phone available, and trying to hire football players as employees so the team would follow as patrons, a business style that led to the bar's longevity and success.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Adding to the Tap Room's charm were a 50 ft -long bar that stretched nearly the entire length of the building and dominated the room, an old coin-operated cigarette machine, a juke box that still played 45s, and a deer head adorned with Mardi Gras beads, sunglasses and a tie.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Miller was a constant figure behind the cash register for 50 years until her health started to decline around 2000.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: She died at age 82 in May 2006.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: A month later the Tap Room caught fire.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Due to lack of insurance the bar was closed for over a year, reopening in August 2007.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Most of the furniture inside the bar was replaced, including the bar.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: The exposed rafters darkened by the fire were simply painted black, and a skylight was installed where the roof had burned through.

title: Maxine's Tap Room
text: Considerable efforts were made to retain many things that had been in the bar for a very long time, such as the older lights and signs.

title: I Love to Laugh
