title: Walkdown
text: For example the chords G Major and E minor (a minor third apart) may be joined by an intervening chord to create stepwise motion in the bass: G-D/F♯ -Em (I-V6/4-vi).

title: Walkdown
text: The second chord, D Major, is performed with its third note, the F#, in the bass.

title: Walkdown
text: Walkdowns may be performed by the upright bass player, the electric bass player, the guitarist, or a piano player.

title: Dave Meros
text: Dave Meros (born 8 February 1956 in Salinas, California), is an American bass guitar player, best known as the bass player for progressive rock band Spock's Beard.

title: Dave Meros
text: Meros is also currently the bass player for Iron Butterfly and has also played with such artists as Gary Myrick, Bobby Kimball of Toto, Simon Phillips, Steve Lukather, Michael Landau, Glenn Hughes, Mark Lindsay of Paul Revere and the Raiders and Big Big Train, and played for Eric Burdon and The Animals for nearly 16 years.

title: Dave Meros
text: He was also tour manager for many of those years and has worked as a tour manager for further artists as well.

title: Dave Meros
text: As a bassist, Meros' musical influences are varied, including Paul McCartney, John Entwistle, Chris Squire, James Jamerson, Marcus Miller, Francis "Rocco" Prestia of Tower of Power, Chuck Rainey and David Hungate.

title: Sean Yseult
text: Sean Yseult (born June 6, 1966) is an American rock musician.

title: Sean Yseult
text: She currently plays bass in the band Star & Dagger.

title: Sean Yseult
text: She has played various instruments with different bands over the years, most notably her bass work with the band White Zombie.

title: Double Dagger
text: Double Dagger was a post-punk trio from Baltimore, Maryland composed of only drums, vocals, and a very loud bass guitar which fills the space a guitar would normally take.

title: Double Dagger
text: Vocalist Nolen Strals and bassist Bruce Willen also comprised the graphic design team Post Typography, which has done work for some very high-profile clients, including the New York Times.

title: Double Dagger
text: Hence, Double Dagger made a habit of referring to their style of post-hardcore as "graphicdesigncore" early in their career.

title: Double Dagger
text: In October 2011, Double Dagger broke up after a small final tour.

title: Double Dagger
text: Their final EP 333 was released in April 2013 alongside a documentary of their final tour, entitled "If We Shout Loud Enough".

title: Didi Beck
text: Didi Beck is a German electric bass and double bass player.

title: Didi Beck
text: He plays in the rockabilly band, the Boppin'B.

title: Didi Beck
text: An accomplished upright bass slap bass player, he teaches slap bass and has written an instruction book on slapping, and a made a video entitled "How to Learn the Rockabilly Slap Bass Starring Didi Beck".

title: Didi Beck
text: His rapid, virtuosic slapping technique can be heard online.

title: Winnebago Deal
text: Winnebago Deal are a rock music band from Oxford, United Kingdom.

title: Winnebago Deal
text: They started life in the late 1990s at Bartholomew School in Eynsham, with Ben Perrier (vocals, guitar) and Ben Thomas (then on guitar) writing songs then recruiting a drummer and bass player through an ad.

title: Winnebago Deal
text: They played their first gig in early 1999 and fired the bass player a few months later, with Ben Thomas switching from guitar to bass.

title: Winnebago Deal
text: By the summer of 2000, Perrier and Thomas' dissatisfaction with their drummer led to his departure, with Thomas switching from bass to drums so the band could continue as a two-piece.

title: Winnebago Deal
text: Winnebago Deal now consists of two Bens, Ben Perrier (vocals, guitar) and Ben Thomas (drums).

title: Zachary Throne
text: Zachary Throne (born April 3, 1967 in Hollywood, California) is an American actor and musician who has appeared in a wide number of television, film and stage productions and on numerous rock, pop and soundtrack albums.

title: Zachary Throne
text: Throne is a self-taught, musician who sings, plays guitar, bass, drums, and piano – and is self-taught on all instruments.

title: Zachary Throne
text: He is the son of Malachi Throne and Judith Merians and is the brother of Joshua Throne.

title: Zachary Throne
text: He earned a Gold record in 1992 for his work on the soundtrack album to the television series "The Heights", on which he performed guitars, bass, piano and vocals as well as co-starred in the series.

title: Zachary Throne
text: The album yielded a hit single, "How Do You Talk To An Angel" (on which Zachary performed on) that was #1 on "Billboard" for two weeks in November 1992.

title: Zachary Throne
text: As an actor, Zachary is best known for playing the recurring role of "Howard", the radio station manager/drug dealer on "Beverly Hills 90210" and for playing "Danny" on the FOX series, "Party Of Five".

title: Zachary Throne
text: As a singer, Zachary has sung on many TV and radio jingles.

title: Zachary Throne
text: He provided the singing voice for the character, "Mark Winkle" on the television series, "California Dreams" as well as the singing voice for the character, "Greg Brady" in the films, "The Brady Bunch Movie" and "A Very Brady Sequel".

title: Zachary Throne
text: Currently, he resides in Las Vegas, Nevada where he performs in many shows.

title: Zachary Throne
text: From 2012-2014, he was the lead singer/lead guitar player/bass player for the Sin City Sinners, a group that also featured former Faster Pussycat guitarist and co-founder Brent Muscat as well as Slash bass player, Todd Kerns.

title: Zachary Throne
text: With the group, he recorded two albums, "DIVEBAR Days Revisited" and "A Sinners Christmas 2", both released in 2013.

title: Even Steven Levee
text: Even Steven Levee born Steven Louis Levee, is an American musician, bass player, recording engineer, record producer and former nightclub concert promoter.

title: Even Steven Levee
text: He is best known for his work with such bands as Lifeforce, ZRS, Brad Factor:10, The Slashtones, The Freak Parade, and his production work with Hedi, Barbara Lee George, MC Magic D and Gun Hill.

title: Even Steven Levee
text: As a bass player he is known for his diversity, playing with rock, funk, jazz, blues and hip hop artists, and for his use of various fretted and fretless four, five and six string bass guitars.

title: Even Steven Levee
text: He is also well known within the music industry for hosting premier "all star" jam sessions at various nightclubs in the New York area during the 1990s.

title: Even Steven Levee
text: Even has appeared on HBO and "Late Night with Conan O'Brien" during the current century and continues to work in Music and the Information Technology field.

title: Supagroup
text: Supagroup is an American rock and roll band from New Orleans, Louisiana.

title: Supagroup
text: Their current lineup includes vocalist and rhythm guitarist Chris Lee, lead guitarist Benji Lee, bassist Brewer Brian Broussard, and drummer Leon Touzet.

title: Supagroup
text: Chris Lee is married to former White Zombie bassist Sean Yseult.

title: Supagroup
text: In early 2003, the band won the New Orleans regional poll in The 2nd Annual Independent Music Awards for their song "She's Hot (I'm On A Roll)".

title: New Bolton Center
text: New Bolton Center is the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine’s 700 acre campus in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania.

title: New Bolton Center
text: It is home to one of the busiest large animal teaching veterinary clinics in the nation.

title: New Bolton Center
text: Since 1958, it has been located at the former South Brook Farm.

title: New Bolton Center
text: Founded in 1964 with contributions from equestrienne Esther du Pont Thouron and others, each year the George D. Widener Hospital for Large Animals (named for horseman George D. Widener, Jr.) sees more than 4,000 patient visits, and its Field Service sees more than 31,000 patient visits.

title: New Bolton Center
text: In addition to its role as one of the nation’s finest equine surgical facilities, New Bolton Center encompasses hospital facilities for the care of large animals and livestock as well as diagnostic laboratories serving the agriculture industry and the monitoring of emerging infectious disease.

title: New Bolton Center
text: Prior to the opening of "New" Bolton Center in 1952, the old Bolton Mansion in Levittown was the site of the farm for the School of Veterinary Medicine.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: Brenda McCowan is a research behaviorist interested in evolutionary, biological, and ecological aspects of animal behavior and communication.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: Her work focuses on improving the health and welfare of domesticated production animals, captive species (zoo, laboratory), and wildlife using applied animal behavior and bioacoustics.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: She received her BS in Animal Physiology from Cornell University in 1985, and her PhD in Biological Anthropology from Harvard University in 1994.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: Dr. McCowan is the Program Head of Primate Behavioral Management at California National Primate Research Center, a position she has held since 2004.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: Dr. McCowan has been on the faculty at the University of California – Davis since 1999, and is currently an Associate Adjunct Professor in the Department of Population Health and Reproduction at the UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: She also heads the McCowan Lab of Behavioral Management at UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine.

title: Brenda McCowan
text: Dr. McCowan is also affiliated with the Alaska Whale Foundation, SETI Institute, Hubbs-Sea World Institute, and Santa Fe Institute.

title: Supporting Healthy Marriage Project
text: The Supporting Healthy Marriage Project (SHM) is part of the Healthy Marriage Initiative funded by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families, that was launched in 2003 as "the first large-scale, multisite, multiyear, rigorous test of marriage education programs for low-income married couples".

title: Supporting Healthy Marriage Project
text: The project is motivated by research that "indicates that married adults and children raised by both parents in stable, low-conflict households do better on a host of outcomes".

title: Supporting Healthy Marriage Project
text: The evaluation is led by MDRC, in collaboration with Abt Associates and other partners.

title: Supporting Healthy Marriage Project
text: USASpending.gov reports payments of more than $30 million from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to MDRC for work on the Supporting Healthy Marriage Project from 2009 to 2012.

title: Melarsomine
text: Melarsomine (melaminylthioarsenate) is a trypanocidal agent.

title: Melarsomine
text: In the U.S., it is marketed under the trade names "Immiticide" (Merial) and "Diroban" (Zoetis), and is approved by the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine for the treatment of adult heartworm ("Dirofilaria immitis") infection in dogs.

title: Melarsomine
text: It is not approved for treatment in cats, or dogs in late-stage infection.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::0
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: The Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc. (CPACS) is 501(c)(3), private, nonprofit human services organization in metropolitan Atlanta, headquartered in northern DeKalb County, Georgia, United States of America.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::1
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: The organization was founded in 1980 and provides broad services for American citizens and non-citizens of all race, ethnicity, and national origin.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::2
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: The organization's primary services include community health, social services, housing, senior services, translation and interpretation, transportation services, education and enrichment programs for children, youth, and families, community education, legal and immigration assistance, counseling, advocacy, and research.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::3
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: CPACS's core objective is to help immigrants and refugees achieve the American Dream.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::4
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: The center operates the CPACS Cosmo Health Center, a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that serves populations with limited access to health care.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::5
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: Since 2005, the organization has held the Tea Walk, a two-mile empowerment walk along the Buford Highway Corridor to celebrate community diversity and promote civic engagement.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::6
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: CPACS is a member of the Association of Asian Pacific Community Health Organizations (AAPCHO), which is part of the National Council of Asian Pacific Americans.

chunk_id: 5ac547525542993e66e822a3::Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.::7
title: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
text: CPACS is one of the first and largest Asian American and Pacific Islander human services agencies in the Southeastern United States.

title: Ontario Veterinary College
text: The Ontario Veterinary College (OVC) is the oldest veterinary school in Canada.

title: Ontario Veterinary College
text: It is located on the campus of the University of Guelph in Guelph, Ontario.

title: Ontario Veterinary College
text: The OVC is one of five veterinary schools that offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, DVM program in Canada.

title: Ontario Veterinary College
text: The OVC was ranked 1st in Canada and 4th in the world for veterinary medicine by the QS World University Rankings 2015.

title: Food and Drug Administration
text: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or USFDA) is a federal agency of the United States Department of Health and Human Services, one of the United States federal executive departments.

title: Food and Drug Administration
text: The FDA is responsible for protecting and promoting public health through the control and supervision of food safety, tobacco products, dietary supplements, prescription and over-the-counter pharmaceutical drugs (medications), vaccines, biopharmaceuticals, blood transfusions, medical devices, electromagnetic radiation emitting devices (ERED), cosmetics, animal foods & feed and veterinary products.

title: Food and Drug Administration
text: As of 2017, 3/4th of the FDA budget (approximately $700 million) is funded by the pharmaceutical companies due to the Prescription Drug User Fee Act.

title: Oyewale Tomori
text: Tomori was born in Ilesa, Osun State, Nigeria on 3 February 1946.

title: Oyewale Tomori
text: He received a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine(DVM) from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria as well as a Doctorate degree, Ph.D in virology from the University of Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria where he was appointed professor of virology in 1981, the same year he received the United State of America Department of Health and Human Services Public Health Service Certificate for contributions to Lassa Fever Research.

title: Oyewale Tomori
text: Three years (1984) after his appointment as a professor of virology, he was appointed the head of the Department of Virology.

title: Oyewale Tomori
text: At the University of Ibadan Tomori's research interest focuses on viral infections including Ebola Hemorrhagic Fever, Yellow Fever, Lassa Fever.

title: Oyewale Tomori
text: He served as the Regional Virologist for the World Health Organization Africa Region ( 1994-2004) before he was appointed as the pioneer vice chancellor of Redeemer's University, Ogun State, Nigeria, a tenure that ended in 2011.

title: United States Public Health Service
text: The Public Health Service Act of 1944 structured the United States Public Health Service (PHS), founded in 1798, as the primary division of the U.S. Department of Health, Education and Welfare (HEW; which was established in 1953), which later became the United States Department of Health and Human Services in 1979–1980 (when the Education agencies were separated into their own U.S. Department of Education).

title: United States Public Health Service
text: The Office of the Surgeon General was created in 1871.

title: United States Public Health Service
text: The PHS comprises all Agency Divisions of Health and Human Services and the Commissioned Corps.

title: United States Public Health Service
text: The Assistant Secretary for Health (ASH) oversees the PHS and the United States Public Health Service Commissioned Corps.

title: Western University of Health Sciences
text: Western University of Health Sciences (WesternU) is a private, non-profit, graduate school for the health professions, with a main campus located on 22 acre in downtown Pomona, California, and an additional medical school campus on 50 acres in Lebanon, Oregon.

title: Western University of Health Sciences
text: WesternU offers degrees in osteopathic medicine, dental medicine, optometry, podiatric medicine, nursing, physician assistant studies, physical therapy, pharmacy, biomedical sciences, and veterinary medicine.

title: Western University of Health Sciences
text: With an enrollment of 3,839 students (2016–17), WesternU is one of the largest graduate schools for the health professions in California, offering 21 academic programs in nine colleges.

title: Western University of Health Sciences
text: The university also operates two patient care centers, and has a pet wellness center on its Pomona campus.

title: Western University of Health Sciences
text: The WesternU Pomona campus is also home to the Center for Oral Health (a non-profit organization focusing on promoting oral health), the Southern California Museum of Medical History, and the Harris Family Center for Disability and Health Policy.

title: Cinizasaurus
text: "Cinizasaurus" is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Mexico that were initially interpreted as belonging to a theropod dinosaur.

title: Cinizasaurus
text: The remains, NMMNH P-18400, consist of a tibia, vertebrae, and fragments, and came from the ?

title: Cinizasaurus
text: late Carnian-age Upper Triassic Bluewater Creek Member of the Chinle Formation, near Fort Wingate.

title: Cinizasaurus
text: Andrew Heckert, in his unpublished thesis, proposed the name "Cinizasaurus hunti" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was first referred to in the scientific literature in a 2007 redescription of Late Triassic North American material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Parker, 2007).

title: Cinizasaurus
text: In the redescription, the authors could only assign the material to Archosauriformes.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: Sphaerotholus is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of the western United States and Canada.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: To date, three species have been described: the type species, "S. goodwini", from the Den-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation (Late Campanian) of San Juan County, New Mexico, USA; "S. buchholtzae", from the Hell Creek Formation (Late Maastrichtian) of western Carter County, Montana, USA; and "S. edmontonense", from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: The etymology of "Sphaerotholus" is a combination of the Greek "sphaira", meaning "ball", and "tholos", meaning "dome", and is a reference to the characteristically dome-shaped pachycephalosaurian skull.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: The survival of "Sphaerotholus" from the Campanian of New Mexico to the end of the Maastrichtian of Montana demonstrates that this taxon had both a relatively long duration (approximately 7-8 million years) and a widespread distribution.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: Williamson and Carr, who first described the genus in 2002, diagnose it as follows: "Differs from all other pachycephalosaurids where known in the possession of a parietosquamosal bar that decreases in depth laterally as seen in caudal view and is bordered by a single row of nodes and one lateroventral corner node."

title: Sphaerotholus
text: "Sphaerotholus" is considered a highly derived pachycephalosaur.

title: Oryctodromeus
text: Oryctodromeus (meaning "digging runner") was a genus of small ornithopod dinosaur.

title: Oryctodromeus
text: Fossils are known from the middle Cretaceous Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, USA, both of the Cenomanian stage, roughly 95 million years ago.

title: Oryctodromeus
text: A member of the small, presumably fast-running herbivorous family Thescelosauridae, "Oryctodromeus" is the first dinosaur published that shows evidence of burrowing behavior.

title: Cryptoraptor
text: "Cryptoraptor" (meaning "secret thief") is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Mexico that were initially interpreted as belonging to a dinosaur.

title: Cryptoraptor
text: The remains, NMMNH P-17375, consist of a fragmentary skeleton including vertebrae, a pubis, and parts of the thigh bones.

title: Cryptoraptor
text: This specimen came from the Norian-age Upper Triassic Bull Canyon Formation in Quay County.

title: Cryptoraptor
text: Adrian Hunt, in his unpublished dissertation, proposed the name "Cryptoraptor lockleyi" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was first referred to in the scientific literature in a 2007 redescription of Late Triassic North American material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Parker, 2007).

title: Cryptoraptor
text: In the redescription, the authors could only assign the material to Archosauria.

title: Comanchesaurus
text: "Comanchesaurus" is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Mexico that were initially interpreted as belonging to a theropod dinosaur.

title: Comanchesaurus
text: The remains, NMMNH P-4569, consist of a partial skeleton including vertebral centra and hindlimb bones, and came from the Norian-age Upper Triassic Bull Canyon Formation of Guadalupe County.

title: Comanchesaurus
text: Adrian Hunt, in his unpublished dissertation, proposed the name "Comanchesaurus kuesi" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was first referred to in the scientific literature in a 2007 redescription of Late Triassic North American material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Parker, 2007).

title: Comanchesaurus
text: In the redescription, the authors found the material to belong to a "possible indeterminate saurischian".

title: McFarland, USA
text: McFarland, USA (also known as McFarland) is a 2015 American sports drama film directed by Niki Caro, produced by Mark Ciardi and Gordon Gray, written by Christopher Cleveland, Bettina Gilois and Grant Thompson with music composed by Antônio Pinto.

title: McFarland, USA
text: The film was co-produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Mayhem Pictures.

title: McFarland, USA
text: Based on the true story of a 1987 cross country team from a mainly Latino high school in McFarland, California, the film stars Kevin Costner as Jim White, the school's coach, who leads the team to win a state championship.

title: McFarland, USA
text: The film also stars Maria Bello and Morgan Saylor.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: Mark Thomas Ciardi (born August 19, 1961; pronounced CHAR-dee) is an American film producer and former Major League Baseball pitcher.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: He is currently the Founder & CEO of Apex Entertainment.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: Mark has a rich breadth of experience as a Film Executive, and Producer.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: Apex Entertainment is an independent content production firm that also serves as a financier for media properties.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: Prior to Apex, Mark was the co-founder of Mayhem Pictures that had an overall first look deal with Walt Disney Studios for twelve years.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: At Mayhem, Ciardi produced films including "The Rookie", "Miracle", Invincible, The Game Plan, Secretariat, and Million Dollar Arm and Kevin Costner's McFarland USA.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: Awaiting release is the worldwide best-selling novel, Fallen.

title: Mark Ciardi
text: He also produced the Emmy Award winning, ESPN 30 for 30 documentary titled "Big Shot".

title: Dinosaur (film)
text: Dinosaur is a 2000 American CGI animated adventure film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation and The Secret Lab and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

title: Dinosaur (film)
text: It is the 39th Disney animated feature film and Disney's The Secret Lab computer animated feature, though it is not officially labeled as one of the animated classics in the United Kingdom, where "The Wild" (2006) is included in the canon instead.

title: Fruitadens
text: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur.

title: Fruitadens
text: The name means "Fruita tooth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado (USA), where its fossils were first found.

title: Fruitadens
text: It is known from partial skulls and skeletons from at least four individuals of differing biological ages, found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado.

title: Fruitadens
text: "Fruitadens" is the smallest known ornithischian dinosaur, with young adults estimated at 65 to in length and 0.5 to in weight.

title: Fruitadens
text: It is interpreted as an omnivore and represents one of the latest-surviving heterodontosaurids.

title: Dakotadon
text: Dakotadon is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur from the Barremian-age Lower Cretaceous Lakota Formation of South Dakota, USA, known from a partial skull.

title: Dakotadon
text: It was first described in 1989 as "Iguanodon lakotaensis", by David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork.

title: Dakotadon
text: Its assignment has been controversial.

title: Dakotadon
text: Some researchers suggest that ""I." lakotaensis" was more basal than "I. bernissartensis", and related to "Theiophytalia", but David Norman has suggested that it was a synonym of "I. bernissartensis".

title: Dakotadon
text: Gregory S. Paul, working on a revision of iguanodont species, gave "I." "lakotaensis" its own genus ("Dakotadon") in 2008.

title: John S. Burke Catholic High School
text: John S. Burke Catholic High School, referred to locally as Burke Catholic, is a private, Roman Catholic high school in Goshen, New York and is located within the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York.

title: John S. Burke Catholic High School
text: Burke Catholic is the only Catholic high school located in Orange County.

title: John S. Burke Catholic High School
text: The school's colors are blue and white, with their sports teams, the Burke Catholic Eagles, carrying on those colors.

title: John S. Burke Catholic High School
text: Occasionally, silver is added to the school's colors.

title: John S. Burke Catholic High School
text: The school motto is "Non Vox Sed Votum", Latin for "Not Words But Deeds".

title: Spalding Catholic High School
text: Spalding Catholic High School was a private, Roman Catholic high school in Granville, Iowa.

title: Spalding Catholic High School
text: It is located in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Sioux City.

title: Spalding Catholic High School
text: The high school closed at the end of the 2013 school year and unified into Gehlen Catholic High School in LeMars, Iowa.

title: Spalding Catholic High School
text: Spalding Catholic School is now a PreK through 6th grade system.

title: St. Petersburg Catholic High School
text: St. Petersburg Catholic High School is a private, co-educational Roman Catholic high school in St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: St. Petersburg Catholic High School
text: It is located in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Saint Petersburg.

title: St. Petersburg Catholic High School
text: The campus was originally opened in February 1957 as Bishop Barry High School for boys.

title: St. Petersburg Catholic High School
text: In 1973, Bishop Barry High School and the nearby Notre Dame Academy for girls merged to become St. Petersburg Catholic High School.

title: St. Petersburg Catholic High School
text: (A decade earlier, St. Paul's High School for girls was merged into Notre Dame Academy.)

title: Bishop Carroll Catholic High School
text: Bishop Carroll Catholic High School is a private high school located in Wichita, Kansas, United States.

title: Bishop Carroll Catholic High School
text: Along with Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School, it is one of two Catholic high schools in the city, part of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Wichita.

title: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School
text: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School, sometimes called Kapaun, is a private, four year, co-educational, secondary school operated by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Wichita.

title: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School
text: It is located in the east side of Wichita, Kansas.

title: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School
text: The school colors are blue and white.

title: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School
text: The average annual enrollment is approximately 850 students.

title: Monroe Catholic High School
text: Monroe Catholic High School is a private, Roman Catholic high school in Fairbanks, Alaska.

title: Monroe Catholic High School
text: It is the only Catholic high school in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Fairbanks.

title: Monroe Catholic High School
text: It is the northernmost Roman Catholic high school in the Americas.

title: Bishop Manogue High School
text: Bishop Manogue Catholic High School is a Catholic high school in Reno, Nevada.

title: Bishop Manogue High School
text: It is the only Catholic high school in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Reno and one of only two Catholic high schools in the state of Nevada.

title: Carmel High School (Mundelein, Illinois)
text: Carmel Catholic High School is a co-educational, college preparatory, Catholic high school run jointly by the priests and brothers of the Order of Carmelites and the Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

title: Carmel High School (Mundelein, Illinois)
text: Located in Mundelein, Illinois, Carmel serves all of Lake County, as well as some of the surrounding counties, and southern Wisconsin.

title: Carmel High School (Mundelein, Illinois)
text: An institution of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago, Carmel Catholic is one of three Carmelite-run high schools in the Chicago area, the others being Joliet Catholic High School and Mount Carmel High School.

title: Fremont School District 79
text: Fremont School District 79 is a school district located in Mundelein, Illinois, and it is composed of Fremont Elementary School, Fremont Intermediate School, and Fremont Middle School.

title: Fremont School District 79
text: Fremont Middle School, the one in which the students of the most seniority attend, 16% feed into Adlai E. Stevenson High School in Lincolnshire, Illinois.

title: Fremont School District 79
text: Seventy-nine percent of the students feed into Mundelein High School in Mundelein, Illinois, and the other 5% of the students either will go to Grayslake Central High School in Grayslake, Illinois or Carmel Catholic High School in Mundelein, Illinois .

title: Fremont School District 79
text: The current superintendent is Dr. Bill Robertson, with the principals of Fremont Elementary School, Fremont Intermediate School, and Fremont Middle School being Stefan Ladenburger (both elementary and intermediate) and Pamela Motsenbocker.

title: Bishop Sullivan Catholic High School
text: Bishop Sullivan Catholic High School (from 1949 to 1993, Norfolk Catholic High School; from 1993-2004, Catholic High School; commonly referred to as "Catholic" or "CHS") is a Roman Catholic secondary school in Virginia Beach, Virginia, founded as Norfolk Catholic High School in 1949 and moved to Virginia Beach in 1993.

title: Bishop Sullivan Catholic High School
text: In 2003, the school was renamed in honor of Walter Francis Sullivan, Bishop Emeritus of the Diocese of Richmond and a significant benefactor during the school's move to Virginia Beach.

title: Bishop Sullivan Catholic High School

title: Bishop Sullivan Catholic High School

title: United States presidential election, 1976
text: The United States presidential election of 1976 was the 48th quadrennial presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 2, 1976.

title: United States presidential election, 1976
text: The winner was the Dark horse candidate Jimmy Carter, a former Governor from Georgia with his running mate, Walter Mondale, a U.S. Senator from Minnesota, the Democratic candidates, over the incumbent President Gerald Ford from Michigan and his running mate, Bob Dole, a U.S. Senator from Kansas, the Republican candidates.

title: United States presidential election, 2016
text: The United States presidential election of 2016 was the 58th quadrennial American presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 8, 2016.

title: United States presidential election, 2016
text: In a surprise victory, the Republican ticket of businessman Donald Trump and Indiana Governor Mike Pence defeated the Democratic ticket of former First Lady, U.S. Senator of New York and Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and U.S. Senator from Virginia Tim Kaine.

title: United States presidential election, 2016
text: Trump took office as the 45th President, and Pence as the 48th Vice President, on January 20, 2017.

title: United States presidential election, 2016
text: Concurrent with the presidential election, Senate, House, and many gubernatorial and state and local elections were also held on November 8.

title: United States presidential election, 2012
text: The United States presidential election of 2012 was the 57th quadrennial American presidential election.

title: United States presidential election, 2012
text: It was held on Tuesday, November 6, 2012.

title: United States presidential election, 2012
text: The Democratic nominee, incumbent President Barack Obama, and his running mate, Vice President Joe Biden, were elected to a second term, defeating the Republican nominee, former Governor of Massachusetts Mitt Romney and his running mate, Representative and future House Speaker Paul Ryan of Wisconsin.

title: 2044 election
text: The United States presidential election of 2044, scheduled for Tuesday, November 8, 2044, will be the 65th quadrennial U.S. presidential election.

title: 2044 election
text: Voters will select presidential electors who in turn will either elect a new president and vice president through the electoral college or re-elect the incumbents.

title: 2044 election
text: The series of presidential primary elections and caucuses are likely to be held during the first six months of 2044.

title: 2044 election
text: This nominating process is also an indirect election, where voters cast ballots selecting a slate of delegates to a political party's nominating convention, who then in turn elect their party's presidential nominee.

title: Michigan Democratic primary, 2016
text: The 2016 Michigan Democratic primary took place on March 8 in the U.S. state of Michigan as one of the Democratic Party's primaries ahead of the 2016 presidential election.

text: The United States presidential election of 2020, scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, 2020, will be the 59th quadrennial U.S. presidential election.

title: United States presidential election, 2020

title: United States presidential election, 1968
text: The United States presidential election of 1968 was the 46th quadrennial presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 5, 1968.

title: United States presidential election, 1968
text: The Republican nominee, former Vice President Richard Nixon, won the election over the Democratic nominee, incumbent Vice President Hubert Humphrey.

title: United States presidential election, 1968
text: Analysts have argued the election of 1968 was a major realigning election as it permanently disrupted the New Deal Coalition that had dominated presidential politics for 36 years.

title: United States presidential election, 1960
text: The United States presidential election of 1960 was the 44th quadrennial presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 8, 1960.

title: United States presidential election, 1960
text: The Republican Party nominated incumbent Vice President Richard Nixon, while the Democratic Party nominated John F. Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Massachusetts.

title: United States presidential election, 1960
text: The incumbent President, Republican Dwight D. Eisenhower, was not eligible for re-election after being elected the maximum two times allowed by the Twenty-second Amendment; he was the first President denied the choice to run for a third term by that amendment.

title: United States presidential election, 1960
text: This was the first presidential election in which residents in Alaska and Hawaii were able to participate, as both had become states in 1959.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: The United States presidential election of 1964 was the 45th quadrennial presidential election.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: It was held on Tuesday, November 3, 1964.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: Democratic candidate and incumbent President Lyndon B. Johnson had come to office less than a year earlier following the assassination of his predecessor John F. Kennedy.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: Johnson, who had successfully associated himself with Kennedy’s popularity, won 61.1% of the popular vote, the highest win by a candidate since James Monroe’s re-election in 1820.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: It was the most lopsided US presidential election in terms of popular votes, and the tenth-most lopsided presidential election in the history of the United States in terms of electoral votes.

title: United States presidential election, 1964
text: No candidate for president since has equalled or surpassed Johnson’s percentage of the popular vote, and since 1820, only Abraham Lincoln in 1864, Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1936, Richard Nixon in 1972 and Ronald Reagan in 1980 and 1984 have won by a greater electoral vote margin.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: The United States presidential election of 1892 was the 27th quadrennial presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 8, 1892.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: It witnessed a re-match of the closely contested presidential election in 1888.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: Former Democratic President Grover Cleveland and incumbent Republican President Benjamin Harrison both ran for election to a second term.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: In 1888, Cleveland won the popular vote over Harrison, but lost in the electoral college.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: In a re-match, Cleveland won both the popular and electoral vote, thus becoming the first and to date only person in American history to be elected to a second, non-consecutive presidential term.

title: United States presidential election, 1892
text: The new Populist Party, formed by groups from The Grange, the Farmers' Alliances, and the Knights of Labor, also fielded a ticket; they polled best in the West, winning in five states and taking a total of 22 electoral votes.

title: Romano-British culture
text: Romano-British culture is the culture that arose in Britain under the Roman Empire following the Roman conquest in AD 43 and the creation of the province of Britannia.

title: Romano-British culture
text: It arose as a fusion of the imported Roman culture with that of the indigenous Britons, a people of Celtic language and custom.

title: Romano-British culture
text: It survived the 5th century Roman departure from Britain.

title: Romano-British culture
text: Scholars such as Christopher Snyder believe that during the 5th and 6th centuries – approximately from AD 410 when the Roman legions withdrew, to AD 597 when St Augustine of Canterbury arrived – southern Britain preserved an active sub-Roman culture that survived the attacks from the Anglo-Saxons and even used a vernacular Latin when writing.

title: History of Wales
text: The history of Wales begins with the arrival of human beings in the region thousands of years ago.

title: History of Wales
text: Neanderthals lived in what is now Wales, or "Cymru" in Welsh, at least 230,000 years ago, while "Homo sapiens" arrived by about 31,000 BC.

title: History of Wales
text: However, continuous habitation by modern humans dates from the period after the end of the last ice age around 9000 BC, and Wales has many remains from the Mesolithic, Neolithic, and Bronze Age.

title: History of Wales
text: During the Iron Age the region, like all of Britain south of the Firth of Forth, was dominated by the Celtic Britons and the Brittonic language.

title: History of Wales
text: The Romans, who began their conquest of Britain in AD 43, first campaigned in what is now northeast Wales in 48 against the Deceangli, and gained total control of the region with their defeat of the Ordovices in 79.

title: History of Wales
text: The Romans departed from Britain in the 5th century, opening the door for the Anglo-Saxon invasion.

title: History of Wales
text: Thereafter Brittonic language and culture began to splinter, and several distinct groups formed.

title: History of Wales
text: The Welsh people were the largest of these groups, and are generally discussed independently of the other surviving Brittonic-speaking peoples after the 11th century.

title: Durotriges
text: The Durotriges were one of the Celtic tribes living in Britain prior to the Roman invasion.

title: Durotriges
text: The tribe lived in modern Dorset, south Wiltshire, south Somerset and Devon east of the River Axe and the discovery of an Iron Age hoard in 2009 at Shalfleet, Isle of Wight gives evidence that they lived in the western half of the island.

title: Durotriges
text: After the Roman conquest, their main "civitates", or settlement-centred administrative units, were Durnovaria (modern Dorchester, "the probable original capital") and Lindinis (modern Ilchester, "whose former, unknown status was thereby enhanced").

title: Durotriges
text: Their territory was bordered to the west by the Dumnonii; and to the east by the Belgae.

title: Corieltauvi
text: The Corieltauvi (formerly thought to be called the Coritani, and sometimes referred to as the Corieltavi) were a tribe of people living in Britain prior to the Roman conquest, and thereafter a "civitas" of Roman Britain.

title: Corieltauvi
text: Their territory was in what is now the English East Midlands.

title: Corieltauvi
text: They were bordered by the Brigantes to the north, the Cornovii to the west, the Dobunni and Catuvellauni to the south, and the Iceni to the east.

title: Corieltauvi
text: Their capital was called "Ratae Corieltauvorum", known today as Leicester.

title: AD 43
text: AD 43 (XLIII) was a common year starting on Tuesday (link will display the full calendar) of the Julian calendar.

title: AD 43
text: At the time, it was known as the Year of the Consulship of Caesar and Vitellius (or, less frequently, year 796 "Ab urbe condita").

title: AD 43
text: The denomination AD 43 for this year has been used since the early medieval period, when the Anno Domini calendar era became the prevalent method in Europe for naming years.

title: Togodumnus
text: Togodumnus (d. AD 43) was a historical king of the British Catuvellauni tribe at the time of the Roman conquest.

title: Togodumnus
text: He can probably be identified with the legendary British king Guiderius.

title: Roman conquest of Britain
text: The Roman conquest of Britain was a gradual process, beginning effectively in AD 43 under Emperor Claudius, whose general Aulus Plautius served as first governor of Roman Britain (Latin: "Britannia" ).

title: Roman conquest of Britain
text: Great Britain had already frequently been the target of invasions, planned and actual, by forces of the Roman Republic and Roman Empire.

title: Roman conquest of Britain
text: In common with other regions on the edge of the empire, Britain had enjoyed diplomatic and trading links with the Romans in the century since Julius Caesar's expeditions in 55 and 54 BC, and Roman economic and cultural influence was a significant part of the British late pre-Roman Iron Age, especially in the south.

title: Sussex chicken
text: The Sussex chicken is a dual purpose breed of chicken that originated in England around the time of the Roman conquest of Britain in AD 43 that is a popular garden chicken in many countries.

title: Sussex chicken
text: They come in eight colours (with a couple more being developed) and have a bantam version at 1/4 size; the bantams may be any of the eight colours.

title: Catuvellauni
text: The Catuvellauni were a Celtic tribe or state of southeastern Britain before the Roman conquest, attested by inscriptions into the 4th century.

title: History of England
text: England became inhabited more than 800,000 years ago, as the discovery of flint tools and footprints at Happisburgh in Norfolk has revealed.

title: History of England
text: The earliest evidence for early modern humans in North West Europe, a jawbone discovered in Devon at Kents Cavern in 1927, was re-dated in 2011 to between 41,000 and 44,000 years old.

title: History of England
text: Continuous human habitation in England dates to around 13,000 years ago (see Creswellian), at the end of the last glacial period.

title: History of England
text: The region has numerous remains from the Mesolithic, Neolithic, and Bronze Age, such as Stonehenge and Avebury.

title: History of England
text: In the Iron Age, England, like all of Britain south of the Firth of Forth, was inhabited by the Celtic people known as the Britons, including some Belgic tribes (e.g. the Atrebates, the Catuvellauni, the Trinovantes, etc.) in the south east.

title: History of England
text: In AD 43 the Roman conquest of Britain began; the Romans maintained control of their province of Britannia until the early 5th century.

title: "Q" Is for Quarry

text: The books feature Hannah Scarlett and the historian Daniel Kind, and are the first series of crime novels by a British detective novelist to be set in the Lake District, a region in North-West England.

text: June Thomson (also known as June Valerie Thomson), (born 1930, in Rettendon, Essex, United Kingdom) is a detective novelist.

title: Sue Grafton
text: She is best known as the author of the 'alphabet series' (""A" Is for Alibi", etc.) featuring private investigator Kinsey Millhone in the fictional city of Santa Teresa, California.

title: Sue Grafton
text: The daughter of detective novelist C. W. Grafton, she has said the strongest influence on her crime novels is author Ross Macdonald.

title: Sue Grafton

title: Andy Straka
text: Andy Straka is a Shamus Award-winning American crime novelist.

title: Andy Straka
text: Born and raised in upstate New York and a graduate of Williams College, he worked in publishing and medical sales for nearly fifteen years before turning to writing in the late 1990s.

title: Andy Straka
text: His debut private-eye novel, "A Witness Above", garnered Shamus, Anthony, and Agatha Award nominations for "Best First Novel" in 2002.

title: Andy Straka
text: "A Killing Sky" received an Anthony Award nomination in 2003, and Straka's third book, "Cold Quarry", won a 2004 Shamus Award.

title: Andy Straka
text: His series of six Frank Pavlicek novels features a former New York City police detective who also spends much of his time flying various hawks to help inspire him to solve criminal cases.

title: Andy Straka
text: The fourth novel in the Pavlicek series, "Kitty Hitter", was called a "great read" by Library Journal.

title: Andy Straka
text: "Kitty Hitter" was re-released with a new title, "The Night Falconer", as an e-book and paperback.

title: Andy Straka
text: A fifth book featuring Pavlicek is the novella "Flightfall".

title: Andy Straka
text: Another full-length novel, "The K Street Hunting Society", was released as book 6 in the Pavlicek series in 2014.

title: C. Hugh Holman

title: C. Hugh Holman
text: He was a Professor of English at the University of North Carolina Chapel Hill and its Provost from 1966 to 1968.

title: C. Hugh Holman
text: He was the vice president of the National Humanities Center.

title: C. Hugh Holman
text: He was the author of many books about Southern literature, and the founding co-editor of the "Southern Literary Journal".

title: C. Hugh Holman
text: He was the recipient of several awards.

title: Rupaye Dus Karod
text: Rupaye Dus Karod is a 1991 Indian Bollywood suspense thriller film directed by Sikander Bharti and produced by Waman K. Dehsmukh and written by Shabdh Kumar.

title: Rupaye Dus Karod
text: The film was made in the style of formula-based potboilers and was a hit.

title: Rupaye Dus Karod
text: It stars Rajesh Khanna in the lead role and supporting cast includes Chunky Pandey, Amrita Singh, Sonu Walia, Avinash Wadhavan, Deepika Chikhalia, Sadashiv Amrapurkar, Kiran Kumar in pivotal roles.

text: Rupaye Dus Karod (ten crores of rupees) is the story of a detective novelist (writing in Hindi) - Ravi Varma (Rajesh Khanna) whose father had to flee from India in his childhood itself because of a conspiracy masterminded by his wicked business partners and later Ravi finds himself in mystery murder and another plot to have tried to earn 10 crore by fraudulent means .

title: Rubislaw quarry
text: Rubislaw Quarry was opened in 1740 and is located at the Hill of Rubislaw in the west end of the Scottish city of Aberdeen.

title: Rubislaw quarry
text: In 1778/9, Aberdeen City Council sold it to a businessman for £13, as it was not thought to be a source of good building material.

title: Rubislaw quarry
text: However, over the next 200 years, an estimated six million tonnes of granite were excavated from the quarry, giving Aberdeen the name of 'The Granite City'.

title: Rubislaw quarry
text: Rubislaw Quarry is one of the biggest man-made holes in Europe.

title: He Who Whispers
text: He Who Whispers is a mystery novel (1946) by detective novelist John Dickson Carr.

title: He Who Whispers
text: Like Many of the works by this author feature so-called impossible crimes (for the most part, falling into the category of the locked room mystery).

title: He Who Whispers
text: In this case, the novel falls into a smaller category of Carr's work in that it is suggested that the crime is the work of a supernatural being (here, a vampire).

title: He Who Whispers
text: The detective is Dr. Gideon Fell, who ultimately uncovers a rational explanation for the novel's events.

title: He Who Whispers
text: Carr considered this one of his best impossible crime novels.

title: The Crooked Hinge
text: The Crooked Hinge is a mystery novel (1938) by detective novelist John Dickson Carr.

title: The Crooked Hinge
text: It combines a seemingly impossible throat-slashing with elements of witchcraft, an automaton modelled on Maelzel's Chess Player, and the story of the Tichborne Claimant.

title: The Crooked Hinge
text: It was dedicated to fellow author Dorothy Sayers "in friendship and esteem."

title: Nesting (voting districts)
text: "Nesting" is the delimitation of voting districts for one elected body in order to define the voting districts for another body.

title: Nesting (voting districts)
text: For example, in California, the State Assembly (the lower house) is composed of 80 members, each one representing 1/80th of California's population, and the State Senate (the upper house) is composed of 40 members, each one representing 1/40th of California's population.

title: Nesting (voting districts)
text: In this case, the process of nesting could either be first defining the 80 Assembly districts, and then defining the Senate districts as a merge of two Assembly districts, or first defining the 40 Senate districts, and then creating the Assembly districts by splitting each Senate district into two.

title: Nesting (voting districts)
text: If the Assembly districts and the Senate districts are created independently of each other, then the process of nesting is not used.

text: New York's 1st State Senate district is one of 62 districts of the New York State Senate.

title: New York's 1st State Senate district

title: California State Senate
text: The California State Senate is the upper house of the California State Legislature.

title: California State Senate
text: Due to the state's large population and relatively small legislature, the State Senate has the largest population per representative ratio of any state legislative house.

title: California State Senate
text: In the United States House of Representatives, California is apportioned 53 representatives, each representing approximately 704,566 people, while in the State Senate, each of the 40 Senators represents approximately 931,349 people, with the result that California state senators each actually represent more voters than California's representatives to the United States Congress do.

title: California State Senate
text: Each member roughly represents a population equivalent to the state of Delaware.

title: California State Senate
text: As a result of Proposition 140 in 1990 and Proposition 28 in 2012, members elected to the legislature prior to 2012 are restricted by term limits to two four-year terms (eight years), while those elected in or after 2012 are allowed to serve 12 years in the legislature in any combination of four-year state senate or two-year state assembly terms.

title: New York's 3rd State Senate district

title: New York's 3rd State Senate district

title: Steven Bradford

title: Steven Bradford

title: Steven Bradford
text: Prior to his election to the state senate, he was an assemblymember for the 62nd district of the California State Assembly.

title: Steven Bradford
text: Bradford was elected to represent the 51st district in a special election held on September 1, 2009, after Curren Price resigned his seat to take a seat in the California State Senate.

title: Steven Bradford

title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins

title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins

title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins

title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The Hawaiʻi State Senate is the upper chamber of the Hawaii State Legislature.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The senate consists of twenty-five members elected from an equal number of constituent districts across the islands.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The senate is led by the President of the Senate, elected from the membership of the body, currently Ron Kouchi.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The forerunner of the Hawaii State Senate during the government of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻ i was the House of Nobles originated in 1840.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: In 1894 the Constitution of the Republic of Hawaii renamed the upper house the present senate.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: Senators are elected to four-year terms and are not subject to term limits.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: Like most state legislatures in the United States, the Hawaii State Senate is a part-time body and senators often have active careers outside government.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The lower chamber of the legislature is the Hawaiʻi House of Representatives.

title: Hawaii Senate
text: The membership of the Senate also elects additional officers to include the Senate Vice President, Senate Chief Clerk, Assistant Chief Clerk, Senate Sergeant at Arms and Assistant Sergeant at Arms.

title: New York's 4th State Senate district

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia
text: Ellenbrook, and its neighbouring suburbs of The Vines and Aveley, are unusual for Perth in being a significant distance from neighbouring suburbs.

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia
text: Given this relative isolation and the distance from the CBD, Ellenbrook has been designed and developed as a self-sustainable community.

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia

title: Ellenbrook, Western Australia

title: Pakistan Air Force
text: The Pakistan Air Force (PAF) (Urdu: ‎ —"Pāk Fizāʾiyah" , , reporting name: PAF) is the aerial warfare branch of the Pakistan Armed Forces, tasked primarily with the aerial defence of Pakistan, with a secondary role of providing air support to the Pakistan Army and the Pakistan Navy.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: The United Negro College Fund, also known as UNCF or the United Fund, is an American philanthropic organization that funds scholarships for black students and general scholarship funds for 37 private historically black colleges and universities.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: UNCF was incorporated on April 25, 1944 by Frederick D. Patterson (then president of what is now Tuskegee University), Mary McLeod Bethune, and others.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: UNCF is headquartered at 1805 7th Street, NW in Washington, D.C.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: In 2005, UNCF supported approximately 65,000 students at over 900 colleges and universities with approximately $113 million in grants and scholarships.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: About 60% of these students are the first in their families to attend college, and 62% have annual family incomes of less than $25,000.

title: United Negro College Fund
text: UNCF also administers over 450 named scholarships.

title: Karaboro languages

title: Karaboro languages

title: Karaboro languages
text: Within Senufo they are thought to be most closely related to the Senari languages.

title: Hanna Varis
text: Hanna Leena Kristiina Varis (b. 1959 in Kuusankoski) is a Finnish graphic artist and painter.

title: Hanna Varis
text: She earned a Master of Arts degree from the Aalto University School of Arts, Design and Architecture in 1990.

title: Hanna Varis

title: Hanna Varis
text: She has held over 70 solo exhibitions and participated at over 140 group exhibitions.

title: Hanna Varis
text: Her works are part of major art collections in Finland and abroad, such as the Kiasma, Amos Anderson Art Museum, and Helsinki Art Museum in Helsinki, Wäinö Aaltonen Museum of Art in Turku, and Albertina Museum in Vienna.

text: The Albertina is a museum in the Innere Stadt (First District) of Vienna, Austria.

title: Albertina

title: Albertina

title: Albertina
text: The museum also houses temporary exhibitions.

title: Gwangjang Market
text: Gwangjang Market, previously Dongdaemun Market, is a traditional street market in Jongno-gu, Seoul, South Korea.

title: Gwangjang Market

title: German language
text: German ("Deutsch" ] ) is a West Germanic language that is mainly spoken in Central Europe.

title: German language
text: It is the most widely spoken and (co-) official language in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, South Tyrol (Italy), the German-speaking Community of Belgium, and Liechtenstein.

title: German language
text: It is also one of the three official languages of Luxembourg.

title: German language
text: The languages which are most similar to German are the other members of the West Germanic language branch: Afrikaans, Dutch, English, the Frisian languages, Low German/Low Saxon, Luxembourgish, and Yiddish.

title: German language
text: German is the second most widely spoken Germanic language, after English.

title: English language
text: English is a West Germanic language that was first spoken in early medieval England and is now a global "lingua franca".

title: English language
text: Named after the Angles, one of the Germanic tribes that migrated to England, it ultimately derives its name from the Anglia (Angeln) peninsula in the Baltic Sea.

title: English language
text: It is closely related to the Frisian languages, but its vocabulary has been significantly influenced by other Germanic languages, particularly Norse (a North Germanic language), as well as by Latin and Romance languages, particularly French.

title: Proto-Norse language
text: Proto-Norse (also called Proto-Scandinavian, Primitive Norse, Proto-Nordic, Ancient Nordic, Ancient Scandinavian, Old Nordic, Old Scandinavian, Proto-North Germanic, North Proto-Germanic or Common Scandinavian) was an Indo-European language spoken in Scandinavia that is thought to have evolved as a northern dialect of Proto-Germanic in the first centuries CE.

title: Proto-Norse language
text: It is the earliest stage of a characteristically North Germanic language, and the language attested in the oldest Scandinavian Elder Futhark inscriptions, spoken around from the 2nd to 8th centuries (corresponding to the late Roman Iron Age and the Germanic Iron Age).

title: Proto-Norse language
text: It evolved into the dialects of Old Norse at the beginning of the Viking Age in about 800, which later themselves evolved into modern North Germanic languages.

title: Dutch language
text: Dutch ( ) is a West Germanic language that is spoken by around 24 million people as a first language—including the population of the Netherlands and about sixty percent that of Belgium—and by another 5 million as a second language.

title: Dutch language
text: It is the third most widely spoken Germanic language, after English and German.

title: Old Frisian
text: Old Frisian is a West Germanic language spoken between the 8th and 16th centuries in the area between the Rhine and Weser on the European North Sea coast.

title: Old Frisian
text: The Frisian settlers on the coast of South Jutland (today's Northern Friesland) also spoke Old Frisian but no medieval texts of this area are known.

title: Old Frisian
text: The language of the earlier inhabitants of the region between the Zuiderzee and Ems River (the Frisians mentioned by Tacitus) is attested in only a few personal names and place-names.

title: Old Frisian
text: Old Frisian evolved into Middle Frisian, spoken from the 16th to the 19th century.

title: Afrikaans
text: Afrikaans ( ) is a West Germanic language spoken in South Africa, Namibia and, to a lesser extent, Botswana and Zimbabwe.

title: Afrikaans
text: It evolved from the Dutch vernacular of South Holland (Hollandic dialect) spoken by the mainly Dutch settlers of what is now South Africa, where it gradually began to develop distinguishing characteristics in the course of the 18th century.

title: Afrikaans
text: Hence, it is a daughter language of Dutch, and was previously referred to as "Cape Dutch" (a term also used to refer collectively to the early Cape settlers) or "kitchen Dutch" (a derogatory term used to refer to Afrikaans in its earlier days).

title: Afrikaans
text: However, it is also variously described as a creole or as a partially creolised language.

title: Afrikaans
text: The term is ultimately derived from Dutch "Afrikaans-Hollands " meaning "African Dutch".

title: Afrikaans
text: It is the first language of most of the Afrikaners and Coloureds of Southern Africa.

title: Leer
text: Leer is a town in the district of Leer, the northwestern part of Lower Saxony, Germany.

title: Leer
text: It is situated on the river Leda, a tributary of the river Ems, near the border with the Netherlands.

title: Suorva
text: Suorva or Suorvadammen (the Suorva Dam) is a small settlement situated at the southern parts of Akkajaure, in Stora Sjöfallet National Park, Sweden.

title: Suorva
text: The settlement can be reached by car (and bus, from Gällivare).

title: Suorva

title: Suorva

title: Old Saxon
text: Old Saxon, also known as Old Low German, was a Germanic language and the earliest recorded form of Low German (spoken nowadays in Northern Germany, the northeastern Netherlands, southern Denmark, the Americas and parts of Eastern Europe).

title: Old Saxon
text: It is a West Germanic language, closely related to the Anglo-Frisian languages.

title: Old Saxon
text: It has been documented from the 8th century until the 12th century, when it gradually evolved into Middle Low German.

title: Old Saxon
text: It was spoken throughout modern northwestern Germany, primarily in the coastal regions and in the eastern Netherlands by Saxons, a Germanic tribe who inhabited the region of Saxony.

title: Old Saxon
text: It partially shares Anglo-Frisian's (Old Frisian, Old English) Ingvaeonic nasal spirant law which sets it apart from Low Franconian and Irminonic languages, such as Dutch, Luxembourgish and German.

title: Leda (river)
text: The Leda is a river in north-western Germany in the state of Lower Saxony.

title: Leda (river)
text: It is a right tributary of the Ems and originates at the confluence of the Sagter Ems and the Soeste (Dreyschloot) near the town of Barßel.

title: Leda (river)
text: The Leda flows into the Ems near the town of Leer.

title: Leda (river)
text: On the southern bank of the Leda, in the "Overledingen Land" (Overledingen="country over the Leda"), opposite Leer, lies the small settlement of Kloster Muhde ("Muhde" from the Old Frisian "mutha" meaning "(river) mouth").

title: Leda (river)
text: The total length of the river is 29 km , of which the lower 1.9 km are navigable for sea-going vessels.

title: British people
text: British people, or Britons, are the citizens of the United Kingdom, British Overseas Territories, and Crown dependencies.

title: Randall Cunningham
text: Randall Wade Cunningham (born March 27, 1963) is a former American football quarterback in the National Football League (NFL).

text: He played in the NFL for 16 seasons, primarily with the Philadelphia Eagles.

title: Randall Cunningham
text: Cunningham is also known for his tenure with the Minnesota Vikings.

text: He is the younger brother of former college and professional football player Sam Cunningham and the father of Randall Cunningham II and world champion high jumper Vashti Cunningham.

title: David Masur
text: Masur graduated from Columbia High School in 1980.

title: David Masur
text: He was a multi-sport athlete at Columbia, playing on the basketball and lacrosse team.

title: David Masur
text: He had his greatest success as a three-year starter on the Columbia soccer team, winning the Group IV state championship his junior and senior seasons.

title: David Masur
text: He was a Parade All-American and New Jersey State Player of the Year.

title: David Masur
text: In May 2006, Masur was elected to the Columbia High School Hall of Fame.

title: David Masur
text: In 1979, the New York Cosmos drafted Masur out of high school, but he elected to attend Rutgers University where he played on the men's soccer team from 1981 to 1984.

title: David Masur
text: He was the team's 1982 and 1983 MVP, and served as team captain from 1982 to 1984.

title: David Masur
text: Masur made the All-Regional team as a sweeper from 1982 to 1984.

title: David Masur

title: David Masur

title: Ken Rose (gridiron football)

title: Ken Rose (gridiron football)

title: Ken Rose (gridiron football)

title: Sharon Gannon
text: Sharon Gannon (born July 4, 1951 in Washington, D.C.) is a yoga teacher, animal rights advocate, musician, author, dancer/choreographer and painter.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: Along with David Life, she is the co-founder of the Jivamukti Yoga Method which contributed to the exponential rise in popularity of yoga in the west during the late 20th century.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: The Jivamukti Yoga Method distinguishes itself as a path to enlightenment by promoting compassion for all beings, challenging the modern belief that enslaving and exploiting animals and the natural world is our right as the dominant species.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: The Jivamukti Yoga Method teaches its students that they must be willing to promote the happiness of all beings without exception if they wish to realize their fullest capacity for joy.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: Jivamukti students are encouraged to adopt a diet that eliminates all animal products (vegan) as this is the diet that causes the least amount of harm to the earth and other beings, humans included.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: Core to the teachings of Jivamukti Yoga is the concept of shunyata or (emptiness) which is found in the ancient yogic scriptures.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: This idea can be simply stated as: everything you see and experience in the world comes from your perception of it.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: If you want to change someone or to change the world, you start by changing yourself by changing your views.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: When you begin to embrace this concept and put it into practice then you cannot find solace in complaining or blaming others.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: You are freed from seeing yourself as a victim of others or of circumstances.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: According to Gannon: "How you treat others will determine how others treat you.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: How others treat you will determine how you see yourself.

title: Sharon Gannon
text: How you see yourself will determine who you are."

title: See Yourself
text: "See Yourself" is a song by English musician George Harrison, released on his 1976 album "Thirty Three & 1/3".

title: See Yourself
text: Harrison began writing the song in 1967, while he was a member of the Beatles, in response to the public outcry surrounding bandmate Paul McCartney's admission that he had taken the hallucinogenic drug LSD.

title: See Yourself
text: McCartney's announcement created a reaction in the press similar to that caused in 1966 by John Lennon's statement that the Beatles were more popular than Christianity.

title: See Yourself
text: In its finished form, the song's lyrics advocate self-awareness and consideration for the consequences of one's actions.

title: See Yourself
text: Musically, the composition contains unusual shifts in time signature from standard 4/4 to 9/8, while the songwords reflect the era of its genesis by recalling themes first espoused in the Beatles tracks "Within You Without You" and "All You Need Is Love".

title: No Plan (EP)
text: No Plan is an extended play, comprising songs written and recorded by English musician David Bowie, released posthumously on 8 January 2017.

title: No Plan (EP)
text: The release coincided with what would have been Bowie's 70th birthday, almost a year after his death.

title: No Plan (EP)
text: "No Plan" compiles the original songs written for Bowie's Broadway musical, "Lazarus", including the titular "Lazarus", "No Plan", "Killing a Little Time", and "When I Met You".

title: No Plan (EP)
text: The songs were first recorded by the cast of the musical as part of its official soundtrack.

title: No Plan (EP)
text: The recordings featured on "No Plan" come from the sessions for Bowie's twenty-fifth and final studio album "Blackstar", with "Lazarus" appearing as the third track on the album.

title: No Plan (EP)
text: Upon release, "No Plan" debuted at #138 on the "Billboard" 200.

title: No Plan (EP)
text: The music video for the title track was also released in accompaniment with the EP.

title: No Plan (EP)

title: We Laughed
text: "We Laughed" is a three-track single by English musician Billy Bragg as part of the Rosetta Life project.

title: We Laughed
text: The single was released in 2005 in the UK and peaked at No. 11.

title: We Laughed
text: It also reached No. 38 in Ireland in 2006.

title: We Laughed
text: For the three songs on the single, Bragg collaborated with three patients of Trimar Hospice in Weymouth, who each wrote lyrics based on their illness and feelings.

title: We Laughed
text: The songs were produced by English guitarist Robbie McIntosh.

title: Who Can See It
text: "Who Can See It" is a song by English musician George Harrison, released on his 1973 album "Living in the Material World".

title: Who Can See It
text: The lyrics reflect Harrison's uneasy feelings towards the Beatles' legacy, three years after the group's break-up, and serve as his statement of independence from expectations raised by the band's unprecedented popularity.

title: Who Can See It
text: Some music critics and biographers suggest that he wrote the song during a period of personal anguish, following the acclaim he had received as a solo artist with the 1970 triple album "All Things Must Pass" and his 1971–72 Bangladesh aid project.

title: Who Can See It
text: The revelatory nature of the lyrics has encouraged comparisons between "Living in the Material World" and John Lennon's primal therapy-inspired 1970 release, "Plastic Ono Band".
5:55 is the second album by French musician and actress Charlotte Gainsbourg.
It is also her first album release in twenty years.
Charlotte collaborated on the album with French duo Air, English musician Jarvis Cocker, and Irish singer-songwriter Neil Hannon, as well as Radiohead's main producer Nigel Godrich.
"The Songs That We Sing" and "5:55" were released as singles.
The album went platinum in France, selling over 500,000 copies.
In the United States, the album sold a modest 22,000 copies.
"The Songs That We Sing" was #78 on "Rolling Stone"' s list of the 100 Best Songs of 2007.

title: Gem Archer
text: Colin Murray "Gem" Archer (born 7 December 1966) is an English musician, best known as a member of the English rock bands Oasis, Beady Eye and Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds.

title: Gem Archer
text: He is also known for his work with Heavy Stereo.

title: Gem Archer
text: He joined Oasis as rhythm guitarist in November 1999, and handled lead guitar for acoustic songs as well.

title: Gem Archer
text: He also contributed to the writing of some of the band's songs.

title: Gem Archer
text: Oasis broke up in August 2009, but in November 2009, Liam Gallagher announced he was writing new material with Archer as well as other ex-Oasis members minus his brother Noel, under the name Beady Eye.

title: Gem Archer
text: After two albums with Beady Eye, 2011's "Different Gear, Still Speeding" and 2013's "BE", the band officially disbanded in October 2014.

title: Gem Archer

title: Within You Without You
text: "Within You Without You" is a song written by George Harrison and released on the Beatles' 1967 album "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band".

title: Within You Without You
text: It was Harrison's second composition in the Indian classical style, after "Love You To", and was inspired by his six-week stay in India with his mentor and sitar teacher, Ravi Shankar, over September–October 1966.

title: Within You Without You
text: Recorded in London without the other Beatles, the song features Indian instrumentation such as sitar, dilruba and tabla, and was performed by Harrison and members of the Asian Music Circle.

title: Within You Without You
text: The recording marked a significant departure from the Beatles' previous work; musically, it evokes the Indian devotional tradition, while the overtly spiritual quality of the lyrics reflects Harrison's absorption in Hindu philosophy and the teachings of the Vedas.

title: Within You Without You
text: Although the song was his only composition on "Sgt. Pepper", Harrison's endorsement of Indian culture was further reflected in the inclusion of yogis such as Paramahansa Yogananda among the crowd depicted on the album cover.

title: Ryan Johansen
text: Ryan Johansen (born July 31, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre, an alternate captain for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL).

title: Ryan Johansen

title: Ryan Johansen
text: In 2009–10, he moved to the major junior level with the Portland Winterhawks of the Western Hockey League (WHL).

title: Ryan Johansen
text: After his first WHL season, he was selected fourth overall by the Blue Jackets in the 2010 NHL Entry Draft.

title: Ryan Johansen
text: Internationally, he has competed for the Canadian national junior team at the 2011 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships, where he earned a silver medal and was named to the Tournament All-Star Team.

title: Ryan Johansen
text: In 2015, he participated in the 2015 NHL Skills Competition and was named the 2015 NHL All-Star Game MVP.

title: 60th National Hockey League All-Star Game

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: The Stanley Cup is a trophy awarded annually to the playoff champion club of the National Hockey League (NHL) ice hockey league.

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: It was donated by the Governor General of Canada Lord Stanley of Preston in 1892, and is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America.

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: Inscribed the "Dominion Hockey Challenge Cup", the trophy was first awarded to Canada's amateur ice hockey clubs who won the trophy as the result of challenge games and league play.

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: Professional clubs came to dominate the competition in the early years of the twentieth century, and in 1913 the two major professional ice hockey organizations, the National Hockey Association (NHA) (forerunner of the NHL) and the Pacific Coast Hockey Association (PCHA), reached a gentlemen's agreement in which their respective champions would face each other in an annual series for the Stanley Cup.

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: After a series of league mergers and folds, it became the "de facto" championship trophy of the NHL in 1926, though it was nominally still subject to external challenge.

title: List of Stanley Cup champions
text: After 1947, the Cup became the "de jure" NHL championship prize.

title: Fred Doherty
text: Frederick "Doc" Doherty (June 15, 1887 – February 12, 1961) was a Canadian professional ice hockey player.

title: Fred Doherty

title: Fred Doherty

title: Fred Doherty
text: After returning from World War I duty, he played one game in the National Hockey League with the Montreal Canadiens to end his career.

title: Fred Doherty
text: He played on several league champions, leading to play in several Stanley Cup championships, but was not a member of a Stanley Cup-winning team.
