title: Travis Richards
text: Travis John Richards (born March 22, 1970) is a former professional ice hockey defenseman.

title: Travis Richards
text: Richards graduated from Robbinsdale Armstrong High School in Plymouth, Minnesota in 1988.

title: Travis Richards
text: Richards was a member of the University of Minnesota Gophers hockey program before making his professional debut during the 1993-94 season.

title: Travis Richards
text: A child psychology major, Richards would spend four years at the University of Minnesota where his brother Todd was a Gopher from 1985 to 1989.

title: Travis Richards
text: Earning WCHA Second Team All-Star honors on defense in 1992 and in 1993, Richards would join the US National Team at the 1993 World Championships at the end of his senior year.

title: Travis Richards
text: Drafted by the Minnesota North Stars of the National Hockey League in the ninth round (169th overall) of the 1988 NHL Entry Draft, Richards played only three games in the NHL for the Dallas Stars .

title: Travis Richards
text: On July 26, 1996, Richards became the second player ever to sign with the Grand Rapids Griffins, then of the International Hockey League, now of the American Hockey League.

title: Travis Richards
text: Richards played in each of the team's first ten seasons and became team captain in 2001.

title: Travis Richards
text: He holds the record for most career games as a Griffin with 655.

title: Travis Richards

title: Travis Richards

title: Travis Richards

title: Rebel Highway
text: Rebel Highway was a short-lived revival of American International Pictures created and produced by Lou Arkoff, the son of Samuel Z. Arkoff and Debra Hill for the Showtime channel in 1994.

title: Rebel Highway
text: The concept was 10-week series of 1950s "drive-in classic" B-movies remade "with a '90s edge".

title: Rebel Highway
text: The impetus for the series, according to Arkoff was, "what it would be like if you made "Rebel Without a Cause" today.

title: Rebel Highway
text: It would be more lurid, sexier, and much more dangerous, and you definitely would have had Natalie Wood's top off".

title: Rebel Highway
text: Originally, Arkoff wanted to call the series, "Raging Hormones" but Showtime decided on "Rebel Highway" instead.

title: Rebel Highway
text: Arkoff and Hill invited several directors to pick a title from one of Samuel Arkoff's movies, hire their own writers and create a story that could resemble the original if they wanted.

title: Rebel Highway
text: In addition, they had the right to a final cut and select their own director of photography and the editor.

title: Rebel Highway
text: Each director was given a $1.3 million budget and 12 days to shoot it with a cast of young, up and coming actors and actresses.

title: Rebel Highway
text: According to Arkoff, the appeal to directors was that, "They weren't hampered by big studios saying, 'You can't do this or that.'

title: Rebel Highway
text: And all the directors paid very close attention to the detail of the era.

title: Rebel Highway
text: We want these shows to be fun for the younger generation and fun for the older generation".

title: Asthma-related microbes

title: Asthma-related microbes

title: Asthma-related microbes

title: Asthma-related microbes
text: These viral respiratory infections are mostly caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human rhinovirus (HRV).

title: Asthma-related microbes
text: Although RSV infections increase the risk of asthma in early childhood, the association between asthma and RSV decreases with increasing age.

title: Asthma-related microbes
text: HRV on the other hand is an important cause of bronchiolitis and is strongly associated with asthma development.

title: Asthma-related microbes

title: Asthma-related microbes

title: Duty to settle
text: A liability insurance company's duty to settle is defined as an implied obligation to by the insurer to a policyholder and to a claimant to attempt "in good faith to effectuate prompt, fair, and equitable settlements of claims in which liability has become reasonably clear."

title: Duty to settle
text: To the surprise of many, a typical liability insurance policy makes no express contractual promise to settle.

title: Duty to settle
text: In California, "an insurer, who wrongfully refuses to accept a reasonable settlement within the policy limits is liable for the entire judgment against the insured even if it exceeds the policy limits."

title: Duty to settle
text: A rationale for this duty is that "[w]hen an offer is made to settle a claim in excess of policy limits for an amount within policy limits, a genuine and immediate conflict of interest arises between carrier and assured."

title: Duty to settle
text: "An insurer who denies coverage does so at its own risk.

title: Duty to settle
text: Such factors as a belief that the policy does not provide coverage, should not affect a decision as to whether the settlement offer in question is a reasonable one."

title: Duty to settle
text: "It is the duty of the insurer to keep the insured informed of settlement offers." "

title: Duty to settle
text: [A]n insurer potentially can be liable for unreasonably coercing an insured to contribute to a settlement fund."

title: Cyclone Donna
text: Severe Tropical Cyclone Donna was the strongest off-season South Pacific tropical cyclone on record during the month of May.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: The twenty-first tropical disturbance, third named storm, and second severe tropical cyclone of the annual cyclone season, Donna formed from an area of disturbed weather that was first monitored west-northwest of Fiji on 1 May 2017.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: The disturbance drifted eastward amid an increasingly favorable environment, and it was designated Tropical Depression 21F late on 2 May.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: Twelve hours later, it intensified into a Category 1 on the Australian tropical cyclone scale and was designated Tropical Cyclone Donna as the storm's motion shifted west and then south.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: After reaching its initial peak as a Category 4 cyclone early on 6 May, the effects of wind shear and upwelling caused the storm to weaken.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: However, it reintensified into a Category 5 cyclone on 8 May.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: Soon after, Donna entered a region of strong westerly flow and began to rapidly weaken.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: Continuing to accelerate in a southerly direction, Donna eventually weakened into a tropical low on 10 May.

title: Cyclone Donna
text: By 16 May, Donna's remnants had fully dissipated.

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: The 1999 Odisha cyclone (IMD designation BOB 03, JTWC designation 05B) was the strongest recorded tropical cyclone in the North Indian Ocean and among the most destructive in the region.

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: The 1999 Odisha cyclone organized into a tropical depression in the Andaman Sea on 25 October, though its origins could be traced back to an area of storms in the Sulu Sea four days prior.

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: The disturbance gradually strengthened as it took a west-northwesterly path, reaching cyclonic storm strength the next day.

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: Taking advantage of highly favorable conditions, the storm rapidly intensified, attaining super cyclonic storm intensity on 28 October before peaking with winds of 260 km/h (160 mph) and a record-low pressure of 912 mbar (hPa; 26.93 inHg).

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: The storm maintained this intensity as it made landfall on Odisha on 29 October.

title: 1999 Odisha cyclone
text: The cyclone steadily weakened due to persistent land interaction and dry air, remaining quasi-stationary for two days before slowly drifting offshore as a much weaker system; the storm dissipated on 1 November over the Bay of Bengal.

title: Cyclone Anne

title: Cyclone Anne

title: Cyclone Anne
text: Over the next few days, the system gradually developed while moving southwestward.

title: Cyclone Anne
text: Once it became a tropical cyclone, it was named Anne on January 8.

title: Cyclone Anne
text: The next day, Anne rapidly intensified, becoming the fourth major tropical cyclone to affect Vanuatu within four years.

title: Cyclone Anne
text: On January 11, Anne peaked in intensity while it was equivalent to a Category 5 on the Saffir–Simpson hurricane wind scale, and a Category 4 on the Australian tropical cyclone intensity scale.

title: Cyclone Anne
text: After turning southward on January 12, Anne struck New Caledonia, becoming the strongest tropical cyclone to affect the French Overseas Territory.

title: Cyclone Anne
text: The system subsequently weakened as it started to interact with Tropical Cyclone Agi.

title: Cyclone Anne

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: Intense Tropical Cyclone Hondo (JTWC designation: 16S) was the strongest and longest lived tropical cyclone to develop during the 2007–08 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: The third tropical cyclone and first intense tropical cyclone of the season, Hondo developed out of a tropical disturbance in early February about 1,020 km (635 mi) east-southeast of Diego Garcia.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: The disturbance quickly strengthened, becoming a moderate tropical storm on February 4 and a severe tropical storm the following day.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: After a brief period of slower intensification, Hondo rapidly intensified into an intense tropical cyclone and reached its peak intensity with winds of 215 km/h (130 mph ) on February 7.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: The cyclone gradually weakened over the next several days due to an increase in forward speed and a decrease in sea surface temperatures.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: On February 12, Hondo rapidly degenerated into a remnant-low pressure area.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: Over the following week, the remnant low traveled in a general west-northwest direction with no development.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: On February 20, about 2,780 km (1,725 mi) northeast of where the final advisories were issued, the storm began to regenerate.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: The next day, advisories were issued on Tropical Disturbance Ex-Hondo, which briefly strengthened into a tropical depression.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: However, according to the Joint Typhoon Warning Center, Hondo continued to strengthen and attained winds of 95 km/h (60 mph ) before passing directly over Réunion.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: Interaction with the island caused the storm to weaken and degenerate into a remnant low once more.

title: Cyclone Hondo
text: The storm dissipated on February 29 after executing a counterclockwise loop.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: The 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season included Cyclone Inigo, which tied Cyclone Gwenda in 1999 as the most intense tropical cyclone on record in the Australian basin.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: It began on 1 November 2002 and ended on 30 April 2003.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: The regional tropical cyclone operational plan also defines a "tropical cyclone year" separately from a "tropical cyclone season", which runs from 1 July 2002 to 30 June 2003.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: These dates conventionally delimit the period of each year when most tropical cyclones form in the Australian region, which is defined as in the southern hemisphere between 90°E and 180°E.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: The season's ten tropical depressions existed within these dates, with the first, designated as Tropical Cyclone 07S, entering the basin on 27 December 2002.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: The last system, Cyclone Epi, dissipated on 6 June 2003.

title: 2002–03 Australian region cyclone season
text: Tropical cyclones in this area were monitored by four Tropical Cyclone Warning Centres (TCWCs): the Australian Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) in Perth, Darwin, and Brisbane and one in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.

title: Cyclone Gonu
text: Super Cyclonic Storm Gonu (also simply known as Cyclone Gonu) is the strongest tropical cyclone on record in the Arabian Sea, and is also the strongest named cyclone in the northern Indian Ocean.

title: Cyclone Gonu
text: The second named tropical cyclone of the 2007 North Indian Ocean cyclone season, Gonu developed from a persistent area of convection in the eastern Arabian Sea on June 1, 2007.

title: Cyclone Gonu
text: With a favorable upper-level environment and warm sea surface temperatures, it rapidly intensified to attain peak winds of 235 km/h (145 mph) on June 4, according to the India Meteorological Department.

title: Cyclone Gonu
text: Gonu weakened after encountering dry air and cooler waters, and early on June 6, it made landfall on the easternmost tip of Oman, becoming the strongest tropical cyclone to hit the Arabian Peninsula.

title: Cyclone Gonu
text: It then turned northward into the Gulf of Oman, and dissipated on June 7 after making landfall in southern Iran, the first landfall in the country since 1898.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: Tropical Cyclone Kesiny was the first recorded tropical cyclone – the equivalent of a minimal hurricane – to make landfall in the month of May 2002 in the south-west Indian Ocean.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: The final named storm of the busy 2001–02 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season, Kesiny formed on May 2 from a trough near the equator.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: Its formation was the result of an increase in the Madden–Julian oscillation, which also contributed to a twin storm in the north Indian Ocean that hit Oman, and another set of storms in northeast and southeast Indian Ocean.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: Kesiny initially moved to the southeast, but later turned to the southwest due to a strengthening ridge.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: On May 6, it intensified into a tropical cyclone, but later weakened and was not expected to re-strengthen.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: However, Kesiny developed an eye and re-intensified into a tropical cyclone on May 9, reaching peak winds of 130 km/h before striking Madagascar about 60 km southeast of Antsiranana.

title: Cyclone Kesiny
text: It weakened while crossing the country, and after turning to the south it struck the country again before dissipating on May 11.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: Severe Tropical Cyclone Esau became the strongest tropical cyclone to affect New Caledonia on record during February and March 1992.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: A shallow tropical depression developed within the monsoon trough during 24 February, about 370 km (230 mi) to the northeast of Port Vila, Vanuatu.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: Over the next day the system gradually developed further as it moved towards the south-west under the influence of a northerly steering flow, before it passed over Pentecost Island in northern Vanuatu during 25 February.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: After passing over Pentecost the system continued to move towards the southwest and passed near the island of Malampa, before the depression turned northwards and executed a small clockwise loop as it passed over the island of Espiritu Santo.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: The system was subsequently named Esau during 26 February, after it had developed into a tropical cyclone.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: Over the next couple of days the system moved south-westwards towards Australia and away from the islands of Vanuatu.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: Esau subsequently executed a second clockwise loop during 28 February, before it peaked as a Category 4 tropical cyclone on both the Australian tropical cyclone intensity scale and the Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: After it had peaked the system moved south-eastwards and threatened Southern Vanuatu, before turning southwards and threatening the French overseas territory of New Caledonia.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: Esau made landfall on the French territory during 4 March, as a category 3 severe tropical cyclone before degenerating into an extratropical cyclone during 5 March.

title: Cyclone Esau
text: The systems remnants made landfall on New Zealand's North Island during 8 March, before they were last noted during the next day over the South Pacific Ocean.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: The 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season was one of the least active South Pacific tropical cyclone seasons on record, with only three tropical cyclones occurring during the season.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: The season ran from November 1, 2011 to April 30, 2012, however, any tropical cyclones that form before June 30, 2012 would have fallen within the 2011–12 tropical cyclone year and would have counted towards the season total.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: The strongest and only severe tropical cyclone that occurred during the season was Severe Tropical Cyclone Jasmine, which tracked in from out of the South Pacific basin.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: Within the basin, tropical cyclones are monitored by the Regional Specialized Meteorological Center (RSMC) in Nadi, Fiji, and the Tropical Cyclone Warning Center (TCWC) in Wellington, New Zealand.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: RSMC Nadi attaches an F designation to tropical disturbances that form in or move into the South Pacific.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: The United States Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) issues unofficial warnings within the South Pacific, designating tropical storm-equivalent or greater tropical cyclones with a number and a P suffix.

title: 2011–12 South Pacific cyclone season
text: RSMC Nadi and TCWC Wellington both use the Australian Tropical Cyclone Intensity Scale, and measure windspeeds over a period of ten minutes, while the JTWC measures sustained winds over a period of one minute and uses the Saffir–Simpson Hurricane Scale.

title: Whole life insurance
text: Whole life insurance, or whole of life assurance (in the Commonwealth of Nations), sometimes called "straight life" or "ordinary life," is a life insurance policy which is guaranteed to remain in force for the insured's entire lifetime, provided required premiums are paid, or to the maturity date.

title: Whole life insurance
text: As a life insurance policy it represents a contract between the insured and insurer that as long as the contract terms are met, the insurer will pay the death benefit of the policy to the policy's beneficiaries when the insured dies.

title: Whole life insurance
text: Because whole life policies are guaranteed to remain in force as long as the required premiums are paid, the premiums are typically much higher than those of term life insurance where the premium is fixed only for a limited term.

title: Whole life insurance
text: Whole life premiums are fixed, based on the age of issue, and usually do not increase with age.

title: Whole life insurance
text: The insured party normally pays premiums until death, except for limited pay policies which may be paid-up in 10 years, 20 years, or at age 65.

title: Whole life insurance
text: Whole life insurance belongs to the cash value category of life insurance, which also includes universal life, variable life, and endowment policies.

text: He was born in Paris, France, and educated at Eton College and at Balliol and Exeter Colleges, Oxford.

title: Douglas Ainslie
text: A contributor to the Yellow Book, he met and befriended Oscar Wilde at age twenty-one while an undergraduate at Oxford.

title: Douglas Ainslie
text: He was also associated with other such notable figures as Aubrey Beardsley, Walter Pater and Marcel Proust.

title: Douglas Ainslie
text: The first translator of the Italian philosopher Benedetto Croce into English, he also lectured on Hegel.

text: Lydia Vladimirovna Litvyak (Лидия Владимировна Литвяк, (August 18, 1921 in Moscow – August 1, 1943 in Krasnyi Luch), also known as Lilya, was a fighter pilot in the Soviet Air Force during World War II.

title: Lydia Litvyak
text: With twelve solo victories and four shared kills over a total of 66 combat missions, over about two years of missions, she was the first female fighter pilot to shoot down an enemy plane, the first of two female fighter pilots who have earned the title of fighter ace, and the holder of the record for the greatest number of kills by a female fighter pilot.

text: She was shot down near Orel during the Battle of Kursk as she attacked a formation of German planes.

text: Eino Ilmari "Illu" Juutilainen (21 February 1914 – 21 February 1999) was a fighter pilot of the Ilmavoimat (Finnish Air Force), and the top scoring non-German fighter pilot of all time.

title: Ilmari Juutilainen
text: This makes him the top flying ace of the Finnish Air Force, leading all Finnish pilots in score against Soviet aircraft in World War II (1939–40 and 1941–44), with 94 confirmed aerial combat victories in 437 sorties.

title: Manfred Meurer
text: Manfred Meurer (8 September 1919 – 22 January 1944) was a German fighter pilot during World War II.

title: Manfred Meurer
text: A flying ace, he claimed 65 aerial victories making him the fifth most successful night fighter pilot in the history of aerial warfare.

title: Manfred Meurer
text: All of his victories were claimed over the Western Front in Defense of the Reich missions against the Royal Air Force's (RAF) Bomber Command.

title: Paul Zorner
text: Paul Anton Guido Zorner, born Paul Zloch (31 March 1920 – 27 January 2014) was a German night fighter pilot, who fought in the "Luftwaffe" during World War II.

title: Paul Zorner
text: Zorner is credited with 59 night aerial victories claimed in 272 missions, including 110 night fighter missions.

title: Paul Zorner
text: Zorner was the ninth most successful fighter pilot in the "Luftwaffe" and in the history of aerial warfare.

title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
text: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag is an IMAX film centered on the experiences of a USAF F-15 Eagle fighter pilot, then-Captain John Stratton, who wants to be professionally successful as a fighter pilot.

title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
text: It chronicles his experience during USAF Red Flag training at Nellis AFB, a simulated air war designed to train pilots for combat.

title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
text: Directed by Stephen Low and presented by Boeing, the film shows how airmen simulate a war without killing one another, as well as the training of military air base firemen, military ordnance crews, midair refueling operations, cockpit views, and other aspects of aerial combat.

title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag

title: Albert Ball
text: At the time of his death he was the United Kingdom's leading flying ace, with 44 victories, and remained its fourth-highest scorer behind Edward Mannock, James McCudden, and George McElroy.

title: Ashley Rolfe
text: Ashley Rolfe is one of the United States Air Force female fighter pilots who qualified to fly McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.

title: Ashley Rolfe
text: As a member of the Massachusetts Air National Guard, she makes history at the 104th Fighter Wing as the first female fighter pilot in the wing’s 70-year history in Aug. 18, 2016.

title: Ashley Rolfe
text: She served in 67th Fighter Squadron at Kadena.

title: Ashley Rolfe

title: Ashley Rolfe

title: Ayesha Farooq

title: Ayesha Farooq
text: In 2013, she became first and only Pakistani and South Asian female fighter pilot after topping the final exams to qualify.

title: Ayesha Farooq
text: She now flies missions in a Chinese-made Chengdu J-7 fighter jet alongside her 24 male colleagues in Squadron 20.

title: Egon Mayer

title: Egon Mayer
text: He was credited with 102 enemy aircraft shot down in over 353 combat missions.

title: Egon Mayer

title: Egon Mayer

title: Duchy of Thuringia
text: The Duchy of Thuringia was an eastern frontier march of the Merovingian kingdom of Austrasia, established about 631 by King Dagobert I after his troops had been defeated by the forces of the Slavic confederation of Samo at the Battle of Wogastisburg.

title: Duchy of Thuringia
text: It was recreated in the Carolingian Empire and its dukes appointed by the king until it was absorbed by the Saxon dukes in 908.

title: Duchy of Thuringia
text: From about 1111/12 the territory was ruled by the Landgraves of Thuringia as Princes of the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Khosrow IV
text: Khosrow IV was a Sasanian usurper who ruled briefly in 631.

title: Khosrow IV
text: Little is known about his rule, he appears to have ruled during a time of upheaval and chaos across the Sasanian Empire the 7th century has the century where Iran has plunged into its "dark ages".

title: Khosrow IV
text: He was the son of Mah-Adhur Gushnasp, who was the minister of the Sasanian Empire during the reign of Ardashir III, and Kahar-dukht, the daughter of Yazdandar, who was the son of Khosrau I.

title: Khosrow IV
text: His rule seems to coincide with other pretenders such as Hormizd VI so it is likely that he ruled a district or province rather than the Empire in its entirety.

title: Khosrow IV
text: He was killed after a few days of reign.

title: Farrukhzad Khosrow V
text: Farrukhzad Khosrau V was briefly king of the Sasanian Empire from March 631 to April 631.

title: Farrukhzad Khosrow V
text: He was the son of Khosrau II.

title: Samo
text: Samo founded the first recorded political union of Slavic tribes, known as Samo's Empire ("realm", "kingdom", or "tribal union"), stretching from Silesia to present-day Slovenia, ruling from 623 until his death in 658.

title: Samo
text: According to Fredegarius, the only contemporary source, Samo was a Frankish merchant who unified several Slavic tribes against robber raids and violence by nearby settled Avars, showing such bravery and command skills in battle that he was elected as the "Slavic king" (Latin: "Rex Sclavorum" ).

title: Samo
text: In 631, Samo successfully defended his realm against the Frankish Kingdom in the three-day Battle of Wogastisburg.

title: Chach of Alor
text: Chach (c. 631-711 CE) (Sindhi: چچ‎ ) was a Brahmin who reigned as king of Sindh in the mid-7th century CE.

title: Chach of Alor
text: A former prime minister to the king Rai Sahasi II, Chach ascended to the throne by marrying the king's widow.

title: Chach of Alor
text: The Brahmin dynasty under Chach expanded the kingdom of Sindh, and his successful efforts to subjugate surrounding monarchies and ethnic groups into an empire covering the entire Indus valley and beyond were recorded in the "Chach Nama".

title: Ashur-etil-ilani
text: Ashur-etil-ilani was a king of Assyria (c. 631 BC – c. 627 BC).

title: Ashur-etil-ilani
text: He succeeded his father Ashurbanipal.

title: Suintila
text: Suintila, or "Swinthila", "Svinthila"; (ca. 588 – 633/635) was Visigothic King of Hispania, Septimania and Galicia from 621 to 631.

title: Suintila
text: There was a new peace in the Kingdom of the Visigoths.

title: Suintila
text: As a direct result, by 624 the king was able to retake those lands that had been under the control of the Byzantine Empire.

title: Suintila
text: He was a son of Reccared I and wife Bado, and a brother of the general Geila.

title: Samo's Empire
text: Samo's Empire is the historiographical name for the Slavic tribal union established by King ("rex") Samo, which existed between 631 and 658 A.D..

title: Samo's Empire
text: The centre of the union was most likely in Moravia, while the union included Silesia, Bohemia, Lusatia and Carantania.

title: Sasanian Empire
text: The Sasanian Empire ( or ), also known as the Sassanian, Sasanid, Sassanid or Neo-Persian Empire, known to its inhabitants as Ērānshahr in Middle Persian, was the last period of the Persian Empire (Iran) before the rise of Islam, named after the House of Sasan who ruled from 224 to 651 AD.

title: Sasanian Empire
text: The Sasanian Empire, which succeeded the Parthian Empire, was recognised as one of the leading world powers alongside its neighbouring arch-rival the Roman-Byzantine Empire, for a period of more than 400 years.

title: Hormizd VI

title: Tenskwatawa
text: Tenskwatawa (also called Tenskatawa, Tenskwatawah, Tensquatawa or Lalawethika) (January 1775 – November 1836) was a Native American religious and political leader of the Shawnee tribe, known as the Prophet or the Shawnee Prophet.

title: Tenskwatawa
text: He was a younger brother of Tecumseh, leader of the Shawnee.

title: Tenskwatawa
text: In his early years Tenskwatawa was given the name Lalawethika ("He Makes a Loud Noise" or "The Noise Maker"), but he changed it around 1805 and transformed himself from a hapless, alcoholic youth into an influential spiritual leader.

title: Tenskwatawa
text: Tenskwatawa denounced the Americans, calling them the offspring of the Evil Spirit, and lead a purification movement that promoted unity among the American Indians, rejected acculturation to the American way of life, and encouraged his followers to pursue traditional ways.

title: Tecumseh
text: Native American Shawnee warrior and chief, who became the primary leader of a large, multi-tribal confederacy in the early years of the nineteenth century.

title: Tecumseh
text: Born in the Ohio Country (present-day Ohio), and growing up during the American Revolutionary War and the Northwest Indian War, Tecumseh was exposed to warfare and envisioned the establishment of an independent Indian nation east of the Mississippi River under British protection and worked to recruit additional members to his tribal confederacy from the southern United States.

title: Tecumseh's Confederacy
text: Tecumseh's Confederacy was a group of Native Americans in the Old Northwest that began to form in the early 19th century around the teaching of Tenskwatawa (The Prophet).

title: Tecumseh's Confederacy
text: The confederation grew over several years and came to include several thousand warriors.

title: Tecumseh's Confederacy
