title: Kazan International Airport
text: Kazan Airport served nearly 3.8 million citizens of the region .

title: Pitt Meadows Airport
text: Pitt Meadows Airport (ICAO: CYPK) is a Canadian general aviation airport located in the southwest of corner of Pitt Meadows, British Columbia.

title: Pitt Meadows Airport
text: In 2016, it was the 17th busiest airport in Canada with 109,188 aircraft movements and is the 4th busiest airport in the Lower Mainland.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: Charlotte Douglas International Airport (IATA: CLT, ICAO: KCLT, FAA LID: CLT) is a joint civil-military public international airport located in Charlotte, North Carolina, United States.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: Established in 1935 as Charlotte Municipal Airport, in 1954 the airport was renamed Douglas Municipal Airport after former Charlotte mayor Ben Elbert Douglas, Sr. The airport gained its current name in 1982 and, as of September 2017, it is the second largest hub for American Airlines after Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, with service to 161 domestic and international destinations.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: As of 2016 it was the 5th busiest airport in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and aircraft movements.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: It was also the 7th business airport in the world ranked by aircraft movements Charlotte is the largest airport in the United States without any nonstop service to Asia.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: The airport serves as a major gateway to the Caribbean Islands.

title: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
text: CLT covers 5,558 acres (2,249 ha) of land.

title: Logan International Airport
text: Logan International Airport (IATA: BOS, ICAO: KBOS, FAA LID: BOS) , officially known as General Edward Lawrence Logan International Airport, is an international airport located in the East Boston neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, United States (and partly in the town of Winthrop, Massachusetts).

title: Logan International Airport
text: It covers 2384 acre , has six runways and four passenger terminals, and employs an estimated 16,000 people.

title: Logan International Airport
text: It is the largest airport in the New England region and 17th-busiest airport in the United States, with 33.5 million total passengers in 2015.

title: Logan International Airport
text: It is named after General Edward Lawrence Logan.

title: Logan International Airport
text: In 2016, Massport reported an 8.5% increase in passenger traffic comparing 2015 to 2016, giving the airport a total of about 36.3 million passengers.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: Coimbatore International Airport (IATA: CJB, ICAO: VOCB) is the primary airport serving the city of Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: It is located at Peelamedu, about 13 km from the center of the city.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: Previously known as Peelamedu Civil Aerodrome, it is the 19th busiest airport in India in terms of passengers handled, 16th busiest in terms of total aircraft movement and 14th busiest in terms of cargo handled.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: The airport is the second largest airport in terms of passenger traffic and cargo after Chennai International Airport In Tamil Nadu.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: About five domestic and three international airlines serve the airport.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: The Airport also serves as a growing hub for Cargo transportation.

title: Townsville Airport
text: Townsville Airport (IATA: TSV, ICAO: YBTL) is a major Australian regional airport that services the city of Townsville.

title: Townsville Airport
text: The airport is also known as Townsville International Airport, and Garbutt Airport, a reference to its location in the Townsville suburb of Garbutt.

title: Townsville Airport
text: Townsville Airport is serviced by major Australian domestic and regional airlines, and in 2011/12 handled 1.7 million passengers making it the 11th busiest airport in Australia.

title: American Airlines Shuttle
text: American Airlines Shuttle is the brand name for American Airlines' hourly air shuttle service operating in the Northeastern United States.

title: American Airlines Shuttle
text: It serves Logan International Airport in Boston, LaGuardia Airport in New York City, and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Washington, D.C.

title: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
text: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport (IATA: DLC, ICAO: ZYTL) is the airport serving the city of Dalian in Liaoning Province, China.

title: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
text: It is located in Ganjingzi District, about 10 km northwest of the city center.

title: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
text: In 2014 the airport handled 17,203,640 passengers, making it the busiest airport in Northeast China and the 16th busiest nationwide.

title: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
text: The airport is the hub for Dalian Airlines and a focus city for China Southern Airlines and Hainan Airlines.

title: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
text: As Zhoushuizi Airport has reached its designed capacity, the new Dalian Jinzhouwan International Airport is being built on reclaimed land to replace it.

title: Denver International Airport
text: Denver International Airport (DEN), (IATA: DEN, ICAO: KDEN, FAA LID: DEN) , is an airport in Denver, Colorado, United States.

title: Denver International Airport
text: At 33,531 acres (52.4 sq mi), it is the largest airport in the United States by total land area.

title: Denver International Airport
text: Runway 16R/34L, with a length of 16000 ft , is the longest public use runway in the United States.

title: Denver International Airport
text: As of 2016, DEN was the 18th busiest airport in the world and the sixth busiest in the United States by passenger traffic with over 58 million passengers.

title: Denver International Airport
text: It also has the third largest domestic connection network in the country.

title: Denver International Airport
text: s of 2017 , the airport features 135 gates spread out over three detached, yet internally connected, linear concourses (A, B & C).

title: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle
text: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle (or Eastern Air Shuttle) was the brand name of Eastern's air shuttle.

title: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle
text: It began operations on April 30, 1961 and was sold in 1989 to Donald Trump, and later became the Trump Shuttle.

title: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle
text: In April 1992, the shuttle service began as the USAir Shuttle (presently American Airlines Shuttle).

title: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle
text: The shuttle originally flew between New York City, Boston, Washington, D.C. and Newark.

title: Eastern Air Lines Shuttle
text: The shuttle's slogan was "Imagine life without us."

title: Xanthoceras
text: Xanthoceras sorbifolium (yellowhorn, shiny leaf yellowhorn, goldenhorn, Chinese flowering chestnut) is a woody perennial in the soapberry family, Sapindaceae, and the only species in the genus Xanthoceras.

title: Xanthoceras
text: It is native to northern China in the provinces of Gansu, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Nei Monggol, Ningxia, Shaanxi, and Shandong.

title: Xanthoceras
text: It is also cultivated in Russia, having been imported there since the 19th Century.

title: Ehretia

title: Ehretia
text: It contains about 50 species.

title: Ehretia
text: The generic name honors German botanical illustrator Georg Dionysius Ehret (1708–1770).

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: John Paul "Jack" Fox (May 21, 1885 – June 28, 1963) was a professional baseball player whose career spanned 11 seasons, including one in Major League Baseball.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: During that one season in 1908, Fox played with the Philadelphia Athletics.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: Fox compiled a major league batting average of .200 with two runs, six hits and two stolen bases in nine games played.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: Fox also played in the minor leagues with the Class-C Poughkeepsie Colts (1906), the Class-B Albany Senators (1906–07), the Class-A Jersey City Skeeters (1908), the Class-A Memphis Egyptians (1908), the Class-B Wilkes-Barre Barons (1909), the Class-B Troy Trojans, the Class-A Lincoln Railsplitters (1910–11), the Class-B Harrisburg Senators (1912–14), the Class-D Bradford Drillers (1914) and the Class-B Scranton Miners (1915–16).

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: He started his minor league career as an outfielder, but later converted into a pitcher.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: Fox compiled a career minor league batting average of .251 with 670 hits in 694 games played.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: As a pitcher, he compiled a win–loss record of 90–63 in 185 career minor league games pitched.

title: Jack Fox (baseball)
text: Fox batted and threw right-handed.

title: Ron Herbel
text: Ronald Samuel Herbel (January 16, 1938 – January 20, 2000) was a right-handed Major League Baseball pitcher.

title: Ron Herbel
text: His .029 career batting average is the lowest batting average in Major League history for a player with a minimum of 100 at-bats.

title: Dick Kauffman
text: Howard Richard "Dick" Kauffman (June 22, 1888 – April 16, 1948) was a professional baseball player whose career spanned 11 seasons, two of which were spent in Major League Baseball (MLB) with the St. Louis Browns (1914–15).

title: Dick Kauffman
text: Kauffman, a first baseman, compiled a career major league batting average of .259 with 10 runs scored, 36 hits, nine doubles, two triples, and 16 runs batted in (RBIs) in 44 games played.

title: Dick Kauffman
text: His professional career began in 1911 with the minor league York White Roses.

title: Dick Kauffman
text: Kauffman's first MLB season came in 1914.

title: Dick Kauffman
text: He was again called-up in 1915.

title: Dick Kauffman

title: Sousaphone
text: The sousaphone ( ), is a brass instrument in the same family as the more widely known tuba.

title: Sousaphone
text: Created around 1893 by J.W. Pepper at the direction of American bandleader John Philip Sousa (whom the instrument was then named after), it was designed to be easier to play than the concert tuba while standing or marching, as well as to carry the sound of the instrument above the heads of the band.

title: Sousaphone
text: Like the tuba, sound is produced by moving air past the lips, causing them to vibrate or "buzz" into a large cupped mouthpiece.

title: Sousaphone
text: Unlike the tuba, the instrument is bent in a circle to fit around the body of the musician; it ends in a large, flaring bell that is pointed forward, projecting the sound ahead of the player.

title: Sousaphone
text: Because of the ease of carrying and the direction of sound, it is widely employed in marching bands, as well as various other musical genres.

title: Sousaphone
text: Sousaphones were originally made out of brass but in the mid-20th century started to be made from lighter materials like fiberglass; today both types are in wide use.

title: Bukkehorn
text: A bukkehorn (Norwegian) or bockhorn (Swedish), also called ″Billy Goat Horn″ in English, is an ancient Scandinavian musical instrument, made from the horn of a ram or a goat.

title: Bukkehorn
text: The horn is usually made from a goat horn harvested 5 to 7 years before the instrument is crafted.

title: Bukkehorn
text: It was traditionally used by shepherds and milkmaids on summer dairy farms in the mountains, as a signal-instrument or as a scaring instrument.

title: Bukkehorn
text: When the horn later got finger holes it became possible to play melodies with it.

title: Bukkehorn
text: The instrument has two blowing-techniques: the trumpet-principle is the most common, but the clarinet-principle is also used.

title: Experimental musical instrument
text: An experimental musical instrument (or custom-made instrument) is a musical instrument that modifies or extends an existing instrument or class of instruments, or defines or creates a new class of instrument.

title: Experimental musical instrument
text: Some are created through simple modifications, such as cracked drum cymbals or metal objects inserted between piano strings in a prepared piano.

title: Experimental musical instrument
text: Some experimental instruments are created from household items like a homemade mute for brass instruments such as bathtub plugs.

title: Experimental musical instrument
text: Other experimental instruments are created from electronic spare parts, or by mixing acoustic instruments with electric components.

title: Udaka vadya

title: Udaka vadya

title: Udaka vadya

title: Udaka vadya
text: The skill to play this instrument was one of the essential 64 kala to be learnt by a woman.

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: The keyboard glockenspiel (French: "jeu de timbre") or organ glockenspiel is an instrument consisting of a glockenspiel operated by a piano keyboard.

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: It was first used by George Frideric Handel in the oratorio "Saul" (1739).

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: It was also used in the 1739 revivals of his "Il Trionfo del Tempo" and "Acis and Galatea", and the next year in "L'Allegro, il Penseroso ed il Moderato".

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: Half a century later, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart employed a "strumento d’acciaio" in "The Magic Flute" (1791) to represent Papageno's magic bells, and this instrument is believed to have been a keyboard glockenspiel.

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: This part is nowadays sometimes taken by a celesta.

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: Maurice Ravel preferred the keyboard version of the instrument because it can play a true ff dynamic for brilliance and iridescence in orchestral climaxes.

title: Keyboard glockenspiel
text: In the late 20th century, the firm of Bergerault began manufacturing a three-octave (F2–E4) mallet instrument with a damping mechanism operated by a foot pedal, which is capable of dealing with the wide range called for in contemporary scores.

title: Asset classes
text: An asset class is a group of instruments which have similar financial characteristics and behave similarly in the marketplace.

title: Asset classes
text: We can often break these instruments into those having to do with real assets and those having to do with financial assets.

title: Asset classes
text: Often, assets within the same asset class are subject to the same laws and regulations; however, this is not always true.

title: Asset classes
text: For instance, futures on an asset are often considered part of the same asset class as the underlying instrument but are subject to different regulations than the underlying instrument.

title: Accompaniment
text: Accompaniment is the musical parts which provide the rhythmic and/or harmonic support for the melody or main themes of a song or instrumental piece.

title: Accompaniment
text: There are many different styles and types of accompaniment in different genres and styles of music.

title: Accompaniment
text: In homophonic music, the main accompaniment approach used in popular music, a clear vocal melody is supported by subordinate chords.

title: Accompaniment
text: In popular music and traditional music, the accompaniment parts typically provide the "beat" for the music and outline the chord progression of the song or instrumental piece.

title: Accompaniment
text: The accompaniment for a vocal melody or instrumental solo can be played by a single musician playing an instrument such as piano, pipe organ, or guitar.

title: Accompaniment
text: While any instrument can in theory be used as an accompaniment instrument, keyboard and guitar-family instruments tend to be used if there is only a single instrument, as these instruments can play chords and basslines simultaneously (chords and a bassline are easier to play simultaneously on keyboard instruments, but a fingerpicking guitarist can play chords and a bassline simultaneously on guitar).

title: Accompaniment
text: A solo singer can accompany herself by playing guitar or piano while she sings, and in some rare cases, a solo singer can even accompany himself or herself just using his or her voice and body (e.g., Bobby McFerrin).

title: Chrysalis (magazine)

title: Introduction to Metaphysics (Bergson)
text: "Introduction to Metaphysics" (French: ""Introduction à la Métaphysique"") is a 1903 essay about the concept of reality by Henri Bergson.

title: Introduction to Metaphysics (Bergson)
text: For Bergson, reality occurs not in a series of discrete states but as a process similar to that described by process philosophy or the Greek philosopher Heraclitus.

title: Introduction to Metaphysics (Bergson)
text: Reality is fluid and cannot be completely understood through reductionistic analysis, which he said "implies that we go around an object", gaining knowledge from various perspectives which are relative.

title: Introduction to Metaphysics (Bergson)
text: Instead, reality can be grasped absolutely only through intuition, which Bergson expressed as "entering into" the object.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: Duration (French: "la durée") is a theory of time and consciousness posited by the French philosopher Henri Bergson.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: Bergson sought to improve upon inadequacies he perceived in the philosophy of Herbert Spencer, due, he believed, to Spencer's lack of comprehension of mechanics, which led Bergson to the conclusion that time eluded mathematics and science.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: Bergson became aware that the moment one attempted to measure a moment, it would be gone: one measures an immobile, complete line, whereas time is mobile and incomplete.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: For the individual, time may speed up or slow down, whereas, for science, it would remain the same.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: Hence Bergson decided to explore the inner life of man, which is a kind of duration, neither a unity nor a quantitative multiplicity.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: Duration is ineffable and can only be shown indirectly through images that can never reveal a complete picture.

title: Duration (philosophy)
text: It can only be grasped through a simple intuition of the imagination.

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: Samuel Eliot Morison, (July 9, 1887 – May 15, 1976) was an American historian noted for his works of maritime history and American history that were both authoritative and popular.

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: He received his Ph.D. from Harvard University in 1912, and taught history at the university for 40 years.

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: He won Pulitzer Prizes for "Admiral of the Ocean Sea" (1942), a biography of Christopher Columbus, and "John Paul Jones: A Sailor's Biography" (1959).

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: In 1942, he was commissioned to write a history of United States naval operations in World War II, which was published in 15 volumes between 1947 and 1962.

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: Morison wrote the popular "Oxford History of the American People" (1965), and co-authored the classic textbook "The Growth of the American Republic" (1930) with Henry Steele Commager.

title: Samuel Eliot Morison
text: Over the course of his distinguished career, Morison received eleven honorary doctoral degrees, and garnered numerous literary prizes, military honors, and national awards from both foreign countries and the United States, including two Pulitzer Prizes, two Bancroft Prizes, the Balzan Prize, the Legion of Merit, and the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: The 2011 Pulitzer Prizes were announced on Monday, April 18, 2011. "

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: The Los Angeles Times" won two prizes, including the highest honor for Public Service. "

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: The New York Times" also won two awards.

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: No prize was handed out in the Breaking News category. "

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: The Wall Street Journal" won an award for the first time since 2007.

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: Jennifer Egan's "A Visit From the Goon Squad" picked up the Fiction prize after already winning the 2010 National Book Critics Circle Award.

title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
text: Photographer Carol Guzy of "The Washington Post" became the first journalist to win four Pulitzer Prizes.

title: Henri Bergson
text: Henri-Louis Bergson (] ; 18 October 1859 – 4 January 1941) was a French philosopher, influential especially in the first half of the 20th century and after WWII in continental philosophy.

title: Thomas Friedman
text: Thomas Loren Friedman (born July 20, 1953) is an American journalist and author.

title: Thomas Friedman
text: He is a three time Pulitzer Prize winner.

title: Élan vital
text: Élan vital (] ) is a term coined by French philosopher Henri Bergson in his 1907 book "Creative Evolution", in which he addresses the question of self-organisation and spontaneous morphogenesis of things in an increasingly complex manner.

title: Élan vital
text: "Elan vital" was translated in the English edition as "vital impetus", but is usually translated by his detractors as "vital force".

title: Élan vital
text: It is a hypothetical explanation for evolution and development of organisms, which Bergson linked closely with consciousness – with the intuitive perception of experience and the flow of inner time.

title: Time and Free Will
text: Time and Free Will: An Essay on the Immediate Data of Consciousness (French: "Essai sur les données immédiates de la conscience") is Henri Bergson's doctoral thesis, first published in 1889.

title: Time and Free Will
text: The essay deals with the problem of free will, which Bergson contends is merely a common confusion among philosophers caused by an illegitimate translation of the unextended into the extended, as a means of introducing his theory of duration, which would become highly influential among continental philosophers in the following century.

title: Moina Mathers
text: Moina Mathers, born Mina Bergson (28 February 1865 – 25 July 1928), was an artist and occultist at the turn of the 20th century.

title: Moina Mathers
text: She was the sister of French philosopher Henri Bergson, the first man of Jewish descent to be awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1927.

title: Moina Mathers
text: She is, however, more known for her marriage to the English occultist, Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers, one of the founders of the organisation Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn and, after his death in 1918, for being the head of a successor organisation, called the Rosicrucian Order of the Alpha et Omega.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Matter and Memory (French: "Matière et mémoire", 1896) is a book by the French philosopher Henri Bergson.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Its subtitle is "Essay on the relation of body and spirit" ("Essai sur la relation du corps à l’esprit"), and the work presents an analysis of the classical philosophical problems concerning this relation.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Within that frame the analysis of memory serves the purpose of clarifying the problem.

title: Matter and Memory
text: "Matter and Memory" was written in reaction to the book "The Maladies of Memory" by Théodule Ribot, which appeared in 1881.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Ribot claimed that the findings of brain science proved that memory is lodged within a particular part of the nervous system; localized within the brain and thus being of a material nature.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Bergson was opposed to this reduction of spirit to matter.

title: Matter and Memory
text: Defending a clear anti-reductionist position, he considered memory to be of a deeply spiritual nature, the brain serving the need of orienting present action by inserting relevant memories.

title: Matter and Memory
text: The brain thus being of a practical nature, certain lesions tend to perturb this practical function, but without erasing memory as such.

title: Matter and Memory
text: The memories are, instead, simply not 'incarnated', and cannot serve their purpose.

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: Lana Del Rey is the second EP by American singer and songwriter Lana Del Rey.

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: It was released on January 10, 2012 in the United States and Canada through Interscope Records.

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: After publishing two unsuccessful works, an EP, "Kill Kill" (2008) and a studio album, "Lana Del Ray" (2010), the four-track EP was released in anticipation of Del Rey's major label debut "Born to Die" (2012).

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: The tracks are influenced by several genres, including indie pop, hip hop, and alternative music.

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: The lyrics and melody were written primarily by Del Rey, Patrik Berger, and Justin Parker.

title: Lana Del Rey (EP)
text: Production of the album was led by Emile Haynie, who also co-wrote "Blue Jeans".

title: Back to December
text: "Back to December" is a song written and recorded by American singer/songwriter Taylor Swift for her third studio album "Speak Now" (2010).

title: Back to December
text: The song was sent to country radio in the United States on November 15, 2010, as the second single from "Speak Now".

title: Back to December
text: According to Swift, "Back to December" is the first time she ever apologizes to someone in a song.

title: Back to December
text: Critics speculate that the song is about Taylor Lautner, Swift's ex-boyfriend, which was later acknowledged by Lautner.

title: Back to December
text: "Back to December" is considered an orchestral country pop ballad and its lyrics are a remorseful plea for forgiveness for breaking up with a former lover.

title: Kill Kill (song)
text: "Kill Kill" is a song written by American singer-songwriter Elizabeth Grant released originally under the stage name "Lizzy Grant" in 2008 and "Lana Del Ray in 2010.

title: Kill Kill (song)
text: Grant is widely known now as Lana Del Rey.

title: Kill Kill (song)
text: Kill Kill was first released on October 21, 2008, on Grant's three-track extended play of the same name.

title: Kill Kill (song)
text: It was then later included on her first album under the name Lana Del Ray, ""Lana Del Ray A.K.A. Lizzy Grant"" also alternatively titled simply ""Lana Del Rey"".

title: Video Games (song)
text: "Video Games" is a song recorded by American singer and songwriter Lana Del Rey for her second studio album and major label debut, "Born to Die" (2012).

title: Video Games (song)
text: It was first released to the Internet on June 29, 2011, was later released on her extended play, "Lana Del Rey", and re-released as the lead single from her second studio album, "Born to Die" on October 10, 2011, through Interscope Records.

title: Video Games (song)
text: The song was produced by Robopop while the lyrics were written by Del Rey and Justin Parker.

title: Video Games (song)
text: "Video Games" is a baroque pop ballad that speaks of the protagonist who, despite being ignored by her significant other, resolves to love him regardless.

title: Yoann Lemoine
text: Yoann Lemoine (born 16 March 1983) is a French music video director, graphic designer and singer-songwriter.

title: Yoann Lemoine
text: His most notable works include his music video direction for Katy Perry's "Teenage Dream", Taylor Swift's single "Back to December", Lana Del Rey's "Born to Die" and Mystery Jets' "Dreaming of Another World".

title: Lana Del Ray (album)
text: Lana Del Ray (alternatively written as Lana Del Ray a.k.a. Lizzy Grant) is the debut studio album by American singer and songwriter Lana Del Rey.

title: Lana Del Ray (album)
text: The album was released digitally via the iTunes Store by 5 Points Records on January 4, 2010 when she was known as Lana Del "Ray".

title: Lana Del Ray (album)
text: However, the record was eventually pulled from retailers soon afterwards because, according to Del Rey, the label was unable to fund it.

title: Lana Del Ray (album)
text: Del Rey ultimately bought back the rights to the album, whose title uses an alternate spelling of the singer's stage name, "Del Rey" being spelled "Del Ray" instead.

title: Lana Del Ray (album)
text: After releasing "Born to Die" (2012) under her stage name Lana Del Rey, she expressed her wish to re-release the album.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: "Blue Jeans" is a song by American singer-songwriter Lana Del Rey for her second studio album "Born to Die" (2012).

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: It was released on April 8, 2012, by Interscope Records as the third single from the record.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Produced by Emile Haynie, the song was written by Del Rey, Haynie, and Dan Heath.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: It is a downtempo ballad with hip hop influences.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: A controversial performance of the song on "SNL" placed Del Rey under scrutiny and polarized opinion.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Charting across Europe and Asia, "Blue Jeans" reached the top 10 in Belgium, Poland, and Israel.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Two music videos were created for the song.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: The first was self-produced.

title: Blue Jeans (Lana Del Rey song)
text: The second was shot and directed by Yoann Lemoine, featuring film noir elements and crocodiles.

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: "Yayo" is a song by American singer and songwriter Lana Del Rey.

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: It appears on her first extended play, "Kill Kill", her debut album, "Lana Del Ray", and her third EP, "Paradise".

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: After the release of her third EP, the song charted in France.

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Before signing to a major record label, Del Rey released a self-produced music video for "Yayo".

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Ubiquitously, the song garnered acclaim, many reviewers saying the song was one of the best songs Del Rey has ever written and praising Del Rey's voice.

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: Appearing on three of Del Rey's albums to date, the song is one of few that was authored solely by her.

title: Yayo (Lana Del Rey song)
text: The original version of the song was released through 5 Point Records and produced by David Kahne, later being remastered by Emile Haynie and Dan Heath.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: American singer and occasional actress Lana Del Rey has appeared in three films as an actress, eighteen television shows, and three commercials, along with offering her talents to five films as singer.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: Del Rey's first appearance was in the independent film "Poolside" (2010), which features Del Rey playing Lisa, a rich girl who spends her days smoking cigarettes by the pool.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: She received top billing for the project.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: Del Rey's next appearance was in a less-than-one-minute long short art film titled "Lana Del Rey" which was produced by Interview magazine and features noir-ish style and cinematic themes.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: Del Rey's breakout appearance was in an Anthony Mandler directed film, which Del Rey wrote, titled "Tropico" (2013).

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: The film features Del Rey as a fictionalized version of Eve while also playing the Virgin Mary.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: "Tropico" received positive reviews and was Del Rey's second film that gave her top billing.

title: Lana Del Rey videography
text: Along with appearing in a handful of short films, Del Rey has appeared in 18 television shows and specials as herself along with appearing in campaign commercials for companies including Keds and H&M.

title: Lana Del Rey discography
text: American singer and songwriter Lana Del Rey has released five studio albums, four extended plays, 20 singles, and 16 music videos. Lana Del Rey signed a record deal with 5 Points Records in 2007 and the following year, she released her debut EP, "Kill Kill", under the stage name Lizzy Grant.

title: Lana Del Rey discography
text: Her debut studio album, "Lana Del Ray", was shelved initially and was released in January 2010 under the name Lana Del Ray.

title: Lana Del Rey discography
text: However, the record was pulled three months later.

title: Clock Tower, Brighton
text: The Clock Tower (sometimes called the Jubilee Clock Tower) is a free-standing clock tower in the centre of Brighton, part of the English city of Brighton and Hove.

title: Clock Tower, Brighton
text: Built in 1888 in commemoration of Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee, the distinctive structure included innovative structural features and became a landmark in the popular and fashionable seaside resort.

title: Clock Tower, Brighton
text: The city's residents "retain a nostalgic affection" for it, even though opinion is sharply divided as to the tower's architectural merit.

title: Clock Tower, Brighton
text: English Heritage has listed the clock tower at Grade II for its architectural and historical importance.

title: Galle Clock Tower
text: The Galle Clock Tower (or Anthonisz Memorial Clock Tower) is located within the Galle Fort in Galle, Sri Lanka.

title: Galle Clock Tower
text: The Clock Tower is a popular landmark and overlooks the central Moon Bastion, on the site of the former guard room.

title: Galle Clock Tower
text: The Clock Tower was constructed in 1883, paid for through public subscriptions by the people of Galle, in recognition of Dr. P. D. Anthonisz.

title: Galle Clock Tower
text: The clock itself was the sole gift of a grateful patient, Mudaliyar Samson de Abrew Rajapakse.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: On 22 June 1954 The foundation stone of this great mosque was laid in a religious customs.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: That day fell on the birth day of Ali al-Ridha, eighth Imam of shia.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: The construction of it was ended in 1961.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: Azam mosque had been built basis on the Islamic architecture.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: This mosque made of four prayer halls and three towering balconies.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: The diameter of the large dome of the mosque is 30 metres and its height above the roof of the mosque is 15 metres and 35 metres from the basement of the mosque.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: The minarets of the mosque has 25 metres length above the roof of the mosque and 45 metres from the basement of the mosque.

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: The upper part of the minarets is 5 metres .

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: It has special section and used to call to prayers (A'zaan).

title: Azam mosque of Qom
text: A towering clock tower with a big clock is located in the north of the mosque and this tower can be seen from all the four sides of the mosque.

title: Eski Imaret Mosque
text: Eski Imaret Mosque (Turkish: "Eski Imaret Camii" ) is a former Eastern Orthodox church converted into a mosque by the Ottomans.

title: Eski Imaret Mosque
text: The church has traditionally been identified with that belonging to the Monastery of Christ Pantepoptes (Greek: Μονή του Χριστού Παντεπόπτη ), meaning "Christ the all-seeing".

title: Eski Imaret Mosque
text: It is the only documented 11th-century church in Istanbul which survives intact, and represents a key monument of middle Byzantine architecture.

title: Eski Imaret Mosque
text: Despite that, the building remains one among the least studied of the city.

title: Birgu Clock Tower
text: The Birgu Clock Tower (Maltese: "It-Torri tal-Arloġġ tal-Birgu" ), also called the "Vittoriosa Clock Tower" and originally the Civic Clock Tower, was a clock tower in Birgu, Malta.

title: Birgu Clock Tower
text: It was located in Victory Square, the city's main square, and it was a prominent landmark in Birgu and the rest of the Three Cities.

title: Birgu Clock Tower
text: The tower was probably built in the Middle Ages, although some sources state that it was constructed in 1549.

title: Birgu Clock Tower
text: It served as a watchtower since it had views over the Grand Harbour and the surrounding countryside, and it saw use during the Great Siege of Malta in 1565.

title: Birgu Clock Tower
text: A clock was installed in the tower in the 17th century.

title: Tashkopryu Mosque
text: Tashkyopryu Mosque (Bulgarian: Ташкьопрю джамия "Tashkyopryu Dzhamiya", Turkish: "Taşköprü Camii") is a mosque in Plovdiv, Bulgaria , built by Ottoman Turks in 16th century during their 500-year rule in today's Bulgaria.

title: Tashkopryu Mosque
text: It is currently the third mosque in Plovdiv which is in good condition after Dzhumaya Mosque and Imaret Mosque.

title: Tashkopryu Mosque
text: It is currently inactive despite efforts and demands, mainly by Turks of Bulgaria, to give active status for it.

title: Kumanovo Clock Tower
text: Kumanovo Clock Tower (Macedonian: Саат Кула Куманово ) was a clock tower in Kumanovo, Ottoman Empire (today Republic of Macedonia).

title: Kumanovo Clock Tower
text: The tower is believed to have existed since the second half of the 18th century but there are now known historical facts.

title: Kumanovo Clock Tower
text: It was near Eski Mosque in the former Orta Bunar Neighborhood (Macedonian: Орта Бунар Маало ).

title: Kumanovo Clock Tower
text: It was demolished after the Second World War.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: Hysen Pasha Mosque (Albanian: "Xhamia e Hysen Pashës" ) or Clock Mosque "(Xhamia e Sahatit)" is a Cultural Monument of Albania, located in Berat.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: It was built in 1670 by Hussein Pasha.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: It is named Clock Mosque because in 1870 the Ottomans built a clock tower next to it.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: The clock tower was destroyed during the Communist dictatorship in 1967.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: The mosque also got destroyed with the minaret being the only part left over.

title: Hysen Pasha Mosque
text: After the end of Communism the mosque got renovated.

title: Nusretiye Clock Tower
text: Nusretiye Clock Tower, aka Tophane Clock Tower, is a clock tower situated in Tophane, a neighborhood in Beyoğlu district of Istanbul, Turkey next to Nusretiye Mosque and Tophane Kiosk at the European waterfront of Bosphorus.

title: Nusretiye Clock Tower
text: It was ordered by the Ottoman sultan Abdülmecid I (1823-1861), designed by architect Garabet Amira Balyan and completed in 1848.

title: Clock Tower of Murshidabad
text: The Clock Tower of Murshidabad (locally known just as "Clock Tower" or "Ghari Ghar", also known as "Big Ben of Murshidabad") is a clock tower in the Nizamat Fort Campus in West Bengal, India.

title: Clock Tower of Murshidabad
text: The clock tower stands in the garden space between the Nizamat Imambara and the Hazarduari Palace; to its east, hardly a few feet away, is the old Madina Mosque and the Bacchawali Tope.

title: Opry Mills
text: Opry Mills is a super-regional shopping mall owned by Simon Property Group, formerly by its initial owners Mills Corporation and Gaylord Entertainment.

title: Opry Mills
text: It opened in Nashville, Tennessee in 2000 on the former site of the Opryland USA theme park.

title: Grand Ole Opry
text: The Grand Ole Opry is a weekly country-music stage concert in Nashville, Tennessee, which was founded on November 28, 1925, by George D. Hay as a one-hour radio "barn dance" on WSM.

title: Grand Ole Opry
text: Currently owned and operated by Opry Entertainment (a division of Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc.), it is the longest-running radio broadcast in US history, albeit not the longest-running one on a radio network.

title: Grand Ole Opry
text: Dedicated to honoring country music and its history, the Opry showcases a mix of famous singers and contemporary chart-toppers performing country, bluegrass, Americana, folk, gospel, and comedic performances and skits.

title: Grand Ole Opry
text: It attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors from around the world and millions of radio and Internet listeners.

title: Keith Bilbrey
text: Keith Bilbrey (born August 14, 1952) is an American country music disc jockey and television host in Nashville, Tennessee.

title: Keith Bilbrey
text: He served as a disc jockey at Nashville's WSM, as an announcer on the Grand Ole Opry, and as the host of TNN’s Grand Ole Opry Live.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Nashville Terminal Subdivision is a railroad line owned by CSX Transportation in the U.S. State of Tennessee.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Subdivision is broken up into 5 sections all in Nashville, Tennessee.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The northern part of the Terminal is in Madison, Tennessee at milepost 000/0BA 174 on the southern end of the Ex-L&N Mainline Subdivision at Monfort.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Disptach for the Mainline Sub is known as "LD" which is part of the Cincinnati Division.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From here in Madison begins the double track that stays for another 22 miles south to Brentwood, Tennessee.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At milepost 000/0BA/00H 176.6, the famous Johnny Cash "Amqui" location where the Ex-L&N Evansville, Indiana line, the Henderson Subdivision meets with the Terminal.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Dispatch for the Henderson Sub is known as "SA" and operates on AAR58.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: There are two crossings near each other, Williams Ave and Nesbitt Lane at Amqui.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From here the Terminal goes south about 2 miles to the Nashville National Cemetery to the first major location, known as Ekin, 000179, where there is a cross over track from number 1 to number 2 track (left to right track).

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: There is also the first EDD (Defect Detector) at 000179.1.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Few more miles southward, the next major location appears.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At 000181.0, Maplewood is a major location for the Terminal.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From here the regular Terminal goes south to swap crews at Kayne Ave, and the right side, Radnor Cutoff, detours the city and gives yard departures and arrivals direct access to and from Radnor yard to cities like Louisville and Chicago.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Cutoff runs from Maplewood to Shelby Park double track.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From Shebly the track converges into one to pass the historic Shelby bridge, then it opens back to double track.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From there, the cutoff hits the Intermediates at 0BA187.0 known as Chicken Pike.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Radnor Cutoff carries the L&N mainline classification of "0BA" but meets the main at the same milepost from the Terminal.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At Chicken Pike, trains are staged to await arrival to Radnor yard.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Once they get clearance, speed is decreased to 15, and at 0BA188.1 the EDD (Defect Detector) sounds for departures and arrivals.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: This location is known as North Radnor.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The right track diverging from the #2 is known as A-1, it is for departure trains to Chattanooga and Atlanta.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The left track which goes west from the #1 is known as A-2, and serves as a departure track to Memphis, and if the cutoff is out of service, all northbound departures.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The interesting piece of Maplewood is the crossovers that are there to move trains from the Cutoff to the Main.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Both lines remain double track for a while.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The main runs south for 2 more miles until the Intermediate signals at 000183.0.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Commonly trains will stop before Delmas Ave when Kayne Ave is at capacity and await dispatch permission before moving south.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From here, the main continues south until the CR Cumberland River Swingbridge, where the main converges into a single track shortly to cross the bridge.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At this point, trains had been running at track speed of around 40.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: From the drawbridge into town, speed is reduced to around 10.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: After the bridge is passed, the main returns to double track in downtown.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: On the #1 track about a half a mile south, another connecting track is present.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: This is the Wye track that connects the main with the Bruceton side, while rarely used for mainline trains, locals and river jobs use it.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The location is known as 8th Avenue or 8th Avenue Wye.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The main then runs down to Kayne Ave, the central hotbed of all Nashville thru traffic.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Memphis, Tennessee Ex-L&N Bruceton Subdivision meets with the Terminal.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Bruceton Sub begins at Church Street at 00N0.0.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The line then runs single track until 00N0.7 "11th Avenue" where it turns into double track and also meets the aforementioned, Wye track.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Bruceton line then goes southwest a while to the next signals, at "Shops".

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Now speed has been increased.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The line is still double track until "Sellars", where speed is increased to 40 and jurisdiction transferred to the SD Dispatcher.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: For a short time, 4 main tracks are present and an additional fifth track for switchers and yard movements.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The tracks from left to right in Kayne Ave are as follows: 100, 99, 98, 12, 3.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Kayne Ave yard is also here in this area, which houses some frieght and some switcher engines.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The tracks to the old shed are covered and removed.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Union Station is not an active station, but a historic hotel.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Crew change usually occurs at the "walkway" which is under the Demombreun St bridge by the Kayne Ave Tower.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: This is also where the Ex-NC&StL Chattanooga Subdivision begins.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: Then tracks run south to Fogg St/South End where things get complicated.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At milepost 000/0BA/00J187 the 98 track merges into the 12 track, making for 3 tracks now.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: There is a crossover from 99 to 12, also a crossover from 12 to 3.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: About 2/10ths of a mile down the 99 merges into the 12 track reducing the tracks back to the regular double.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: About 4/10ths of a mile down the line from Fogg St, 000187.4, Oak St, is a crossover track from #2 to #1 (the track names are no longer 3 and 12, but are back to regular names).

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: When trains use this crossover northbound, such as Memphis bound trains from the A-2 line, they refer to it as "Long Lead".

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: And now, the Terminal splits into two parts.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The right side turns into a single track shortly, and will become the Chattanooga Subdivision, and the left side runs south to Brentwood.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision

text: Commonly northbounds will stage at 4th Ave on the #1 to await clearance.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At Danley, the Terminal ends but the same dispatcher handles traffic, "SC".

text: At Oak Street, our main terminal line goes south two miles to 000189.0 known as Criaghead or Vine Hill.

text: And there is also a connection/delivery track to the Nashville and Eastern Railroad which connects the Tennessee Central Railroad Museum to a major railroad.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The #2 track meets the E-Line arrival track which most Memphis trains and locals use.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The B-Line which meets the #1 track is used for departures out of the C yard and local jobs.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: At Mayton, 000192.3, the B line meets the #1 track, and there is a crossover track from #2 to #1.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision

text: The right track is the main, S&NA North, while the left track is the Nashville Subdivision which runs to Columbia and exchanges freight with the TSRR.

title: Nashville Terminal Subdivision
text: The Nashville Terminal Subdivision is one of the busiest locations on the CSX network, and one of the most important.

title: Ryman Auditorium
text: Ryman Auditorium (formerly Grand Ole Opry House and Union Gospel Tabernacle) is a 2,362-seat live performance venue, located at 116 5th Avenue North, in Nashville, Tennessee and is best known as the home of the "Grand Ole Opry" from 1943 to 1974.

title: Ryman Auditorium
text: It is owned and operated by Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc.
