title: Wind chime
text: They are usually hung outside of a building or residence as a visual and aural garden ornament.

title: Wind chime
text: Since the percussion instruments are struck according to the random effects of the wind blowing the chimes, wind chimes have been considered an example of chance-based music.

title: Wind chime
text: The tubes or rods may sound either indistinct pitches, or fairly distinct pitches.

title: Wind chime
text: Wind chimes that sound fairly distinct pitches can, through the chance movement of air, create simple melodies or broken chords.

title: Imprest system
text: The imprest system is a form of financial accounting system.

text: The most common imprest system is the petty cash system.

title: Imprest system
text: The base characteristic of an imprest system is that a fixed amount is reserved, which after a certain period of time or when circumstances require, because money was spent, it will be replenished.

title: Imprest system
text: This replenishment will come from another account source, e.g., petty cash will be replenished by cashing a cheque drawn on a bank account.

title: Uterine cancer
text: Uterine cancer or womb cancer is any type of cancer that emerges from the tissue of the uterus.

title: Uterine cancer
text: It can refer to several types of cancer, with cervical cancer (arising from the lower portion of the uterus) being the most common type worldwide and the second most common cancer in women in developing countries.

title: Uterine cancer
text: Endometrial cancer (or cancer of the inner lining of the uterus) is the second most common type, and fourth most common cancer in women from developed countries.

title: Uterine cancer
text: Risk factors depend on specific type, but obesity, older age, and human papillomavirus infection add the greatest risk of developing uterine cancer.

title: Uterine cancer
text: Early on, there may be no symptoms, but irregular vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain or fullness may develop.

title: Uterine cancer
text: If caught early, most types of uterine cancer can be cured using surgical or medical methods.

title: Uterine cancer
text: When the cancer has extended beyond the uterine tissue, more advanced treatments including combinations of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery may be required.

title: Petty treason
text: Petty treason or petit treason was an offence under the common law of England which involved the betrayal (including murder) of a superior by a subordinate.

title: Petty treason
text: It differed from the better-known high treason in that high treason can only be committed against the Sovereign.

title: Petty treason
text: In England and Wales, petty treason ceased to be a distinct offence from murder by virtue of the Offences against the Person Act 1828.

title: Petty treason
text: It was abolished in Ireland in 1829.

title: Petty treason
text: It never existed in Scotland.

title: Petty treason
text: It has also been abolished in other common-law countries.

title: Petit jury
text: In common law, a petit jury (or trial jury, sometimes petty jury) hears the evidence in a trial as presented by both the plaintiff (petitioner) and the defendant (respondent).

title: Petit jury
text: After hearing the evidence and often jury instructions from the judge, the group retires for deliberation, to consider a verdict.

title: Petit jury
text: The majority required for a verdict varies.

title: Petit jury
text: In some cases it must be unanimous, while in other jurisdictions it may be a majority or supermajority.

title: Petit jury
text: A jury that is unable to come to a verdict is referred to as a hung jury.

title: Petit jury
text: The size of the jury varies; in criminal cases involving serious felonies there are usually 12 jurors, although Scotland uses 15.

title: Petit jury
text: A number of countries that are not in the English common law tradition have quasi-juries on which lay judges or jurors and professional judges deliberate together regarding criminal cases.

title: Petit jury
text: However, the common law trial jury is the most common type of jury system.

title: High treason
text: Treason is criminal disloyalty.

title: High treason
text: Historically, in common law countries, high treason is treason against the state.

title: High treason
text: It was differentiated from petty treason (or "petit" treason), which was treason against a lesser lawful superior (such as a servant killing his master).

title: High treason
text: Petty treason was restricted to cases of homicide in 1351, and came to be considered a more serious degree of murder.

title: Kegelhelm

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: Dukenfield Hall is a country house located between Knutsford and Mobberley in Cheshire, England.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: Now a symmetrical brick building, it originated in the late 16th or early 17th century as a small cruck-framed house, entered at one end.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: During the 17th century it was faced with brick, cross wings were added and the roof was heightened.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: The house was originally called Podmore House.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: Further additions were made to the house in the 19th and 20th centuries.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: It is constructed in plum-coloured brick with stone dressings, and has a stone-slate roof.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: The house is in two storeys plus an attic.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: Its entrance front is E-shaped, and has three projecting wings with gables.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: The house is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II* listed building.

title: Dukenfield Hall
text: Associated with the house are two structures listed at Grade II.

title: Dukenfield Hall

title: Jeff Hoover

title: Jeff Hoover

title: Feirstein Graduate School of Cinema
text: The Barry R. Feirstein Graduate School of Cinema, more commonly referred to as the Feirstein Graduate School of Cinema, is a film school and one of the graduate schools of Brooklyn College, a senior college within the City University of New York.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: Charles T. Holt House is a historic home located at Haw River, Alamance County, North Carolina.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: It was designed by noted architect George Franklin Barber and built in 1897.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: The house is a 2 1/2-story, rectangular dwelling sheathed in wood, slate, brick and stone in the Queen Anne style.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: It features peaks, turrets and decorative chimney stacks.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: Also on the property are the contributing carriage house, servant's quarters, gas house, corn crib, barn, and well house / flowerhouse.

title: Charles T. Holt House
text: It was built for textile businessman Charles T Holt, the son of Thomas Michael Holt, governor of North Carolina, and his wife Gena Jones Holt, the daughter of Thomas Goode Jones, governor of Alabama.

title: Farr House
text: The Farr House is a historic house located at 106 E. Wynoka St. in Pierre, South Dakota.

title: Farr House
text: Built in 1904, the house was designed by architect E. J. Donahue in the Colonial Revival style.

title: Farr House
text: Donahue's design exhibits Georgian and Adamesque influences and features Ionic columns on the porch, two-story Ionic pilasters at the front corners, Palladian windows, and a dentillated cornice.

title: Farr House
text: The house's first owner, Colonel Farr, was a veteran and banker; his wife, Mary Noyes-Farr, was one of the first female doctors in Pierre.

title: Farr House
text: Peter Norbeck later lived in the house during his term as South Dakota Governor, and Governor Carl Gunderson also lived in the house for a short time.

title: Farr House
text: The house is now a bed and breakfast.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: Edmund Sharpe (31 October 1809 – 8 May 1877) was an English architect, architectural historian, railway engineer, and sanitary reformer.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: Born in Knutsford, Cheshire, he was educated first by his parents and then at schools locally and in Runcorn, Greenwich and Sedbergh.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: Following his graduation from Cambridge University he was awarded a travelling scholarship, enabling him to study architecture in Germany and southern France.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: In 1835 he established an architectural practice in Lancaster, initially working on his own.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: In 1845 he entered into partnership with Edward Paley, one of his pupils.

title: Edmund Sharpe
text: Sharpe's main focus was on churches, and he was a pioneer in the use of terracotta as a structural material in church building, designing what were known as "pot" churches, the first of which was St Stephen and All Martyrs' Church, Lever Bridge.

title: Thomas H. Gale House

title: Thomas H. Gale House

title: Thomas H. Gale House
text: The house is significant because of what it shows about the architect's early development period.

title: Thomas H. Gale House

title: Mirages (album)

title: Mirages (album)

title: Mirages (album)

title: Mirages (album)

title: Mirages (album)

title: Heisman curse
text: The Heisman curse is a term coined to reference a two-part assertion of a negative future for the winning player of the Heisman Trophy.

title: Heisman curse
text: The "curse" supposes that any college football player who wins the Heisman plays on a team that will likely lose its subsequent bowl game.

title: Heisman curse
text: The trend of post-award failure has garnered the attention of the mainstream media.

title: Heisman curse
text: Talk of a curse in relation to bowl results was particularly prevalent from 2003 to 2008, when six Heisman Trophy winners compiled a cumulative 1–5 bowl game record, and five of those six led number one ranked teams into the Bowl Championship Series (BCS) National Championship Game as favorites (Heisman Trophy winners, including Reggie Bush, who gave back his Heisman Trophy, are 4–8 overall in the BCS National Championship Game and College Football Playoff National Championship, although prior to 2009 they were 1–6).

title: Heisman curse
text: Additionally, the Heisman curse asserts that in most cases a Heisman winner will have either a poor career in the National Football League (NFL), or in fact not even see such a football career at all.

title: Heisman curse
text: Although many Heisman winners have not enjoyed success at the professional level, including players like Matt Leinart, Andre Ware, Jason White, Rashaan Salaam, Eric Crouch, Ty Detmer, Troy Smith and Gino Torretta, proponents of the "curse" rarely cite highly successful players such as Barry Sanders, Charles Woodson, Eddie George, Tim Brown, Bo Jackson, Marcus Allen, Earl Campbell, and Tony Dorsett among the notables.

title: Dancing Stage Fusion

title: Dance Dance Dance (novel)
text: Dance Dance Dance (ダンス・ダンス・ダンス , Dansu Dansu Dansu ) is the sixth novel by Japanese writer Haruki Murakami.

title: Dance Dance Dance (novel)
text: First published in 1988, it was translated into English by Alfred Birnbaum in 1994.

title: Dance Dance Dance (novel)
text: The book is a sequel to Murakami's novel "A Wild Sheep Chase".

title: Dance Dance Dance (novel)
text: In 2001, Murakami said that writing "Dance Dance Dance" had been a healing act after his unexpected fame following the publication of "Norwegian Wood" and that, because of this, he had enjoyed writing "Dance" more than any other.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
text: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle (ねじまき鳥クロニクル , Nejimakitori Kuronikuru ) is a novel published in 1994–1995 by Japanese author Haruki Murakami.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
text: The American translation and its British adaptation, dubbed the "only official translations" (English) are by Jay Rubin and were first published in 1997.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
text: For this novel, Murakami received the Yomiuri Literary Award, which was awarded to him by one of his harshest former critics, Kenzaburō Ōe.

title: Dance Factory (video game)
text: Dance Factory is a PlayStation 2 game developed by Broadsword Interactive and published by Codemasters.

title: Dance Factory (video game)

title: Dance Factory (video game)

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: "Dub-I-Dub" is a song recorded by Danish Eurodance act Me & My.

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: It was released in September 1995 as the first single from the eponymous album.

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: The song was successful in many European countries, being a top ten hit in Denmark (number 1), Sweden where it peaked at number 2, and Belgium.

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: The song was also a top 20 hit in Finland, Switzerland, Norway and Austria.

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: The single was the subject of multiple remixes and was included on band's best of "The Ultimate Collection", released in 2007.

title: Dub-I-Dub
text: "Dub-I-Dub" was used in video games, such as "Dance Dance Revolution 2ndMix", "Dancing Stage EuroMix", "Dance Dance Revolution Party Collection", and "Dance Dance Revolution X".

title: Trevor Kennedy
text: Trevor Kennedy (born Trevor John Kennedy; born in Perth, Western Australia, on 24 June 1942) is an Australian businessman and company director.

title: Trevor Kennedy
text: He has served on the board of directors of many Australian companies, including Consolidated Press Holdings and Qantas.

title: Trevor Kennedy
text: He is a former journalist and right-hand man of Kerry Packer and a former business associate of Malcolm Turnbull, current leader of the Australian Parliamentary Liberal Party and the 29th Prime Minister of Australia.

title: Brian Cook (football administrator)
text: Brian Carlyle Cook (born 14 November 1955) is a Scottish-born Australian businessman and former Australian rules football player and coach who is the current Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Geelong Football Club in the Australian Football League (AFL).

title: Brian Cook (football administrator)
text: Cook played for a number of different clubs in several Australian states and territories, including the Box Hill Football Club in the Victorian Football Association (VFA), the Melbourne Football Club in the Victorian Football League (VFL), and the East Perth and Subiaco Football Clubs in the Western Australian National Football League (WANFL), and later captain-coached the Ainslie Football Club in the Australian Capital Territory Football League (ACTFL).

title: Brian Cook (football administrator)
text: After his retirement from coaching, Cook occupied positions with the Australian Sports Commission and the West Australian Football Commission, before being appointed CEO of the West Coast Eagles in 1990.

title: Brian Cook (football administrator)
text: He quit this position in 1999 to take up the same role with Geelong.

title: Polygamy in Morocco
text: Polygamy in Morocco is legal, but very uncommon due to restrictions that were introduced by the government in 2004 that mandated financial qualifications a husband must meet in order to marry a second wife.

title: Polygamy in Morocco
text: In addition, a husband must have written permission from his current wife before marrying a second wife.

title: Polygamy in Morocco
text: Breaking these rules and marrying without permission from one's current wife can and has resulted in arrests.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: Prince Dipangkorn Rasmijoti (born 29 April 2005; Thai: ทีปังกรรัศมีโชติ ; rtgs: "Thipangkon Ratsamichot" ; ] ) is a member of the country's Chakri dynasty and heir presumptive to the throne of Thailand.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: He is the fifth son of King Vajiralongkorn.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: His mother is Srirasmi Suwadee, the king's third legal wife.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: His father also has a daughter by his first wife and five children (four sons and a daughter) by his second wife; all the children of the second wife were born before the then-crown prince married their mother but after the Crown Prince married her the 5 children were legitimised by marriage.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: After the Crown Prince divorced his second wife in 1996, he disowned her sons.

title: Dipangkorn Rasmijoti
text: Thus, Dipangkorn is the only recognised son of the king.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: Alan John Cransberg (born 22 September 1958) is an Australian businessman and former Australian rules footballer who is the current chairman of the West Coast Eagles in the Australian Football League, as well as a member of the boards of several other organisations.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: Cransberg grew up in Bunbury, Western Australia, attending Bunbury Senior High School.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: He played for the South Bunbury Football Club in the South West Football League (SWFL), before being recruited by the Swan Districts Football Club in the Perth-based Western Australian National Football League (WANFL) prior to the 1976 season.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: Cransberg went on to play 115 games for Swan Districts, mainly playing as a defender.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: He played at centre half-back in Swan Districts' 1982 premiership team, and also played in the premiership side the following season, retiring after the 1983 season to concentrate on his business career.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: Cransberg graduated from the University of Western Australia in 1980 with an honours degree in civil engineering.

title: Alan Cransberg
text: He joined Alcoa Australia after his graduation, and held various planning, engineering and managerial positions from 1981 to 1997, before being appointed location manager of the company's Pinjarra alumina refinery in 1998.

title: James Packer
text: James Douglas Packer (born 8 September 1967) is an Australian businessman and investor.

title: Leg of mutton nude
text: Double Nude Portrait: The Artist and his Second Wife 1937 (also known as the Leg of mutton nude portrait) is an oil on canvas painting by British artist Stanley Spencer.

title: Leg of mutton nude
text: It depicts Spencer and his soon-to-be second wife, Patricia Preece, beside a raw leg of lamb.

title: Leg of mutton nude
text: The painting is sexually charged: Spencer's second wife was a lesbian in a long-term relationship when they married, and their marriage was never consummated.

title: Leg of mutton nude
text: The painting is held by the Tate Gallery, which describes it as "probably now Spencer's most famous picture".

title: Ben Roberts-Smith
text: Benjamin "Ben" Roberts-Smith, (born 1 November 1978) is an Australian businessman, former Australian Army soldier, and a recipient of the Victoria Cross for Australia (VC), the highest award in the Australian honours system.

title: Ben Roberts-Smith
text: Roberts-Smith was awarded the VC for his actions during a helicopter assault into Tizak on 11 June 2010 as part of an offensive in the Shah Wali Kot region while serving with the Special Air Service Regiment in Afghanistan.

title: Ben Roberts-Smith
text: The medal, together with his Medal for Gallantry awarded during a tour of Afghanistan in 2006, made Roberts-Smith the most highly decorated member of the Australian Defence Force.

title: Ben Roberts-Smith
text: He was presented with the VC by the Governor-General of Australia, Quentin Bryce, at a ceremony in Perth on 23 January 2011.

title: Ben Roberts-Smith
text: He was also later awarded a Commendation for Distinguished Service for his leadership as a patrol commander during a 2012 tour of Afghanistan.

title: Erica Packer
text: Erica Georgia Packer (née Baxter; born 10 November 1977) is an Australian singer and model.

title: Erica Packer
text: She was the second wife of Australia's eighth richest man, James Packer.

title: Crazy John's
text: Crazy John's was a mobile phone retail chain in Australia started by Turkish Australian businessman John Ilhan.

title: Crazy John's
text: Crazy John's was the largest independent phone retailer in Australia, employing more than 400 people with more than 60 retail stores.

title: Crazy John's
text: Following his death in 2007, Ilhan's wife Patricia sold her stake in the company to Vodafone Australia, now a part of Vodafone Hutchison Australia.

title: Crazy John's
text: Originally a dealer of Telstra Mobile, Crazy John's became a Mobile Virtual Network Operator through the Vodafone Australia network, dealing directly with customers and offering its own competitive mobile phone deals and plans.

title: Mırra
text: Mırra is a traditional type of bitter coffee prepared in the Hatay, Adana, Urfa and Mardin provinces of Turkey, as well as in some Arab countries like Lebanon and Syria, which is also sometimes correctly referred to as Arabic coffee because the name is derived from Arabic; "mur" meaning bitter.

title: Mırra
text: Since it is very bitter and dark, it is served in tiny cups without handles similar in size to Italian espresso cups.

title: Mırra
text: The coffee beans for Mırra are common coffea arabica coffee beans, which however are roasted twice in order to give it its bitter taste.They are ground so that they are still grainy, unlike Turkish coffee which is more like a powder.

title: Mırra
text: The coffee is put into a narrow-topped small boiling pot called cezve, and water is added, mostly accompanied by some cardamom in order to give it a more aromatic flavour.

title: Sicko
text: Sicko is a 2007 American documentary film made by filmmaker Michael Moore.

title: Sicko
text: The film investigates health care in the United States, focusing on its health insurance and the pharmaceutical industry.

title: Sicko
text: The movie compares the for-profit, non-universal U.S. system with the non-profit universal health care systems of Canada, the United Kingdom, France and Cuba.

title: Bitter electromagnet
text: A Bitter electromagnet or Bitter solenoid is a type of electromagnet invented in 1933 by American physicist Francis Bitter used in scientific research to create extremely strong magnetic fields. Bitter electromagnets have been used to achieve the strongest continuous manmade magnetic fields on earth (up to 45 teslas - as of 2011).

title: Hollywood Outlaw Movie
text: Hollywood Outlaw, The Unmaking of a Bitter Jester is the director’s cut of the controversial documentary "Bitter Jester" which was buried in 2004 amidst much scandal, never to be seen again.

title: Hollywood Outlaw Movie
text: Directed by, written by, and starring Maija DiGiorgio, this film follows her through the construction and subsequent deconstruction of Bitter Jester, including all of the footage that sparked the scandal leading to blackmail and censorship.

title: Light cavalerie vodka
text: Light cavalerie vodka is a type of bitter.

title: Light cavalerie vodka
text: Specifically a type of Polish bitter known as nalewka, a macerate of herbs and spices in a distilled spirit, in this case vodka.

title: Light cavalerie vodka
text: The family of nalewka for which this belongs is commonly known as "Bitter Drops."

title: Jester
text: A jester, court jester, or fool, was historically an entertainer during the medieval and Renaissance eras who was a member of the household of a nobleman or a monarch employed to entertain him and his guests.

title: Jester
text: A jester was also an itinerant performer who entertained common folk at fairs and markets.

title: Jester
text: Jesters are also modern-day entertainers who resemble their historical counterparts.

title: Zaječická hořká
text: Zaječická hořká (bitter water from Zajecice, administrative part of village Bečov, near Most Northern Bohemia) (German: "Saidschitzer Bitterwasser") is strongly mineralized natural bitter water.

title: Zaječická hořká
text: Known since the 16th century for its purgative and gentle laxative effects.

title: Zaječická hořká
text: Rises from a wells located in the vicinity of Zaječice, Sedlec (part of Korozluky) and Korozluky.

title: Zaječická hořká
text: It ranks among strongly mineralized mineral waters of the Magnesium sulphate type; it is cool, hypertonic, slightly opalescent, yellowish, scent-free, with a strongly bitter flavour.

title: Ratafia
text: Ratafia is a term used for two types of sweet alcoholic beverage, either a fortified wine or a fruit-based beverage.

title: Ratafia
text: The latter type is a liqueur or cordial flavoured with lemon peel, herbs in various amounts (nutmeg, cinnamon, clove, mint, rosemary, anise, etc.) typically combined with sugar.

title: Ratafia
text: It may also be prepared with peach or cherry kernels, bitter almonds, or other fruits, as many different varieties are made.

title: Ratafia
text: The same name is given to a flavouring essence resembling bitter almonds, and also to a light biscuit.

title: Ratafia
text: The former type is a type of "mistelle", a mixture of marc brandy and the unfermented juice of the grape, and it is the type of Ratafia produced in France.

title: Bitter Jester

title: Bitter Jester
text: It's a portrait of the comedy world that includes interviews with a multitude of stars including Richard Pryor, Richard Belzer and many others.

title: Leucopaxillus gentianeus
text: Leucopaxillus gentianeus is a bitter-tasting, inedible mushroom commonly known as the bitter false funnelcap, or the bitter brown leucopaxillus.

title: Leucopaxillus gentianeus
text: A common synonym is "Leucopaxillus amarus".

title: Leucopaxillus gentianeus
text: The bitter taste is caused by a triterpene called cucurbitacin B.

title: Leucopaxillus gentianeus
text: The species was first described in 1873 as "Clitocybe gentianea" by French mycologist Lucien Quélet.

title: Leucopaxillus gentianeus
text: František Kotlaba transferred it to "Leucopaxillus" in 1966.

title: Mayor of Greater Manchester
text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester is a directly elected political post responsible for the strategic government of Greater Manchester, including health, transport, housing, strategic planning, waste management, policing, the Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service and skills.

title: Mayor of Greater Manchester
text: The creation of the Mayor of Greater Manchester was agreed between the then Chancellor of the Exchequer, George Osborne, and Greater Manchester's 10 district council leaders.

title: Mayor of Greater Manchester
text: As well as having specific powers, the Mayor chairs the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, also assuming the powers of the Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner.

title: Mayor of Greater Manchester
text: Tony Lloyd was appointed as Interim Mayor for Greater Manchester on 29 May 2015.

text: It is composed of a bus station, and a single-platform Metrolink light rail station, the latter of which is the terminus of the system's Eccles Line.

title: Eccles Interchange
text: It opened on 21 July 2000.

title: Eccles Interchange
text: It is roughly 310 m away from Eccles railway station.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: The Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner was the police and crime commissioner, an elected official tasked with setting out the way crime is tackled by the Greater Manchester Police in Greater Manchester.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: The post was created on 21 November 2012, following an election held on 15 November 2012, and replaced the Greater Manchester Police Authority.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: Upon the creation of a Mayor of Greater Manchester and the inaugural election to that position, the duties of Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner were absolved into the mayoralty and the office itself abolished.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: For the entirety of its existence, the commissioner was Labour Party politician Tony Lloyd.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: The police and crime commissioner was required to produce a strategic Greater Manchester Police and Crime Plan, setting out the priorities for the Greater Manchester Police, and their work is scrutinised by the Greater Manchester Police and Crime Panel.

title: Greater Manchester Police and Crime Commissioner
text: In November 2014 it was announced that the role would be replaced with a directly elected Mayor of Greater Manchester, and the term of office of the incumbent commissioner was extended to May 2017.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: The Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority (GMITA) was a local government institution responsible for the strategic direction of passenger transport in Greater Manchester.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: It existed from 1969 to 1974 as the SELNEC Passenger Transport Authority and was then replaced by Greater Manchester County Council.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: It was created again in 1986 as the Greater Manchester Passenger Transport Authority.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: It was renamed in 2008 as the Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: Policy of the authority was delivered by the Greater Manchester Passenger Transport Executive.

title: Greater Manchester Integrated Transport Authority
text: It was replaced by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority in 2011.

title: Demography of Greater Manchester
text: The demography of Greater Manchester is analysed by the Office for National Statistics and data is produced for each of its ten metropolitan boroughs, each of the Greater Manchester electoral wards, the NUTS3 statistical sub-regions, each of the Parliamentary constituencies in Greater Manchester, the 15 civil parishes in Greater Manchester, and for all of Greater Manchester as a whole; the latter of which had a population of 2,682,500 at the 2011 UK census.

title: Demography of Greater Manchester
text: Additionally, data is produced for the Greater Manchester Urban Area.

title: Demography of Greater Manchester
text: Statistical information is produced about the size and geographical breakdown of the population, the number of people entering and leaving country and the number of people in each demographic subgroup.

title: Greater Manchester County Council
text: A strategic authority, with responsibilities for public transport, planning, emergency services and waste disposal, it was composed of 106 members drawn from the ten metropolitan boroughs of Greater Manchester.

title: Greater Manchester County Council
text: The Greater Manchester County Council shared power with ten lower-tier district councils, each of which directed local matters.

title: Greater Manchester County Council
text: It was also known as the Greater Manchester Council (GMC) and the Greater Manchester Metropolitan County Council (GMMCC).

title: Transport for Greater Manchester
text: The organisation traces its origins to the Transport Act 1968, when the SELNEC Passenger Transport Executive was established to co-ordinate public transport in and around Manchester.

title: Transport for Greater Manchester
text: Between 1974 and 2011, this body was known as the Greater Manchester Passenger Transport Executive (GMPTE), until a reformation of local government arrangements in Greater Manchester granted the body more powers and prompted a corporate rebranding.

title: Transport for Greater Manchester
text: The strategies and policies of Transport for Greater Manchester are set by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority and its Transport for Greater Manchester Committee.

title: Eric A. Sykes

title: Eric A. Sykes

title: Eric A. Sykes

title: Hot toddy

title: Wassail

title: Christian Bale filmography

title: Christian Bale filmography
text: Bale's role of a young boy, interned in China by the Japanese, received praise from most film critics.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: WWE Extreme Rules (simply known as Extreme Rules) is a professional wrestling event produced annually by WWE, a Connecticut-based promotion, and broadcast live and available only through pay-per-view (PPV) and the WWE Network.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: The name of the event stems from most matches being contested under hardcore wrestling regulations; the defunct Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW) promotion originally used the term to describe the regulations for all of its matches.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: The event name was established in 2009; however, its theme began with its predecessor, One Night Stand, which was promoted in 2005 and 2006 as an ECW reunion show.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: In 2007, WWE promoted the show as one of its own regular PPV events but kept the ECW concept of Extreme Rules matches.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: In 2009, WWE renamed the One Night Stand event to WWE Extreme Rules.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: The 2009 Extreme Rules event was noted by WWE to be a direct continuation of the One Night Stand chronology.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: However, the 2010 event was later promoted as only the second event under a new chronology, one that is no longer a direct continuation of the One Night Stand events.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: Starting in 2010, Extreme Rules was moved from June to late April/early May to replace Backlash as the post-WrestleMania pay-per-view event.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: For 2013, the event was scheduled to take place in mid-May and replace Over the Limit, which was moved to October before being discontinued later that year and replaced by Battleground.

title: WWE Extreme Rules
text: The event will return to the early June slot of WWE's pay-per-view calendar and will be a Raw-exclusive pay-per-view event.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: Roscoe H. Channing, Jr. (January 7, 1868 – April 1, 1961) was an All-American football player, member of the Rough Riders and mining executive.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: Channing was an All-American halfback for Princeton University.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: He was one of eleven players selected by Caspar Whitney for the first ever College Football All-America Team in 1889.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: When the Spanish–American War commenced in 1898, Channing enlisted in Theodore Roosevelt's Rough Riders.

title: Roscoe Channing

title: Roscoe Channing
text: Channing later went into the mining business and managed the mining operations of the Whitney family.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: In the 1920s, he formed a partnership with his friend Cornelius Vanderbilt Whitney.

title: Roscoe Channing
text: The two formed the Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Company in Flin Flon, Saskatchewan, Canada, and Channing served as the company's President.

title: Roscoe Channing

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: Workflow Resource Planning is a new term coined by Charles Lim Chee Pang(the founder of Peliontech) in the year 2003, to name a new class of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Software.

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: Conventional ERP software work in a data entry and processing model.

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: Mr. Charles Lim changed that when he introduced the first WRP software that incorporates workflow functionality into its core design and released this new ERP called Radix ERP.

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: Work flow functionality was not new.

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: Lotus Notes was the pioneer of workflow systems until it went out of favor in early 2000.

title: Workflow Resource Planning
text: From the designs of Lotus Notes, Mr. Charles combined the idea into ERP systems and created Radix WRP, a new class of ERP system with workflow manageability.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: An NTFS symbolic link (symlink) is a filesystem object in the NTFS filesystem that points to another filesystem object.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: The object being pointed to is called the target.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: Symbolic links should be transparent to users; the links appear as normal files or directories, and can be acted upon by the user or application in exactly the same manner.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: Symbolic links to directories or volumes, called junction points and mount points, were introduced with NTFS 3.0 that shipped with Windows 2000.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: From NTFS 3.1 onwards, symbolic links can be created for any kind of file system object.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: NTFS 3.1 was introduced together with Windows XP, but the functionality was not made available (through ntfs.sys) to user mode applications.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: Third-party filter drivers such as Masatoshi Kimura's opensource codice_1 driver could however be installed to make the feature available in user mode as well.

title: NTFS symbolic link
text: The ntfs.sys released with Windows Vista made the functionality available to user mode applications by default.

title: Jens Ritter Instruments

title: Jens Ritter Instruments

title: Jens Ritter Instruments

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: Bio-inspired robotic locomotion is a fairly new subcategory of bio-inspired design.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: It is about learning concepts from nature and applying them to the design of real-world engineered systems.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: More specifically, this field is about making robots that are inspired by biological systems.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: Biomimicry and bio-inspired design are sometimes confused.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: Biomimicry is copying the nature while bio-inspired design is learning from nature and making a mechanism that is simpler and more effective than the system observed in nature.

title: Bio-inspired robotics

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: The biological systems have been optimized for specific tasks according to their habitat.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: However, they are multifunctional and are not designed for only one specific functionality.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: Bio-inspired robotics is about studying biological systems, and look for the mechanisms that may solve a problem in the engineering field.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: The designer should then try to simplify and enhance that mechanism for the specific task of interest.

title: Bio-inspired robotics
text: Bio-inspired roboticists are usually interested in biosensors (e.g. eye), bioactuators (e.g. muscle), or biomaterials (e.g. spider silk).

title: Functionality doctrine
text: In United States trademark law, the functionality doctrine prevents manufacturers from protecting specific features of a product by means of trademark law.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: There are two branches of the functionality doctrine: utilitarian functionality and aesthetic functionality.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: The rationale behind functionality doctrine is that product markets would not be truly competitive if newcomers could not make a product with a feature that consumers demand.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: Utilitarian functionality provides grounds to deny federal trademark protection to product features which do something useful.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: Patent law, not trademark, protects useful processes, machines, and material inventions. Patented designs are presumed to be functional until proven otherwise.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: Aesthetic functionality provides grounds to deny trademark protection to design features which are included to make the product more aesthetically appealing and commercially desirable.

title: Functionality doctrine
text: Aesthetic features are within the purview of copyright law, which provides protection to creative and original works of authorship.

title: Extensibility
text: Extensibility is a software engineering and systems design principle where the implementation takes future growth into consideration.

title: Extensibility
text: The term extensibility can also be seen as a systemic measure of the ability to extend a system and the level of effort required to implement the extension.

title: Extensibility
text: Extensions can be through the addition of new functionality or through modification of existing functionality.

title: Extensibility
text: The central theme is to provide for change – typically enhancements – while minimizing impact to existing system functions.

title: Extensibility
text: An extensible system is one whose internal structure and data flow are minimally or not affected by new or modified functionality, for example recompiling or changing the original source code might be unnecessary when changing a system’s behavior, either by the creator or other programmers.

title: Extensibility
text: Because software systems are long lived and will be modified for new features and added functionalities demanded by users, extensibility enables developers to expand or add to the software’s capabilities and facilitates systematic reuse.

title: Extensibility
text: Some of its approaches include facilities for allowing users’ own program routines to be inserted and the abilities to define new data types as well as to define new formatting markup tags.

title: ProPhoto RGB color space
text: The ProPhoto RGB color space, also known as ROMM RGB (Reference Output Medium Metric), is an output referred RGB color space developed by Kodak.

title: ProPhoto RGB color space
text: It offers an especially large gamut designed for use with photographic output in mind.

title: ProPhoto RGB color space
text: The ProPhoto RGB color space encompasses over 90% of possible surface colors in the CIE L*a*b* color space, and 100% of likely occurring real-world surface colors documented by Pointer in 1980, making ProPhoto even larger than the Wide-gamut RGB color space.

title: ProPhoto RGB color space
text: The ProPhoto RGB primaries were also chosen in order to minimize hue rotations associated with non-linear tone scale operations.

title: ProPhoto RGB color space
text: One of the downsides to this color space is that approximately 13% of the representable colors are imaginary colors that do not exist and are not visible colors.

title: YCoCg
text: The YCoCg color model is the color space formed from a simple transformation of an associated RGB color space into a "luma" value (denoted as Y) and two "chroma" values called "chrominance green" (Cg) and "chrominance orange" (Co).

title: YCoCg
text: It is supported in video and image compression designs such as H.264/MPEG-4 AVC, HEVC, JPEG XR, and Dirac, since it is simple to compute, has good transform coding gain, and can be losslessly converted to and from RGB with fewer bits than are needed with other color models.

title: Blue
text: Blue is the colour between violet and green on the spectrum of visible light.

title: Blue
text: Human eyes perceive blue when observing light with a wavelength between 450 and 495 nanometres. Blues with a higher frequency and thus a shorter wavelength appear more violet, while those with a lower frequency and a longer wavelength gradually appear more green.

title: Blue
text: Pure blue, in the middle, has a wavelength of 470 nanometres.

title: Blue
text: In painting and traditional colour theory, blue is one of the three primary colours of pigments, along with red and yellow, which can be mixed to form a wide gamut of colours.

title: Blue
text: Red and blue mixed together form violet, blue and yellow together form green.

title: Blue
text: Blue is also a primary colour in the RGB colour model, used to create all the colours on the screen of a television or computer monitor.

title: Color space
text: A color space is a specific organization of colors.

title: Color space
text: In combination with physical device profiling, it allows for reproducible representations of color, in both analog and digital representations.

title: Color space
text: A color space may be arbitrary, with particular colors assigned to a set of physical color swatches and corresponding assigned names or numbers such as with the Pantone collection, or structured mathematically, as with NCS System, Adobe RGB or sRGB.

title: Color space
text: A color model is an abstract mathematical model describing the way colors can be represented as tuples of numbers (e.g. triples in RGB or quadruples in CMYK); however, a color model with no associated mapping function to an absolute color space is a more or less arbitrary color system with no connection to any globally understood system of color interpretation.

title: Color space
text: Adding a specific mapping function between a color model and a reference color space establishes within the reference color space a definite "footprint", known as a gamut, and for a given color model this defines a color space.

title: Color space
text: For example, Adobe RGB and sRGB are two different absolute color spaces, both based on the RGB color model.

title: Color space
text: When defining a color space, the usual reference standard is the CIELAB or CIEXYZ color spaces, which were specifically designed to encompass all colors the average human can see.

title: HCL color space
text: HCL is designed to have characteristics of both cylindrical translations of RGB color space such as HSL and HSV and L*a*b* color space.

title: HCL color space
text: HSL and HSV color spaces have the benefit of being perceptually uniform translations of the RGB color space, but their luminance variation does not match the way humans perceive color.

title: HCL color space
text: Perceptually uniform translations of RGB colorspace do have the benefit of outperforming RGB in cases such as high noise environments.

title: HCL color space
text: L*a*b colorspace does correspond to the three channels of human perception, but have poor hue constancy, especially in the blue range.

title: RGBA color space
text: RGBA stands for red green blue alpha.

title: RGBA color space
text: While it is sometimes described as a color space, it is actually simply a use of the RGB color model, with extra alpha channel information.

title: RGBA color space
text: The color is RGB, and may belong to any RGB color space, but an integral alpha value as invented by Catmull and Smith between 1971 and 1972 enables alpha compositing.

title: RGBA color space
text: The inventors named alpha after the Greek letter in the classic linear interpolation formula "α" "A" + (1 − "α") "B" .

title: Brown
text: Brown is a composite color.

title: Brown
text: In the CMYK color model used in printing or painting, brown is made by combining red, black, and yellow, or red, yellow, and blue.

title: Brown
text: In the RGB color model used to project colors onto television screens and computer monitors, brown is made by combining red and green, in specific proportions.

title: Brown
text: The brown color is seen widely in nature, in wood, soil, human hair color, eye color and skin pigmentation.

title: Brown
text: Brown is the color of dark wood or rich soil.

title: Brown
text: According to public opinion surveys in Europe and the United States, brown is the least favorite color of the public; the color most often associated with plainness, the rustic, feces, and poverty.

title: RGB color model
text: The RGB color model is an additive color model in which red, green and blue light are added together in various ways to reproduce a broad array of colors.

title: RGB color model
text: The name of the model comes from the initials of the three additive primary colors, red, green, and blue.

title: RGB color space
text: An RGB color space is any additive color space based on the RGB color model.

title: RGB color space
text: A particular RGB color space is defined by the three chromaticities of the red, green, and blue additive primaries, and can produce any chromaticity that is the triangle defined by those primary colors.

title: RGB color space
text: The complete specification of an RGB color space also requires a white point chromaticity and a gamma correction curve.

title: RGB color space
text: As of 2007, sRGB is by far the most commonly used RGB color space.
