title: Miss Nepal 2015
text: Similarly, Dibyata Vaidya was declared the 1st runner up as Miss Nepal Earth 2015 sent to Miss Earth 2015 and Medha Koirala was the 2nd runner up as Miss Nepal International 2015 sent to Miss International 2015.

title: 2015 Nepal Premier League
text: The 2015 Nepal Premier League (Everest Premier League) was supposed to be the second edition of the Nepal Premier League.

title: 2015 Nepal Premier League
text: Also known as Wai Wai Nepal Premier League, the Twenty20 format was supposed to be held in 2015 in Kathmandu.

title: 2015 Nepal Premier League
text: Initially it was scheduled to be held from 26 March to 4 April 2015 but Cricket Association of Nepal insisted that it will not support NPL unless its name is changed.

title: 2015 Nepal Premier League
text: Later the board decided to support NPL and provided the ground for the competition.

title: 2015 Nepal Premier League
text: The name has been changed into Everest Premier League and is re-scheduled from 24 September to 3 October 2016.

text: Hidden Treasures Fanta Miss Nepal 2013, the 18th Miss Nepal beauty pageant, was held on March 20, 2013 at the Nepal Academy Hall in Kathmandu.

text: Miss Nepal 2012 Shristi Shrestha crowned her successor Ishani Shrestha as Miss Nepal World 2013, who represented Nepal at Miss World 2013 with Rojisha Shahi as Miss Nepal Earth 2013 and was sent to Miss Earth 2013, and Shritima Shah as Miss Nepal International 2013 to Miss International 2013.

title: Miss Nepal 2012
text: Hidden Treasures Miss Nepal 2012, the 18th Miss Nepal beauty pageant, was held on May 6, 2012 at the Hotel Del Annapurna in Kathmandu.

title: Miss Nepal 2012
text: Miss Nepal 2011 Malina Joshi crowned Shristi Shrestha as Miss Nepal World 2012, who represented Nepal at Miss World 2012 with Nagma Shrestha and Subekshya Khadka crowned as Miss Nepal Earth 2012 and Miss Nepal International 2012 who went to Miss Earth 2012 and Miss International 2012 respectively.

title: 1984 South Asian Games
text: The 1984 South Asian Games (or 1st SAF Games) was the first edition of South Asian Games.

title: 1984 South Asian Games
text: It was held in Kathmandu, Nepal from September 17 to 23, 1984.

title: Bhadrabas
text: Bhadrabas is a village development committee in Kathmandu District in the Bagmati Zone of central Nepal, located approximately 15 km northeast of Kathmandu.

title: Bhadrabas
text: At the time of the 2011 Nepal census it had a population of 2,388 and had 503 houses in it.

title: Bhadrabas
text: The oldest high school in the eastern Kathmandu Valley, Adarsh Uchha Madhayamik Vidhalaya is located in Bhadrabas.

title: Bhadrabas
text: The Nepal Red Cross Society is active in Bhadrabas and it has notable health centre.

title: Bhadrabas
text: In 1984, a tobacco smoking World Health Organization questionnaire was given to the inhabitants of Bhadrabas to survey smoking trends in the country.

title: Julian Bolling
text: Julian Bolling (June 19, 1966) is a Sri Lankan medal winning swimmer who has represented his country at numerous international competitions.

title: Julian Bolling
text: He has won 15 gold medals for Sri Lanka at South Asian Games between 1984 to 1991.

title: Julian Bolling
text: He also represented Sri Lanka at the three Olympic games, firstly at Los Angeles (USA) in 1984, then at Seoul (South Korea) in 1988, and finally at Barcelona (Spain) in 1992.

title: Julian Bolling
text: He is the son of Tara Bolling and cousin of Dipika Chanmugam, both of whom have represented Sri Lanka internationally.

title: Julian Bolling
text: Bolling's best performance at an international meet was at the Colombo South Asian Games where he won six Gold medals.

title: Julian Bolling
text: His record was unbeaten until 2016 when Mathew Abeysinghe broke the record by winning 7 Golds in India.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: The Queen's Body Guard of the Yeomen of the Guard are a bodyguard of the British Monarch.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: The oldest British military corps still in existence, it was created by King Henry VII in 1485 at the Battle of Bosworth.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: As a token of this venerability, the Yeomen still wear red and gold uniforms of Tudor style.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: There are 60 Yeomen of the Guard (plus six officers), drawn from retired members of the British Army, Royal Marines and Royal Air Force, but traditionally not the Royal Navy.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: This ban on Royal Navy Personnel was lifted in 2011 and two sailors joined the ranks of the Yeomen of the Guard.

title: Yeomen of the Guard
text: However, the role of the Captain of the Queen's Body Guard of the Yeomen of the Guard is a political appointment — the captain is always the government Deputy Chief Whip in the House of Lords.

title: George Percy, 5th Duke of Northumberland
text: George Percy, 5th Duke of Northumberland PC (22 June 1778 – 22 August 1867), styled Lord Lovaine between 1790 and 1830 and known as The Earl of Beverley between 1830 and 1865, was a British Tory politician.

title: George Percy, 5th Duke of Northumberland
text: He served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard under Sir Robert Peel between 1842 and 1846.

title: George Percy, 5th Duke of Northumberland
text: He succeeded to the title on 12 February 1865, after the death of Algernon Percy, 4th Duke of Northumberland whose wife Eleanor Percy, Duchess of Northumberland had borne no children.

title: Henry Cadogan, 4th Earl Cadogan
text: Henry Charles Cadogan, 4th Earl Cadogan PC (15 February 1812 – 8 June 1873), styled Viscount Chelsea between 1820 and 1864, was a British diplomat and Conservative politician.

title: Henry Cadogan, 4th Earl Cadogan
text: He served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard between 1866 and 1868.

title: Henry Fox-Strangways, 3rd Earl of Ilchester
text: Henry Stephen Fox-Strangways, 3rd Earl of Ilchester PC (21 February 1787 – 8 January 1858), styled Lord Stavordale from birth until 1802, was a British peer and Whig politician.

title: Henry Fox-Strangways, 3rd Earl of Ilchester
text: He served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard under Lord Melbourne from 1835 to 1841.

title: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury
text: Robert Arthur Talbot Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (3 February 183022 August 1903), styled Lord Robert Cecil before 1865 and Viscount Cranborne from June 1865 until April 1868, was a British Conservative statesman, serving as prime minister three times for a total of over 13 years.

title: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury
text: He was the last prime minister to head his full administration from the House of Lords.

title: William Monson, 1st Viscount Oxenbridge
text: William John Monson, 1st Viscount Oxenbridge PC (18 February 1829 – 16 April 1898), known as The Lord Monson between 1862 and 1886, was a British Liberal politician.

title: William Monson, 1st Viscount Oxenbridge
text: He served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard between 1880 and 1885 and in 1886 under William Ewart Gladstone.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: Baron Berkeley of Stratton, in the County of Cornwall, was a title in the Peerage of England.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: It was created in 1658 for John Berkeley, 1st Baron Berkeley of Stratton, a Royalist supporter during the English Civil War, of the Bruton branch of the Berkeley family.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: He was a descendant of Sir Maurice de Berkeley (14th century), younger son of Maurice de Berkeley, 2nd Baron Berkeley (see Baron Berkeley).

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: Charles Berkeley, 2nd Viscount Fitzhardinge, was his brother and Charles Berkeley, 1st Earl of Falmouth, his nephew.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: Lord Berkeley of Stratton's second son, the third Baron (who succeeded his elder brother), was an Admiral in the Royal Navy.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: He died without surviving children and was succeeded by his younger brother, the fourth Baron.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: He was a politician and served as First Lord of Trade between 1714 and 1715.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: On his death the title passed to his eldest son, the fifth Baron.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: He was also a politician and held office as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard and Captain of the Honourable Corps of Gentlemen-Pensioners.

title: Baron Berkeley of Stratton
text: He was childless and the title became extinct on his death in 1775.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: Earl of Aylesford, in the County of Kent, is a title in the Peerage of Great Britain.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: It was created in 1714 for the lawyer and politician Heneage Finch, 1st Baron Guernsey.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: He had already been created Baron Guernsey in the Peerage of England in 1703.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: Finch was the younger son of Heneage Finch, 1st Earl of Nottingham and the great-grandson of Elizabeth Heneage, 1st Countess of Winchilsea.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: Lord Aylesford's eldest son, the second Earl, represented Maidstone and Surrey in Parliament.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: In 1712, he married Mary Fisher, daughter of Sir Clement Fisher, 3rd Baronet.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: Through this marriage Packington Hall in Warwickshire came into the Finch family.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: Their son, the third Earl, sat as a Member of Parliament for Leicestershire and Maidstone.

title: Earl of Aylesford
text: His eldest son, the fourth Earl, represented Castle Rising and Maidstone in the House of Commons, and after entering the House of Lords on his father's death, served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard from 1783 to 1804 and as Lord Steward of the Household from 1804 to 1812.

title: William Street, Limerick
text: William Street (Irish: "Sráid Liam" ) is one of the main thoroughfares of central Limerick City, Ireland.

title: William Street, Limerick
text: The street starts at a junction with O'Connell Street (Limerick's main thoroughfare) and continues in a south-east direction.

title: William Street, Limerick
text: The street is named after William Pery, 1st Baron Glentworth a relation of Edmund Sexton Pery who is credited with the development of the present day Limerick City Centre area known as Newtown Pery.

title: William Pery, 3rd Earl of Limerick
text: William Hale John Charles Pery, 3rd Earl of Limerick KP, PC, DL, JP (17 January 1840 – 8 August 1896), styled Viscount Glentworth until 1866, was an Irish peer and Conservative politician.

title: William Pery, 3rd Earl of Limerick
text: He served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard under Lord Salisbury between 1889 and 1892 and again between 1895 and his death in 1896.

title: William Pery, 3rd Earl of Limerick
text: In 1892 he was made a Knight of the Order of St Patrick.

title: Calcedonio Di Pisa
text: Calcedonio Di Pisa (October 11, 1931 in Palermo – December 26, 1962 in Palermo), also known as Doruccio, was a member of the Sicilian Mafia.

title: Calcedonio Di Pisa
text: He was the boss of the Mafia family in the Noce neighbourhood in Palermo and sat on the first Sicilian Mafia Commission, the coordinating body of Cosa Nostra in Sicily.

title: Antonio Rotolo
text: Antonino "Nino" Rotolo (born January 3, 1946) is an Italian Mafia boss from the Pagliarelli area in Palermo that traditionally was under the control of the Motisi Mafia family.

title: Antonio Rotolo
text: Rotolo was the underboss of Matteo Motisi, but according to some pentiti he was the "de facto" leader representing the mandamento on the Sicilian Mafia Commission.

title: Antonio Rotolo

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Dinosaur behavior is difficult for paleontologists to study since much of paleontology is dependent solely on the physical remains of ancient life.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: However, trace fossils and paleopathology can give insight into dinosaur behavior.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Interpretations of dinosaur behavior are generally based on the pose of body fossils and their habitat, computer simulations of their biomechanics, and comparisons with modern animals in similar ecological niches.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: As such, the current understanding of dinosaur behavior relies on speculation, and will likely remain controversial for the foreseeable future.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: However, there is general agreement that some behaviors which are common in crocodiles and birds, dinosaurs' closest living relatives, were also common among dinosaurs.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Gregarious behavior was common in many dinosaur species.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Dinosaurs may have congregated in herds for defense, for migratory purposes, or to provide protection for their young.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: There is evidence that many types of dinosaurs, including various theropods, sauropods, ankylosaurians, ornithopods, and ceratopsians, formed aggregations of immature individuals.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Nests and eggs have been found for most major groups of dinosaurs, and it appears likely that dinosaurs communicated with their young, in a manner similar to modern birds and crocodiles.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: The crests and frills of some dinosaurs, like the marginocephalians, theropods and lambeosaurines, may have been too fragile to be used for active defense, and so they were likely used for sexual or aggressive displays, though little is known about dinosaur mating and territorialism.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: Most dinosaurs seem to have relied on land-based locomotion.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: A good understanding of how dinosaurs moved on the ground is key to models of dinosaur behavior; the science of biomechanics, in particular, has provided significant insight in this area.

title: Dinosaur behavior
text: For example, studies of the forces exerted by muscles and gravity on dinosaurs' skeletal structure have investigated how fast dinosaurs could run, whether diplodocids could create sonic booms via whip-like tail snapping, and whether sauropods could float.

title: Battle of Silda
text: Battle of Silda ("Affæren ved Silden" or "Affæren ved Stadt") was a naval battle fought on 23 July 1810 between the United Kingdom and Denmark–Norway near the Norwegian island of Silda in Sogn og Fjordane county.

title: Battle of Silda
text: The battle occurred during the Gunboat War, itself part of the Napoleonic Wars.

title: Battle of Silda

title: Battle of Silda

title: Battle of Calabria
text: The Battle of Calabria, (known to the Italian Navy as the Battle of Punta Stilo) was a naval battle during the Battle of the Mediterranean in the Second World War.

title: Battle of Calabria
text: It was fought between the Italian Royal Navy ("Regia Marina") and the British Royal Navy and the Royal Australian Navy.

title: Battle of Calabria
text: The battle occurred 30 miles to the east of Punta Stilo, Calabria, on 9 July 1940.

title: Battle of Calabria
text: It was one of the few pitched battles of the Mediterranean campaign during the Second World War involving large numbers of ships on both sides.

title: Battle of Calabria
text: Both sides claimed victory, but in fact the battle was a draw and everyone returned to their bases as soon as possible.

title: Battle of the Burbia River
text: The Battle of Río Burbia or the Battle of the Burbia River was a battle fought in the year 791 between the troops of the Kingdom of Asturias, commanded by King Bermudo I of Asturias, and the troops of the Emirate of Córdoba, led by Yusuf ibn Bujt.

title: Battle of the Burbia River
text: The battle occurred in the context of the Ghazws of Hisham I against the Christian rebels of the northern Iberian Peninsula.

title: Battle of the Burbia River
text: The battle took place near the Río Burbia, in the area which is today known as Villafranca del Bierzo.

title: Battle of the Burbia River
text: The battle resulted in Andalusian victory.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: The Battle of Manilla (1574) was a battle in the Manila area mainly in the location of what is now Parañaque between Chinese pirates, led by Limahong and the Spanish colonial forces and their native allies.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: The battle occurred on November 29, 1574 when Limahong's fleet landed in the town of Parañaque and from there, began to assault the fortifications of Intramuros.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: Initially, the inhabitants where disorganized and Limahong's forces routed them.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: Furthermore, the Chinese killed the Master-of-Camp of the Spanish, Martin De Goiti.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: This caused them to delay their assault on Manila as Martin de Goiti's house was an obstacle in their march.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: However, upon the arrival of a certain Filipino hero called, Galo, resistance started to organize.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: Under Galo's command, they were able to resist China-born Limahong until Mexico-born Juan de Salcedo arrived from Ilocos with 300 Ilocano Warriors and Limahong was defeated and eventually forced to retreat.

title: Battle of Manila (1574)
text: Thereafter Limahong abandoned his plans to invade Manila and instead, set up a temporary kingdom in Pangasinan.

title: Battle of Klushino
text: The Battle of Klushino, or the Battle of Kłuszyn, was fought on 4 July 1610, between forces of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland and the Tsardom of Russia during the Polish–Muscovite War, part of Russia's Time of Troubles.

title: Battle of Klushino
text: The battle occurred near the village of Klushino (Polish: "Kłuszyn" ) near Smolensk (Polish: "Smoleńsk").

title: Battle of Klushino
text: In the battle the outnumbered Polish force secured a decisive victory over Russia, due to the tactical competence of hetman Stanisław Żółkiewski and the military prowess of Polish hussars, the elite of the army of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland.

title: Battle of Klushino
text: The battle is remembered as one of the greatest triumphs of the Polish cavalry and an example of excellence and supremacy of the Polish military at the time.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: The Battle of Alhandic (Spanish: "Batalla de Alhandic" ), also known as Zamora's trench Battle ("Batalla del Foso de Zamora"), was a battle that occurred on August 5, 939 in the city of Zamora, Spain.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: The battle occurred when the troops of Abd-ar-Rahman III assaulted the walls of Zamora.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: The defending troops were those loyal to Ramiro II of León, King of the Kingdom of Leon.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: The fighting was so bloody that the tide of the battle did not turn until the ditch surrounding the city walls was entirely filled with corpses.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: The troops of Aberraman III won the day and were able to seize the city of Zamora.

title: Battle of Alhandic
text: This battle should not be confused with the Day of Zamora ("Día de Zamora" or "Jornada del Foso de Zamora") which took place a few decades before in the year 901.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: The Battle of Manila (February 3, 1945 – March 3, 1945) was a major battle of the Philippine campaign of 1944-45, during the Second World War.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: It was fought by American and Filipino forces against Japanese troops in Manila, the capital city of the Philippines.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: The month-long battle, which resulted in the death of over 100,000 civilians and the complete devastation of the city, was the scene of the worst urban fighting in the Pacific theater.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: Japanese forces committed mass murder against Filipino civilians during the battle.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: Along with massive loss of life, the battle also destroyed architectural and cultural heritage dating back to the city's foundation.

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: The battle ended the almost three years of Japanese military occupation in the Philippines (1942–1945).

title: Battle of Manila (1945)
text: The city's capture was marked as General Douglas MacArthur's key to victory in the campaign of reconquest.

title: Battle of Yao (Japan)
text: The Battle of Yao (Japanese: 八尾の戦い , Hepburn: Yao no tatakai ) was a confrontation that took place in 1615 during the early Edo period in Japan.

title: Battle of Yao (Japan)
text: The battle occurred in 1615 during the Siege of Osaka, in which Tokugawa Ieyasu planned to destroy the Toyotomi clan.

title: Battle of Yao (Japan)
text: It was fought between the Tōdō clan and the Chosokabe clan.

title: Battle of Yao (Japan)
text: There is not much detail about the battle, but it is known that the Tõdõ clan was led by Tōdō Takatora, who won the battle, forcing the Chosokabe clan, led by Chōsokabe Morichika, to retreat to Osaka.

title: Battle of Yao (Japan)
text: Though Takatora won the battle, his two sons were died in combat.

title: Battle of Guam (1944)
text: The Second Battle of Guam (21 July – 10 August 1944) was the American recapture of the Japanese-held island of Guam, a U.S. territory in the Mariana Islands captured by the Japanese from the U.S. in the 1941 First Battle of Guam during the Pacific campaign of World War II.

title: Battle of Aspromonte
text: The Battle of Aspromonte, also known as The Day of Aspromonte (in Italian: "La Giornata dell'Aspromonte"), was a battle that took place on 29 August 1862, and was an inconclusive episode of the Italian unification process.

title: Battle of Aspromonte
text: The battle is named after the mountain Aspromonte in southern Italy, which is near the place where the battle occurred.

title: Battle of Aspromonte
text: In the battle, the Royal Italian Army defeated Giuseppe Garibaldi's army of volunteers, who were marching from Sicily towards Rome, with the intent of annexing it into the Kingdom of Italy.

title: Battle of Aspromonte
text: In the battle, which took place a few kilometers from Gambarie, Garibaldi was wounded and taken as prisoner.

title: Steve Malzberg
text: Stephen D. Malzberg (born April 20, 1959) is an American television and radio host, syndicated columnist, and political commentator.

title: Steve Malzberg
text: He is the host of "The Steve Malzberg Show", a cable news and opinion show on Newsmax TV.

title: Steve Malzberg
text: He has also hosted "The Steve Malzberg Show" on various talk radio outlets.

title: Sean Hannity
text: Sean Patrick Hannity (born December 30, 1961) is an American talk show host, author, and conservative political commentator.

title: Sean Hannity
text: Hannity is the host of "The Sean Hannity Show", a nationally syndicated talk radio show.

title: Sean Hannity
text: He also hosts a cable news show, "Hannity", on Fox News Channel.

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: The 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team represented the University of Virginia in the 2009 NCAA Division I FBS football season as a member of the Coastal Division of the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC).

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: The Cavaliers were led by ninth-year head coach Al Groh.

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: The previous season, Groh fired his offensive coordinator, his son Mike Groh, and replaced him with Gregg Brandon, who had himself been fired as the head coach at Bowling Green.

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: Brandon installed the spread offense at Virginia.

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: The Cavaliers finished the season 3–9, 2–6 in conference play and failed to qualify for a bowl game.

title: 2009 Virginia Cavaliers football team
text: Following the conclusion of the season Virginia dismissed Al Groh as head coach and hired Mike London as his replacement.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: Phillip Reginald "Reggie" Witherspoon (born February 21, 1961) is the head coach of the Canisius College men's basketball team and the former head coach of the University at Buffalo men's college basketball team.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: He was fired after the 2012-13 season.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: He was the head coach at Erie Community College, and head coach and assistant coach at Sweet Home High School before he was hired as the interim head coach at Buffalo in December 1999.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: Witherspoon was named full-time head coach on March 10, 2000.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: He was the first African American named head coach of a varsity sports team in any Western New York suburban school district.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: Witherspoon served one season as an assistant at Alabama under head coach Anthony Grant.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: In 2015, Witherspoon was let go by Alabama when Grant was replaced by Avery Johnson.

title: Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)
text: He was subsequently named as an assistant on Matt McCall's staff at UT-Chattanooga.

title: 2006 Miami Hurricanes football team
text: The 2006 Miami Hurricanes football team represented the University of Miami during the 2006 NCAA Division I FBS football season.

title: 2006 Miami Hurricanes football team
text: The team's head coach was Larry Coker.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: Robert Bower "Buzz" Peterson, Jr. (born May 17, 1963) is an American college basketball coach.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: Most recently, Peterson was the head coach of the UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball team.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: He was fired by UNC Wilmington at the conclusion of the 2014 season.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: Peterson was the head coach of the Tennessee Volunteers basketball team for four years before being fired in 2005.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: He previously coached a second stint at Appalachian State—he coached the 2009–10 Mountaineers, as well as the 1996 to 2000 squads.

title: Buzz Peterson
text: Previously, he was the men's basketball head coach at the University of Tulsa and at Coastal Carolina University, a position he held until mid-2007, when he left the program to be executive (Director of Player Personnel) with the Charlotte Bobcats of the NBA.

title: Larry Coker
text: Larry Edward Coker (born June 23, 1948) is an American football coach and former player.

title: Larry Coker
text: From 2001 to 2006, Coker served as the head coach at the University of Miami.

title: Larry Coker
text: His 2001 Miami team was named the consensus national champion after an undefeated season that culminated with a victory in the Rose Bowl over Nebraska.

title: Larry Coker
text: In the process of winning the championship, Coker became the 2nd head coach since 1948 to win the national championship in his first season.

title: Larry Coker
text: (Bennie Oosterbaan from the University of Michigan and Dennis Erickson of Miami were the last 2 head coaches to accomplish this feat.)

title: Larry Coker
text: Coker was fired by Miami on November 24, 2006 following his sixth loss that season.

title: Larry Coker
text: After a stint as a television analyst for ESPNU, Coker was announced as the head coach for UTSA, whose Roadrunners football team began play in 2011.

title: Larry Coker
text: Coker resigned as UTSA coach on January 5, 2016.

title: Holly Bruder
text: Holly Bruder is an American college softball coach.

title: Holly Bruder
text: She currently serves as head coach of NCAA Division I Lamar University softball team.

title: Holly Bruder
text: She has been head coach as Lamar since the program was restarted in 2012.

title: Holly Bruder
text: From 2008 to 2011, she served as head coach at NCAA Division I Morehead State.

title: Holly Bruder
text: Prior to the seasons at Morehead State, she served as head coach at NCAA Division III Denison University for six years (2002–2007).

title: Holly Bruder
text: Before her head coaching assignments, Bruder was assistant coach at Bluffton College in 2001 after beginning her college coaching career as an assistant coach at Albion College (1999–2000).

title: 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team
text: The 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team represented the University of Alabama for the 2006 NCAA Division I FBS football season trying to improve from a 10–2 record in the 2005 season.

title: 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team
text: The Tide was led by head coach Mike Shula entering his fourth year at Alabama.

title: 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team
text: Despite a strong 5–2 start, they finished out the season by losing four of their final five games.

title: 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team
text: The team closed the regular season at 6–6 (4–4, SEC) and lost for a fifth-straight time to rival Auburn.

title: 2006 Alabama Crimson Tide football team
text: Following the loss Shula was fired as head coach and defensive coordinator Joe Kines served as interim head coach for the bowl game.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: The Maggie Dixon Division I Rookie Coach of the Year Award is an award given annually since 2007 to thehead coach in women's college basketball in the NCAA Division I competition who achieves great success in their first year as a Division I head coach.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: Given by the Women's Basketball Coaches Association (WBCA), the award is named for former women's head coach Maggie Dixon, who coached at Army for the 2005–06 season before suddenly dying due to valve complications from an enlarged heart.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: Dixon had been named head coach just 11 days before the start of the season but led the Black Knights to a 20–11 record and won the Patriot League tournament championship.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: It was Army's first basketball team, men or women, to play in the NCAA Tournament.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: Although Army would lose in the first round to Tennessee, Dixon was named the Patriot League Coach of the Year and received much praise from the college basketball community for her coaching job in just her first season.

title: Maggie Dixon Award
text: On April 6, 2006, Dixon died at the age of 28 to what her brother, Pitt men's head coach Jamie Dixon, described as an "arrhythmic episode to her heart."

title: Brian Knorr
text: Brian Knorr (born December 20, 1963) is a college football coach.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He was most recently the defensive coordinator for the Indiana Hoosiers football team.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He graduated from the Air Force Academy and played quarterback.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He also was an assistant at the Air Force Academy when he went to Ohio University with Jim Grobe.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He was the head coach of the Ohio Bobcats program from 2001 to 2004.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He was fired on November 18, 2004, after he compiled an 11–35 (.239) record in four seasons.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He was replaced by the more successful Frank Solich.

title: Brian Knorr
text: He previously served as a defensive coordinator under the previous head coach, Grobe.

title: Brian Knorr
text: His best season came in 2004, when his team went 4–7, including 2–6 in conference play.

title: Brian Knorr
text: Until February 2008 he served as an assistant head coach at the Air Force Academy under head coach Troy Calhoun.

title: Brian Knorr
text: In 2008, he accepted a position that will reunite him with Grobe at Wake Forest University.

title: Brian Knorr
text: In January, 2016, Knorr did not have his contract renewed by Indiana.

title: Richard Jacob
text: Richard L. Jacob Ph.D. (born September 24, 1958, in Niagara Falls, New York), is a sports coach and educator.

title: Richard Jacob
text: He was head coach of Buffalo's Professional Basketball Team Buffalo Rapids from 2005 through 2006.

title: Richard Jacob
text: He left the position in November 2006 to become the interim Chairman of the Business Department Medaille College.

title: Richard Jacob
text: He currently is an associate professor of Sport and Business at Medaille and is the head of the college's Sport Management program.

title: Richard Jacob
text: He was named the General Manager and Head Coach of the new Buffalo Sharks team in 2008, before that team closed and moved to the Premier Basketball League.

title: Richard Jacob
text: Jacob was then named the head coach for the Buffalo Stampede, but soon resigned for personal reasons.

title: Richard Jacob
text: He formerly coached at Niagara University, Niagara County Community College, the University at Buffalo, Villa Maria College, Daemen College, Buffalo State College, and Medaille.

title: Nikola Mladenov
text: Nikola Mladenov (Macedonian: Никола Младенов ; 10 March 1964 – 26 March 2013) was a Macedonian journalist, actor, founder and managing editor of the weekly newspaper "Fokus", widely regarded as one of the most reputable journalists in Macedonia, who along with his colleagues from the newspaper "Mlad borec" is considered to have laid the basis for the pluralistic principles in the Macedonian journalism.

title: Nikola Mladenov
text: The "Award for best research story of the year – Nikola Mladenov", which is awarded by the Macedonian Institute for Media, is named after him.

text: Tea Moderna (Macedonian: Теа Модерна ) is a Macedonian woman's weekly magazine women.

text: The magazine was started in 2003.

title: Hänt Bild
text: It is part of Aller Media AB.

title: Hänt Bild
text: It is published on a weekly basis.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: Per "Henrik" Dorsin (born 20 November 1977) is a Swedish actor, comedian, singer and revue-artist.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: Dorsin started his career as an extra in the 1995 film Vinterviken.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: He started his television career in the satire-show Detta har hänt in 1998.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: He then worked as a revue-artist and dramatist, he produced the revue Slängar av sleven, and has participated in shows with the theater group Stockholms blodbad.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: He also worked with the SVT entertainment show Säpop, and he has been part of the TV4 comedy show "Parlamentet".

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: In 2007 he won the Karamelodiktstipendiet by Povel Ramel.

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: In 2014 Dorsin toured with the comedy play "Henrik Dorsin - näktergalen från Holavedsvägen".

title: Henrik Dorsin
text: And since 2014 Dorsin runs the theater Scalateatern in Stockholm.

title: Den Za Nas
text: Den Za Nas (in Macedonian: Ден за нас ) is the title of the fourth Macedonian language album by the Macedonian superstar Toše Proeski released in 2004.

title: Den Za Nas
text: It is a 2-CD set which contains all of the songs performed on the National final in order to select a song for the Eurovision Song Contest 2004 with which Proeski would represent Macedonia in the contest.

title: Den Za Nas
text: The winning song was "Life" which qualified for the final and finished on the 14th place in the final.

title: Den Za Nas
text: Some extra songs such as "Dzvezdo Severnice", "Me Sakaš So Zborovi", "Ima Li Den Za Nas" and others were recorded especially for the album.

title: Football Weekly
text: Football Weekly is a podcast about football, hosted by "The Guardian" newspaper in the United Kingdom.

title: Football Weekly
text: Originally provided weekly (as its name suggests), its popularity led to a mid-weekly spinoff, "Football Weekly Extra".

title: Football Weekly
text: "Football Weekly" airs on Mondays during the European football season, after the weekend's fixtures, while "Football Weekly Extra" airs on Thursdays.

title: Football Weekly
text: During the Euro 2008, World Cup 2010, Euro 2012, World Cup 2014 and Euro 2016 tournaments the podcast aired daily.

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: Orange Field Tea Factory is engaged in the manufacture of Black tea catering to the Middle - Eastern market and the C-I-S Countries (Commonwealth of Independent States).

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: The factory is situated in Panwilatenne, a very small hamlet in Kandy District, Sri Lanka and located within close proximity to Loolecondera Estate where tea was planted for the first time in the Island by James Taylor (Ceylon).

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: Established in the year 1950 the factory produces Black Tea from leaves grown by about 750 small plantation holders in the westen medium elevational category, at an altitude of between 650 meters to 1000 meters above sea level.

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: Orange Field Tea Factory is registered with The Sri Lanka Tea Board and also is a member of the Ethical Tea Partnership.

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: The average annual production for the past few years has been 500,000 kg.

title: Orange Field Tea Factory
text: The produce is sold weekly at the Colombo tea auctions conducted by the Colombo Brokers' Association, monitored by the Colombo Tea Traders Association.

title: Makedonsko Sonce
text: Makedonsko Sonce (Macedonian: ; English: Macedonian Sun ) is a weekly magazine published in the Republic of Macedonia.

title: Makedonsko Sonce
text: The title means "Macedonian Sun", referring to the Vergina Sun, which is used in the logo of the magazine.

title: Makedonsko Sonce
text: It was established by Gjorgija (George) Atanasoski and the first edition was published on June 24, 1994.

title: Makedonsko Sonce
text: It describes its own political stance as affirming "Macedonian national values, not only on territory of Macedonia but also in the other parts of ethnic Macedonia".

title: 2015 Macedonian Football Supercup
text: The 2015 Macedonian Supercup was the 3rd Macedonian Football Supercup, an annual Macedonian football match played between the winners of the previous season's First League and Macedonian Cup.

title: 2015 Macedonian Football Supercup
text: The game will be played between Rabotnički, who beat Teteks to win the 2015 Macedonian Cup Final, and Vardar, champions of the 2014–15 First League.

title: 2015 Macedonian Football Supercup
text: It was played at Philip II Arena, Skopje and was won by Vardar by 4–3 on penalties after the match was ended 1–1 after the regular and extra time.

title: Hänt Extra
text: Hänt Extra is a Swedish language weekly celebrity and youth magazine published by Aller Media in Stockholm, Sweden.

title: Art Laboe
text: Art Laboe (born Arthur Egnoian on August 7, 1925) is an Armenian American disc jockey, songwriter, record producer, and radio station owner, generally credited with coining the term "Oldies But Goodies".

title: Chinese Australians
text: Chinese Australians () are Australian citizens of Chinese ancestry.

title: Chinese Australians
text: Chinese Australians are one of the largest groups of Overseas Chinese people, forming the largest Overseas Chinese community in Oceania.

title: Chinese Australians
text: Per capita, Australia has more people of Chinese ancestry than any country outside of Asia.

title: Chinese Australians
text: Many Chinese Australians are immigrants from Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and other countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, while many are descendants of such immigrants.

title: Chinese Australians
text: Chinese Australians are also a subgroup of Asian Australians and East Asian Australians and represent the single largest minority ethnicity in the country.

title: Chinese Australians
text: As a whole, Australian residents identifying themselves as having Chinese ancestry made up 5.6% of those nominating their ancestry at the 2016 census and numbered 1,213,903.

title: Interamerican Scout Jamboree
text: The Interamerican Scout Jamboree is the biggest event of the Interamerican Scout Region.

title: Interamerican Scout Jamboree
text: It is held every four years in a different country of the region.

title: Interamerican Scout Jamboree
text: The host country is elected during the Interamerican Scout Conference.

title: Interamerican Scout Jamboree
text: Ecuador was announced as the host of the 15th Interamerican Scout Jamboree at the XXV Interamerican Scout Conference in Buenos Aires, Argentina, on 21 September 2013.

title: Scout Promise
text: Since the publication of "Scouting for Boys" in 1908, all Scouts and Girl Guides around the world have taken a Scout (or Guide) promise or oath to live up to ideals of the movement, and subscribed to a Scout Law.

title: Scout Promise
text: The wording of the Scout Promise (or Oath) and Scout Law have varied slightly over time and from country to country.

title: Scout Promise
text: Some national organization promises are given below.

title: Scout Promise
text: Although most Scouting and Guiding organizations use the word "promise", a few such as the Boy Scouts of America tend to use "oath" instead.

title: Scout Promise
text: Typically, Scouts and Guides will make the three-fingered Scout Sign when reciting the promise.

title: Arabs in India
text: A small but recognizable people with Arab origins have over time settled in the India.

title: Arabs in India
text: Genealogically they are grouped as "Indo-Arabs" or "Indians with Arab ancestry".

title: Arabs in India
text: Those who arrived in Kerala and Gujarat for trading goods were later recruited to the army.

title: Arabs in India
text: Most Arabs were traders, and businessmen who sold or traded silk, diamonds and other valuables resulting in wealthy business men.

title: Arabs in India
text: The city of Surat and villages within the city are known for Arab settlements.

title: Arabs in India
text: Variav and Randev are the few villages that Arabs started their lives in.

title: Arabs in India
text: In Hyderabad, Chaush are Arab community of Hadhrami descent whose ancestors were recruited as soldier by Nizam of Hyderabad.

title: Arabs in India
text: In coastal Karnataka, Iraqis arrived during the reign of Tipu Sultan.

title: Arabs in India
text: They claim their ancestry from Banu Assad.

title: Arabs in India
text: These population migrations may have been favored by both the Nizam of Hyderabad and Tipu Sultan of Mysore because both had their ancestral linkages to these populations.The Asaf Jahi Dynasty claimed Arab ancestry from Asir Province and Tipu Sultan from the Bani Hashim of Hijaz Province in Arabia.

title: Arabs in India
text: Many Arabs having Adnani ancestry such as Quraishi, Ansari, Sayyid tribes and other descendants of the Sahaba were employed by the Princely States in their military as they were found efficient during warfare.

title: Arabs in India
text: In Kerala, Syed Thangals of Hadhrami descent settled around 17th century as missionaries to propagate Islam.

title: Arabs in India
text: There are also Shia Sayyids in Northern region of country who claim descent from Wasit, Iraq like Zaidis although many Arab genealogists dispute this fact.

title: Arabs in India
text: Sunni Sayyid of the country also claim Arab descent from Sufi missionaries.

title: Arabs in India
text: Most of the Sufis migrated from Persia.

title: Arabs in India
text: Sunni Sayyids claim their Arab ancestry through Imam Hassan or Imam Hussain in which case their names may be Hassani, Hussaini or Hashmi.

title: Arabs in India
text: Some also claim descent from both and are termed ""Najeeb AlTarfayn"" or "Noble on both sides".

title: Arabs in India
text: Many Sufi Saints such as Abdul-Qadir Gilani and Moinuddin Chishti and their descendants claim themselves as "Najeeb AlTarfayn" although many genealogists dispute this fact.

title: Arabs in India
text: Sunni Sheikhs also claim Arab descent from Sufis or migrants.

title: Arabs in India
text: They don't know their tribe but trace lineage from Umar - Farooqi, Abu Bakr- Siddiqui, Uthman - Usmani and Ali - Alawi or Mir, who established the Rashidun Caliphate.

title: Arabs in India
text: Many who can vaguely trace their lineage to the Quraish tribe call themselves QuraishiMany having the name Ansari claim their lineage to the Ansar tribes of Madina Munawwara and the companions of the Prophet Muhammad such as Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.

title: Arabs in India
text: Many of the present Sheikhs converted from Hindu castes such as Kayasth and Rajput.

title: KOKO-FM
text: KOKO-FM is a classic hits radio station broadcasting from Kerman, California, for the Fresno area with studio and office located in Los Angeles, California.

title: KOKO-FM
text: KOKO 94 is the home for the Art Laboe Connection, and The Art Laboe Sunday Night Special.

title: KOKO-FM
text: Laboe, by the way, is the station's owner.

title: KOKO-FM
text: Its transmitter is in Kerman.

title: Destinations
text: Girl Scout Destinations, formerly Wider Opportunities or Wider Ops, are events for individual Girl Scouts (ages 11 – 18) hosted by GSUSA or individual Girl Scout councils.

title: Destinations
text: Most Destinations are held within the United States, though each year there are trips abroad, such as to allow participants to be part of the US delegation to another country's national jamboree, or a World Association of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts (WAGGGS) World Centre.

title: Destinations
text: They can range from two days to three weeks long.

title: Destinations
text: Most events are geared toward specified grade levels: Girl Scout Cadettes (6th - 8th grade), Girl Scout Seniors (9th and 10th grade), or Girl Scout Ambassadors (11th and 12th grade).

title: Destinations
text: Girls must go through an application process and sometimes an interview process before being chosen for a Destination.

title: Original Sound
text: Original Sound is a Los Angeles, California-based record label.

title: Original Sound
text: It was founded in the early 1950s by KPOP deejay Art Laboe.

title: Original Sound
text: It began as a small label that specialized in compiling and re-releasing "oldies" R&B and rock 'n' roll songs.

title: Scout Tufankjian
text: Scout Tufankjian is an Armenian-American photojournalist and author based in Brooklyn, New York.

title: Scout Tufankjian
text: She is well known for her photos of American President Barack Obama during his campaign leading up to his presidency.

title: Scout Tufankjian
text: She is also known for her photojournalism work on the Armenian diaspora.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: The Indian Scout is a motorcycle built by the Indian Motocycle Company from 1920 to 1949.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: It rivaled the Chief as Indian's most important model.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: The 101 Scout, made from 1928 to 1931, has been called the best motorcycle Indian ever made.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: A second line of Scouts, with lighter frames and reduced engine displacement, was introduced in 1932 alongside the Standard Scout, which replaced the 101 Scout and shared its frame with the Chief and the Four.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: The small-displacement Scout and the Sport Scout, introduced in 1934, were continued until the end of civilian production in 1942.

title: Indian Scout (motorcycle)
text: Military versions of both models were used by US and other Allied forces during World War II.

title: Shepardson Microsystems
text: Shepardson Microsystems, Inc. (SMI) was a small company producing operating systems and programming languages for the Atari 8-bit and Apple II computer families.

title: Shepardson Microsystems
text: SMI is most noted for authoring Atari's BASIC and Disk Operating System (DOS) products.

title: Atari Assembler Editor
text: The Atari Assembler Editor is a cartridge-based development system used to edit, assemble, and debug 6502 programs for the Atari 8-bit family of home computers.

title: Atari Assembler Editor
text: It was programmed by Kathleen O'Brien of Shepardson Microsystems.

title: Atari Assembler Editor
text: It was the first commercially available assembler for the Atari 8-bit computers.

title: Surround (video game)
text: Surround is a video game programmed by Alan Miller and published by Atari, Inc. for the Atari Video Computer System (later known as the Atari 2600).

title: Surround (video game)
text: It was one of the nine Atari VCS launch titles released in September 1977.

title: Surround (video game)
text: "Surround" is an unofficial port of the arcade game "Blockade", released the previous year by Gremlin.

title: Surround (video game)
text: As such, it is the first home console version of the game that would become widely known across many platforms as "Snake".

title: Surround (video game)
text: As with other early Atari games, it was licensed to Sears, which released it under the name "Chase".

title: Atari XEGS
text: The Atari XE Video Game System (Atari XEGS) is a home video game console released by Atari Corporation in 1987.

title: Atari XEGS
text: Based on Atari's 8-bit 65XE computer, the XEGS is compatible with the existing Atari 8-bit computer software library.

title: Atari XEGS
text: Additionally, it is able to operate as either a stand-alone console or full computer with the addition of its specially designed keyboard.

title: Atari XEGS
text: In computer mode, it may utilize the majority of peripherals released for Atari's 8-bit computer line.

title: Atari XEGS
text: Atari packaged the XEGS as a basic set consisting of only the console and joystick, and as a deluxe set consisting of the console, keyboard, joystick and light gun.

title: HP 64000
text: The HP 64000, introduced circa 1980, is a tool for developing hardware and software for products based on commercial microcomputers.

title: HP 64000
text: The earliest commercial 64000 development systems contain from one to six 64100A Development Stations sharing a hard drive and line printer.

title: HP 64000
text: This arrangement allowed up to six designers and engineers to use their workstations together, sharing the HPIB instrumentation bus and a hard drive and a line printer.

title: HP 64000
text: This was an innovative feature of the 64000 development system since other systems of the era used a timesharing system with a single system processor and memory, making for a more expensive and less flexible development system.

title: Star Ship
text: Star Ship is a video game programmed by Bob Whitehead and published by Atari, Inc. for its Video Computer System (later known as the Atari 2600).

title: Star Ship
text: The game was one of the nine launch titles offered when the Atari 2600 launched on September 11,1977.

title: Star Ship
text: Based on the Atari arcade game "Starship 1", it was the first space-related game developed for the Atari VCS.

title: Star Ship
text: The re-branded Sears TeleGames version is titled Outer Space.

title: Vancouver Whitecaps FC U-23
text: Vancouver Whitecaps FC U-23, formerly known as Whitecaps FC Reserves, was a Canadian soccer team based in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

title: Vancouver Whitecaps FC U-23
text: Although founded in 2005 as part of the development system for the Vancouver Whitecaps USL First Division franchise, beginning in 2011 they became part of the development system for Major League Soccer's Vancouver Whitecaps FC.

title: Vancouver Whitecaps FC U-23
text: The team played in the Premier Development League (PDL), the fourth tier of the American Soccer Pyramid, in the Northwest Division of the Western Conference.

title: Manned Orbital Development System
text: The Manned Orbital Development System was created by the US Air Force Space System Division (SSD) in June 1962.

title: Manned Orbital Development System
text: It was to begin working on plans to use Gemini hardware as the first step in a new US Air Force man-in-space program called MODS (Manned Orbital Development System), a type of military space station that used Gemini spacecraft as ferry vehicles.

title: Manned Orbital Development System
text: The term Blue Gemini first showed up in August 1962 as part of a more specific proposal to fly six Gemini missions with Air Force pilots in a preliminary orientation and training phase of MODS.

title: Manned Orbital Development System
text: MODS was effectively superseded when the Manned Orbital Laboratory was announced in December 1963.

title: New York City Employment and Training Coalition
text: The New York City Employment and Training Coalition is an organization of workforce development and training providers based in New York City.

chunk_id: 5ac2a399554299218029dada::New York City Employment and Training Coalition::1
title: New York City Employment and Training Coalition
text: Members include community-based organizations, community colleges, unions and government agencies.

chunk_id: 5ac2a399554299218029dada::New York City Employment and Training Coalition::2
title: New York City Employment and Training Coalition
text: Seeking to serve as the primary connection point for a fragmented workforce development system, it advocates for effective workforce development policies, adequate program funding and effective use of federal stimulus dollars.

chunk_id: 5ac2a399554299218029dada::New York City Employment and Training Coalition::3
title: New York City Employment and Training Coalition
text: NYCETC also works to sustain an environment that supports a high quality workforce development system to meet the changing needs of New Yorkers.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: The Basic Laws of Israel (Hebrew: חוקי היסוד‎ ‎ , "ħuqey ha-yesod") are the constitutional laws of the State of Israel.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: These laws deal with the formation and role of the principal institutions of the state, and with the relations between the state's authorities.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: They also protect civil rights, although some of these rights were earlier protected at common law by the Supreme Court of Israel.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: The Basic Laws are intended to be draft chapters of the future Israeli constitution, postponed since 1950, and act as a "de facto" constitution until their future incorporation into a formal, unitary, written constitution.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: Israel as of 2017 functions according to an uncodified constitution consisting of both material constitutional law, based upon cases and precedents, common law, and the provisions of these formal statutes.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: The Basic Laws do not cover all constitutional issues, and there is no deadline set for the completion of the process of merging them into one comprehensive constitution.

title: Basic Laws of Israel
text: There is no clear rule determining the precedence of Basic Rules over regular legislation, and in many cases this issue is left to interpretation by the judicial system.

title: Constitution of Israel

title: Constitution of Israel
text: Instead of a formal written constitution, and in accordance with the Harari Decision (החלטת הררי) of 13 June 1950 adopted during the Israeli Constituent Assembly, the State of Israel has enacted several Basic Laws of Israel dealing with the government arrangements and with human rights.

title: Constitution of Israel
text: The Israeli Supreme Court President Aharon Barak ruled that the Basic Laws should be considered the state's constitution, and that became the common approach throughout his tenure (1995-2006).

text: It includes interviews and new versions of pre-existing songs not released on any other CD.

title: Hold Me Up
text: Hold Me Up is the third studio album by American rock band Goo Goo Dolls, released by Metal Blade Records in 1990.

title: Hold Me Up
text: This is considered the band's true major-label debut, as previous albums were organized by the band themselves.

title: Hold Me Up

title: Hold Me Up
text: Some consider this album the Goo Goo Dolls' last true "garage rock" album.

title: Hold Me Up
text: Also, this marks the beginning of John Rzeznik's emergence as the band's principal lead vocalist.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: Jane Marum Roush (born September 24, 1956) is a Virginia lawyer and Judge who served as an interim Justice of the Supreme Court of Virginia.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: On July 27, 2015, Governor Terry McAuliffe announced his appointment of Roush to fill the vacancy created by the retirement of Justice LeRoy F. Millette, Jr. effective July 31, 2015.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: Under the Constitution of Virginia, this original interim appointment was to expire thirty days after the commencement of the next session of the Virginia General Assembly, unless the legislature elected her to a full twelve-year term.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: On August 17, 2015, the General Assembly convened in special session but failed to elect anyone to the full twelve-year term before the Senate of Virginia purported to adjourn sine die.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: The Constitution prohibits one chamber of the legislature from adjourning for more than three days without the consent of the other chamber.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: The Governor claims that this provision applies only to regular sessions of the General Assembly; the House of Delegates and most Senate Republicans claim it applies to special sessions as well, and that the Senate's adjournment was invalid because the House did not consent.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: Because there is legal uncertainty about whether the legislature was still in session, it is unclear whether the governor could fill the vacancy created when Justice Roush's original interim appointment expired on September 16, 2015.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: Nevertheless, the governor announced his view that the legislature was not in session and purported to reappoint her for a second interim term.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: Whether this second interim appointment was valid or invalid has not been determined.

title: Jane Marum Roush
text: If valid, the second interim appointment expired on February 12, 2016, thirty days after the regular session of the General Assembly began on January 13, because the legislature did not elect her to a full twelve-year term.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: This is a list of municipal elections held in the city of Calgary, Alberta, Canada.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: Elections for mayor were held annually until the 1923 election, when the election was for a two-year term.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: From the 1971 election, the mayoral term was three years.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: Elections for councillors and aldermen were held annually until the 1914 election, when the terms switched to two-year overlapping terms, with half of each council up for election each year.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: From the 1971 election, the aldermanic elections lined up fully with the mayoral elections, and were also for three-year terms.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: In 1976, the number of wards expanded to 14 (current number) with one alderman representing each ward for three years.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: On December 14, 2010, council voted to change the title to "councillor", which took effect in the October 2013 election.

title: List of Calgary municipal elections
text: In 2012 the Local Authorities Election Act was amended to increase the term length of the mayor and councillors to 4 years.

title: Joseph Vitale (politician)

title: Kwame Kilpatrick

title: Luke Hubbins

title: Bitið fast í vitið

title: Bitið fast í vitið
text: It was released in late-1982 on the Spor label, within a year of the band's formation in September 1981 – led by vocalists Björk and Eyþór Arnalds .

title: Bitið fast í vitið
text: This was the band's most punk-oriented release and contains five tracks, featuring one in English, "London".

title: Steeltown (band)
text: Steeltown were an Australian band based in the city of Brisbane who performed in the 90s a genre of synth, rock, pop and produced their greatest top forty chart hit with the song 'Hero' which was released in September 1991.

title: Steeltown (band)
text: They notably sold more recordings than any other band of the time based in the state of Queensland.

title: Steeltown (band)
text: (the video and a live performance can be seen on YouTube).

title: Steeltown (band)
text: The group members were Andy Richmond vocals, Peter Howard keyboards, Terry Gidman drums and Kate Richmond vocals and percussion and Reece Speceis Lead Guitar.

title: Steeltown (band)

title: Tappi Tíkarrass
text: Tappi Tíkarrass was an Icelandic punk band which added elements of funk, rock and jazz to their music, marking a difference from other traditional bands at that time.

title: Tappi Tíkarrass
text: The band is also considered the first serious music project of now renowned singer Björk Guðmundsdóttir.

title: INXS
text: INXS ( ) were an Australian rock band, formed as The Farriss Brothers in 1977 in Sydney, New South Wales.

title: INXS
text: They began playing covers in Western Australian pubs and clubs, occasionally playing some of their original music.

title: INXS
text: Mainstays were main composer and keyboardist Andrew Farriss, drummer Jon Farriss, guitarists Tim Farriss and Kirk Pengilly, bassist Garry Gary Beers and main lyricist and vocalist Michael Hutchence.

title: INXS
text: For twenty years, INXS was fronted by Hutchence, whose "sultry good looks" and magnetic stage presence made him the focal point of the band.

title: INXS
text: Initially known for their new wave/pop style, the band later developed a harder pub rock style that included funk and dance elements.

title: Nýtt líf
text: Nýtt Líf ( , English: "New Life") is an Icelandic film directed by Þráinn Bertelsson and released in 1983.

title: Nýtt líf
text: The film is a comedy shot in the Westman Islands and stars Eggert Þorleifsson and Karl Ágúst Úlfsson, among others.

title: Nýtt líf
text: The music features several musicians including the band Tappi Tíkarrass (of which Björk was a member), which contributed the songs "Sperglar" and "Kukl" (a.k.a. "Seiður").

title: Disco polo
text: Disco polo is a musical genre of popular music that is dance music, created in Poland in the late 1980s, initially known as "sidewalks music" ("muzyka chodnikowa").

title: Disco polo
text: This trend, also known as city folklore music, was popular in the mid-late 1990s, with its peak taking place around 1995–1997.

title: Disco polo
text: Later observed a gradual decline in the popularity led to the temporary collapse in the early twenty-first century.

title: Disco polo
text: Disco polo have enjoyed a renaissance of popularity in late 2007.

title: Disco polo
text: Language Dictionary Polish Publishing PWN defines the genre as a Polish variant of disco music, with simple melodies.

title: Disco polo
text: It is derived from disco, Euro disco contemporary folk music influenced by Italo disco and Polish folk songs (specifically, the vulgarized subgenre of which is mostly played at weddings and feasts).

title: Kidandali
text: Kidandali is a stylistic music genre and one of only 2 music genres native to Uganda, the other being Kadongo Kamu.

title: Kidandali
text: Kidandali is a word from the Ganda language which in translation can mean "local party" or "celebration".

title: Kidandali
text: Music concerts and traditional wedding ceremonies (kwanjula) are examples of such "bidandali".

title: Kidandali
text: The music itself is given this name because most times it is the kind of music played or performed at such local parties and functions.

title: Kidandali
text: Some other sources and commentators refer to the genre alternatively as "Band music" while others refer to it as "Afrobeat".

title: Rave music
text: Rave music may either refer to the late 1980s/early 1990s genres of house, breakbeat, acid house, techno and hardcore techno, which were the first genres of music to be played at rave parties, or to any other genre of electronic dance music (EDM) that may be played at a rave.

title: Rave music
text: The genre "rave", also known as hardcore by early ravers, first appeared amongst the UK "acid" movement during the late 1980s at warehouse parties and other underground venues, as well as on UK pirate radio stations.

title: Rave music
text: The genre would develop into oldschool hardcore, which lead onto newer forms of rave music such as drum and bass and 2-step, as well as other hardcore techno genres, such as gabber, hardstyle and happy hardcore.

title: Rave music
text: Rave music is usually presented in a DJ mix set, although live performances are not uncommon.

title: Folk rock
text: Folk rock is a music genre combining elements of folk music and rock music.

title: Folk rock
text: In its earliest and narrowest sense, the term referred to a genre that arose in the United States and the United Kingdom around the mid-1960s.

title: Folk rock
text: The genre emerged from bands such as the Beatles, the Searchers, and the Animals in the UK, and Bob Dylan and the Byrds in the US, who played traditional folk music and songs with rock instrumentation.

title: Folk rock
text: The term "folk rock" is first noted as being used by the U.S. music press in June 1965 to describe the Byrds' music; the band's debut album was released the same month.

title: Miranda (album)

title: Miranda (album)

title: Fez (video game)

title: Fez (video game)
text: The player-character Gomez receives a fez that reveals his two-dimensional (2D) world to be one of four sides of a three-dimensional (3D) world.

title: Fez (video game)
text: The player rotates between these four 2D views to realign platforms and solve the game's puzzles.

title: Fez (video game)
text: The object of the game is to collect cubes and cube fragments to restore order to the universe.

title: Gateways (video game)

title: Team Fortress 2
text: Team Fortress 2 (TF2) is a team-based multiplayer first-person shooter video game developed and published by Valve Corporation.

title: Team Fortress 2
text: It is the sequel to the 1996 mod "Team Fortress" for "Quake" and its 1999 remake, "Team Fortress Classic".

title: Team Fortress 2
text: It was released as part of the video game bundle "The Orange Box" in October 2007 for Microsoft Windows and the Xbox 360.

title: Team Fortress 2
text: A PlayStation 3 version followed in December 2007.

title: Team Fortress 2
text: The game was released for Windows as a standalone entry in April 2008, and was updated to support OS X in June 2010 and Linux in February 2013.

title: Team Fortress 2

title: Portal (video game)
text: The game has since been ported to other systems, including OS X, Linux, and Android.

title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast
text: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast is an additional level for the 2004 first-person shooter video game "Half-Life 2".

title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast
text: Developed by Valve Corporation, it was released on October 27, 2005, through the Steam content delivery service as a free download to owners of the Microsoft Windows version of "Half-Life 2".

title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast
text: "Lost Coast" serves as a technology demonstration, specifically showcasing the high-dynamic-range rendering implemented in the Source engine.

title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast
text: The level was designed with a variety of appropriate environments to emphasize these effects.

title: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast
text: In addition, "Lost Coast" was the first video game developed by Valve to allow developers to explain various elements of design as the player progresses through the level.

title: The Lost Vikings
text: The Lost Vikings is a puzzle-platform video game developed by Silicon & Synapse (now Blizzard Entertainment) and published by Interplay.

title: The Lost Vikings
text: It was originally released for the Super NES in 1992, then subsequently released for the Amiga, Amiga CD32, MS-DOS, and Mega Drive/Genesis systems the next year; the Mega Drive/Genesis version contains five stages not present in any other version of the game.

title: The Lost Vikings
text: Blizzard re-released the game for the Game Boy Advance in 2003.

title: The Lost Vikings
text: In 2014, the game was added to Battle.net as a free download emulated through DOSBox.

title: Portal 2
text: Portal 2 is a 2011 first-person puzzle-platform video game developed and published by Valve Corporation.

title: Portal 2
text: It is the sequel to "Portal" (2007) and was released on April 19, 2011, for Microsoft Windows, OS X, Linux, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360.

title: Portal 2
text: The retail versions of the game are distributed by Electronic Arts while online distribution of the Microsoft Windows, Mac OS X and Linux versions is handled by Valve's content delivery service Steam.

title: Portal 2
text: "Portal 2" was announced on March 5, 2010, following a week-long alternate reality game based on new patches to the original game.

title: Portal 2
text: Before the game's release on Steam, the company released the Potato Sack, a second multi-week alternate reality game, involving 13 independently developed titles which culminated in a distributed computing spoof to release "Portal 2" several hours early.

title: Portal (series)
text: Portal is a series of first-person puzzle-platform video games developed by Valve Corporation.

title: Portal (series)
text: Set in the "Half-Life" universe, the two main games in the series, "Portal" (2007) and "Portal 2" (2011), center on a woman, Chell, forced to undergo a series of tests within the Aperture Science Enrichment Center by a malicious artificial intelligence computer, GLaDOS, that controls the facility.

title: Portal (series)
text: Each test involves using the "Aperture Science Handheld Portal Device" - the "portal gun" - that creates a human-sized wormhole-like connection between nearly any two flat surfaces.

title: Portal (series)
text: The player-character or objects in the game world may move through portals, their momentum conserved.

title: Portal (series)
text: This allows complex "flinging" maneuvers to be used to cross wide gaps or perform other feats to reach the exit for each test chamber.

title: Portal (series)
text: A number of other mechanics, such as lasers, light bridges, tractor funnels, and turrets, exist to aid or hinder the player's goal to reach the exit.

title: Sodium-chloride symporter
text: The sodium-chloride symporter (also known as Na-Cl cotransporter, abbreviated as NCC or NCCT, or as the thiazide-sensitive Na-Cl cotransporter or TSC for short) is a cotransporter in the kidney which has the function of reabsorbing sodium and chloride ions from the tubular fluid into the cells of the distal convoluted tubule of the nephron.

title: Sodium-chloride symporter
text: It is a member of the SLC12 cotransporter family of electroneutral cation-coupled chloride cotransporters.

title: Sodium-chloride symporter
text: In humans, it is encoded by the gene "SLC12A3" (solute carrier family 12 member 3) located in 16q13.

title: Loop of Henle
text: In the kidney, the loop of Henle ( ) (or Henle's loop, Henle loop, nephron loop or its Latin counterpart ansa nephroni) is the portion of a nephron that leads from the proximal convoluted tubule to the distal convoluted tubule.

title: Loop of Henle
text: Named after its discoverer, the German anatomist Friedrich Gustav Jakob Henle, the loop of Henle's main function is to create a concentration gradient in the medulla of the kidney.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: Low pressure receptors are baroreceptors located in the venae cavae and the pulmonary arteries, and in the atria.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: They are also called volume receptors.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: These receptors respond to changes in the wall tension, which is proportional to the filling state of the low pressure side of circulation (below 60mmHg).

title: Low pressure receptors
text: Their impulses regulate the secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH/Vasopressin), renin and aldosterone.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: An elevated atrial pressure produces a decrease in ADH and aldosterone secretion.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: The decrease in vasopressin secretion results in an increase in the volume of urine excreted, serving to lower blood pressure.

title: Low pressure receptors
text: In addition, stretching of atrial receptors increases secretion of atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), which promotes increased water and sodium excretion through the urine.

title: Renal tubular acidosis
text: Renal tubular acidosis (RTA) is a medical condition that involves an accumulation of acid in the body due to a failure of the kidneys to appropriately acidify the urine.

title: Renal tubular acidosis
text: In renal physiology, when blood is filtered by the kidney, the filtrate passes through the tubules of the nephron, allowing for exchange of salts, acid equivalents, and other solutes before it drains into the bladder as urine.

title: Renal tubular acidosis
text: The metabolic acidosis that results from RTA may be caused either by failure to reabsorb sufficient bicarbonate ions (which are alkaline) from the filtrate in the early portion of the nephron (the proximal tubule) or by insufficient secretion of hydrogen ions (which are acidic) into the latter portions of the nephron (the distal tubule).

title: Renal tubular acidosis
text: Although a metabolic acidosis also occurs in those with renal insufficiency, the term RTA is reserved for individuals with poor urinary acidification in otherwise well-functioning kidneys.

title: Renal tubular acidosis
text: Several different types of RTA exist, which all have different syndromes and different causes.

title: Ascending limb of loop of Henle
text: Within the nephron of the kidney, the ascending limb of the loop of Henle is a segment of the loop of Henle downstream of the descending limb, after the sharp bend of the loop.

title: Ascending limb of loop of Henle
text: This part of the renal tubule is divided into a thin and thick ascending limb; the thick portion is also known as the distal straight tubule, in contrast with the distal convoluted tubule downstream.

title: Angiotensin
text: Angiotensin is a peptide hormone that causes vasoconstriction and a subsequent increase in blood pressure.

title: Angiotensin
text: It is part of the renin-angiotensin system, which is a major target for drugs that raises blood pressure.

title: Angiotensin
text: Angiotensin also stimulates the release of aldosterone, another hormone, from the adrenal cortex.

title: Angiotensin
text: Aldosterone promotes sodium retention in the distal nephron, in the kidney, which also drives blood pressure up.

title: Tubuloglomerular feedback
text: In the physiology of the kidney, tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF) is a feedback system inside the kidneys. Within each nephron, information from the renal tubules (a downstream area of the tubular fluid) is signaled to the glomerulus (an upstream area).

title: Tubuloglomerular feedback
text: Tubuloglomerular feedback is one of several mechanisms the kidney uses to regulate glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

title: Tubuloglomerular feedback
text: It involves the concept of purinergic signaling, in which an increased distal tubular sodium chloride concentration causes a basolateral release of adenosine from the macula densa cells.

title: Tubuloglomerular feedback
text: This initiates a cascade of events that ultimately brings GFR to an appropriate level.

title: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait
text: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait (8 January 1917 – 28 February 2003) ("née" Wardropper, known as Sylvia Simpson from 1941 to 1956) was an English biochemist and endocrinologist.

title: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait
text: She worked with her second husband, James Francis Tait, from 1948 until her death in 2003, a partnership described by the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography as "one of the most successful examples of husband-wife scientific collaboration".

title: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait
text: Together, they discovered and identified the hormone aldosterone, the last of a series of naturally occurring biologically potent steroid hormones to be isolated and identified between the 1920s to the 1950s, after the androgens, oestrogens, and glucocorticoid hormones.

title: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait
text: Aldosterone is part of the mechanism that regulates blood pressure, and causes conservation of sodium, secretion of potassium, increased water retention, and increased blood pressure.

title: Sylvia Agnes Sophia Tait
text: It is thought to be responsible for 15 per cent of cases of high blood pressure.

title: Distal renal tubular acidosis
text: Distal renal tubular acidosis (dRTA) or Type 1 renal tubular acidosis (RTA) is the classical form of RTA, being the first described.

title: Distal renal tubular acidosis
text: Distal RTA is characterized by a failure of acid secretion by the alpha intercalated cells of the cortical collecting duct of the distal nephron.

title: Distal renal tubular acidosis
text: This failure of acid secretion may be due to a number of causes, and it leads to an inability to acidify the urine to a pH of less than 5.3.

title: Aldosterone
text: Aldosterone, the main mineralocorticoid hormone, is a steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.

title: Aldosterone
text: It is essential for sodium conservation in the kidney, salivary glands, sweat glands and colon.

title: Aldosterone
text: It plays a central role in the regulation of the plasma sodium (Na), the extracellular potassium (K) and arterial blood pressure.

title: Aldosterone
text: It does so mainly by acting on the mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the nephron.

title: Aldosterone
text: It influences the reabsorption of sodium and excretion of potassium (from and into the tubular fluids, respectively) of the kidney, thereby indirectly influencing water retention or loss, blood pressure and blood volume.

title: Aldosterone
text: When dysregulated, aldosterone is pathogenic and contributes to the development and progression of cardiovascular and renal disease.

title: Aldosterone
text: Aldosterone has exactly the opposite function of the atrial natriuretic hormone secreted by the heart.

title: United States elections, 2018
text: The 2018 United States elections will mostly be held on Tuesday, November 6, 2018.

title: United States elections, 2018
text: These midterm elections will take place in the middle of Republican President Donald Trump's term.

title: United States elections, 2018
